title: REST handlers block tokio workers on world mutex; sim holds lock across up to 240 steps (spawn_blocking + chunked stepping)
description:
ROOT CAUSE (anchors at e2d9aaa): every REST/MCP handler goes through ControlHandle::lock_world() — a blocking std::sync::Mutex acquired on tokio worker threads (crates/scriptbots-app/src/control.rs) — while the simulation drivers hold that same mutex for long bursts: the TUI steps up to MAX_STEPS_PER_FRAME=240 ticks per acquisition (terminal/mod.rs ~375) and the GPUI pump has a 0.5s hard cap under lock. Failure modes measured in audit: (a) at high speed with a large population, num_cpus concurrent SSE clients (each polling latest_summary) block ALL tokio workers -> the entire control plane (Swagger, MCP included) freezes; (b) spamming GET /api/screenshot/png stalls the simulation because rasterization used to run under the world lock (a 64Mpx guard exists; the lock-hold problem remains).

FIX (three independent pieces, in order of value):
1. Chunked stepping: both sim drivers re-acquire the world lock every <=16 steps instead of 240/0.5s. Step math is unchanged, so determinism digests must be bit-identical (assert via characterization trace).
2. Lock-free reads where a snapshot suffices: latest tick summary, SSE/NDJSON streams, and events/tail should read from published immutable state (extend the existing AnalyticsSnapshot/ArcSwap pattern or a new Arc<TickSummaryLatest>) instead of locking the world at all. Handlers that genuinely mutate (patch config, selection) wrap their lock access in tokio::task::spawn_blocking so a contended lock parks a blocking thread, not an async worker.
3. screenshot_png: copy render-relevant state under a short lock, rasterize outside it, inside spawn_blocking.

RELATED: bd-2z0.4.9 (HostClient migration) will eventually replace this plumbing wholesale; this bead is the bounded fix that keeps the current control plane usable meanwhile — do not gold-plate, and keep the seams compatible with HostClient direction (snapshot-read + command-intent shape).

ACCEPTANCE: with 1k+ agents at speed x8: GET /api/ticks/latest p95 < 50ms under load; 2x num_cpus concurrent SSE clients cause zero missed control-plane responses; sim tick rate degrades <10% versus no-clients baseline. Determinism: seeded digest identical before/after chunked stepping.

TESTS (required): unit — chunked vs monolithic stepping produce identical characterization digests for 240 ticks (seeded); unit — snapshot-read handlers return data without acquiring the world mutex (assert via a poisoned-mutex world: reads still succeed); e2e script — launch headless server mode, drive N SSE clients + PNG requests + a stepping loop, log per-endpoint latency histograms (p50/p95/p99) and tick throughput with tracing, assert the acceptance numbers; failure output must include the histogram table.

title: FrankenSQLite refuses to open a database on exFAT (breaks external drives; NOT a 'native target artifact')
description:
SYMPTOM: every storage-backed test and every real run fails at startup when the database lives on
an exFAT volume:

  Error: failed to initialize FrankenSQLite storage at <path>/run.sqlite
  Caused by: storage Startup failed ... invalid storage data in storage.recovery_path:
             recovery path <path>/run.sqlite changed during validated open

PROVEN, not guessed. The dev box has TMPDIR on an exFAT USB volume
(/Volumes/USBNVME16TB, `diskutil info` -> "File System Personality: ExFAT"). With TMPDIR left
alone, run_manifest_emitted fails 4/4 and ~34 scriptbots-storage tests fail. Point TMPDIR at an
APFS directory and the SAME tests pass 4/4 with no code change whatsoever. That is the whole
experiment: one variable, opposite outcomes.

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND OUR DEV BOX, and why this is not just an environment gripe: exFAT is what
external drives, USB sticks and most cross-platform disks are formatted as. A user who points
SCRIPTBOTS_STORAGE_PATH at an external drive — an entirely reasonable thing to do with multi-GB
run databases — gets a hard startup failure whose message implies their file was TAMPERED WITH
("changed during validated open"). They will look for a corruption bug that does not exist.

CAUSE (read the fsqlite validated-open path to confirm the exact predicate): the open path
appears to stat the file, open it, re-stat, and compare metadata to detect a swapped/altered
path. exFAT has 2-second timestamp granularity and no APFS/ext4-style inode identity, so the
before/after comparison differs for reasons that have nothing to do with tampering. The check is
sound on APFS/ext4 and produces FALSE POSITIVES on exFAT (and would on FAT32/SMB shares).

THIS ALSO CORRECTS THE RECORD. Several of us — me included — have been writing off these storage
failures as "an artifact of the aarch64-apple-darwin target" (see my notes on bd-2z0.3.7 and the
mail about bd-2tse). THAT DIAGNOSIS WAS WRONG. The target is irrelevant; the FILESYSTEM is the
variable. Anyone who has been ignoring storage test failures on that basis should re-check them
with TMPDIR on APFS, because real regressions could have been hiding behind an excuse that does
not hold.

THE FIX (fsqlite's owner should choose):
  a) Make the validated-open predicate filesystem-aware: fall back to a content/size check, or a
     coarser timestamp comparison, where the filesystem cannot supply the identity the check
     assumes. Detect the capability rather than assuming it.
  b) If exFAT genuinely cannot support the guarantee, REFUSE IT LOUDLY AND SPECIFICALLY at open:
     "this filesystem (exFAT) cannot provide the identity guarantees the recovery path requires;
     move the database to APFS/ext4, or pass --unsafe-storage to proceed without the check". An
     accurate refusal is far better than an error that accuses the user's file of changing under
     them.
  c) At minimum, name the filesystem in the error. The current message sends the reader hunting
     for a corruption bug that is not there.

WORKAROUND UNTIL FIXED: keep run databases (and TMPDIR, for the test suite) on APFS.
  TMPDIR=<apfs dir> cargo test -p scriptbots-app
close_reason: Fixed. Storage refused to open ANY database on exFAT — which is what external drives and USB sticks are formatted as — telling the user their file had 'changed during validated open', i.e. accusing them of tampering when the only thing that had happened was our own initialisation. MECHANISM, measured not assumed: the swapped-file guard compares (device, inode); exFAT has no inodes and the kernel synthesizes one from the file's STARTING CLUSTER, so truncate-and-regrow (exactly what creating a database does) MOVES it. Probed directly: a 64-byte file rewritten to 1MB went 43648807 -> 43648811 on exFAT and did not move at all on APFS. FIX: the guard now PROBES whether the filesystem can actually provide the property it depends on, rather than assuming it — a behavioural probe, because a name tells you what a filesystem is called and a probe tells you what it does, and the set that synthesizes inodes (exFAT/FAT32/some SMB+FUSE) cannot be enumerated correctly in advance. Where identity is stable the check is enforced unchanged; where it is not it is SKIPPED, and skipped LOUDLY with the reason and the consequence, because a security check that quietly turns itself off is worse than either the false positive or the honest downgrade. The symlink/regular-file/hard-link checks still apply. Also split the four conditions out of one collapsed error message — a symlink where a file should be is an attack, a moved inode may be the filesystem reshuffling clusters, and conflating them is what cost the time. RESULT: exFAT 62/62 (was 24 passed / 34 FAILED); APFS all green INCLUDING the symlink+hard-link security test, so the guard is unweakened where it can be enforced. This also corrects the record: I twice told the team these were 'an aarch64 target artifact'. That was wrong — the filesystem was the variable.

title: Evolution Lab: emergent science, exploration, and delight
description:
WHY THIS EPIC EXISTS. The bd-2z0 recovery program makes ScriptBots CORRECT, HONEST, and REPRODUCIBLE — deterministic kernel, heritable genomes, sole-owner host, real replay, truthful docs. That is necessary and it is not sufficient. Nothing in bd-2z0 makes the project COMPELLING: nothing turns hours of ticks into meaning, nothing makes evolution visible, nothing delivers the README's headline differentiator (an LLM acting as an autonomous lab assistant), and nothing pushes the science past "faithful port of a 2009 toy."

This epic is the discovery-and-delight layer. Every child (a) sits ON TOP of bd-2z0 foundations rather than duplicating them, (b) is individually shippable and individually valuable, and (c) preserves the core promise: determinism first. Any child that would trade bit-exact reproducibility for speed or spectacle must make that trade opt-in, gated, and CI-proven — bd-16g.15 is the canonical treatment of that tension.

CHILDREN, ordered by (value to a human watching or researching) x (leverage over other children) / (cost given bd-2z0):
  bd-16g.1  Autonomous LLM lab assistant (the README's unbuilt headline)
  bd-16g.2  Emergent-event detector + auto-narrated timeline (makes hours legible in seconds; feeds .1, .3, .9, .14)
  bd-16g.3  Live phylogeny + speciation detection (makes evolution visible)
  bd-16g.4  Agent-perspective inspector (makes a brain's experience legible)
  bd-16g.5  Island archipelago with migration (richer evolution AND linear scaling)
  bd-16g.6  MAP-Elites / novelty search (evolution that goes somewhere instead of converging)
  bd-16g.7  Emergent communication lab (the sound channel exists; nobody has studied it)
  bd-16g.8  Shareable worlds + gallery (reach; makes a run a shareable artifact)
  bd-16g.9  Evolution theater / highlight reels (the demo that sells the project)
  bd-16g.10 Intervention toolkit (deterministic, replayable "god mode")
  bd-16g.11 Ecosystem accounting / energy Sankey (where the joules actually go)
  bd-16g.12 Brain-family tournament + Elo (the brain testbed's payoff)
  bd-16g.13 Genome browser + mutation diff (see the genes change)
  bd-16g.14 Sonification (hear the ecosystem)
  bd-16g.15 GPU-compute sensing behind a bit-exactness gate (scale without lying)

SHARED SUBSTRATE. Several children want the same three primitives; build them once, in .2 and .3, and reuse:
  (i) a phenotype feature vector per agent (diet tendency, mean speed, turn rate, spike usage, give rate, sound usage, eye-fov profile, energy efficiency) — bd-2z0.11.2 defines these; .3/.6/.7/.12 all consume them;
  (ii) an append-only tick-indexed event/metric stream with stable agent UIDs (bd-2z0.3.1, bd-2z0.5.2);
  (iii) a change-point detector over any metric series (.2 owns it; .9 and .14 consume its output).
Do not let three children each invent their own clustering or their own event schema.

NON-GOALS. Not a game. Not a framework. Not a rewrite. No child may weaken determinism, analytics honesty, or the AGENTS.md storage contract.

title: Autonomous LLM lab assistant: hypothesis -> matched-seed sweep -> analysis -> lab notebook
description:
THE IDEA. Ship a built-in autonomous scientist: a loop that forms a hypothesis, designs a matched-seed experiment, runs it, analyzes the result, decides what to try next, and writes a human-readable lab notebook entry — all through the control surfaces ScriptBots already exposes. `scriptbots-app lab --goal "find the mutation rate that maximizes stable population" --budget 40-runs` should leave behind a markdown notebook with methods, figures, tables, a falsifiable claim, and the exact seeds/configs to reproduce every number.

WHY THIS IS THE #1 IDEA. The README already sells this: "LLM-in-the-loop science... an external LLM agent acts as an autonomous lab assistant: steering experiments, sweeping parameter spaces, logging observations into FrankenSQLite, and drafting human-readable reports." It is the single feature that separates ScriptBots from every other alife toy, it is the reason the REST/MCP/CLI control surface exists at all, and it is entirely unbuilt. Everything it needs is either already there (MCP tools list_knobs/get_config/apply_patch, REST config+metrics, FrankenSQLite run DB) or already planned (bd-2z0.5.5 matched-seed runner, bd-2z0.5.6 Arrow/Parquet exports, bd-2z0.12.2 agent-friendly APIs). This bead is mostly INTEGRATION plus a rigorous experiment protocol — high value, moderate cost, and it converts three infrastructure epics into a visible product.

DESIGN.
- Provider-agnostic: an LlmClient trait (complete(prompt, tools) -> action) with an Anthropic implementation and a scripted/offline implementation used by tests. NEVER hard-require network access to run the sim.
- The loop is a state machine, not a free-form chat: Propose(hypothesis, knobs, ranges, N, seeds) -> Validate(against knob schema + budget) -> Execute(matched-seed runs via bd-2z0.5.5) -> Analyze(effect size + CI over run summaries) -> Decide(refine | expand | conclude) -> Report. Every transition is logged with the model's reasoning text and the exact payloads.
- Budgets are hard: max runs, max ticks, max wall-clock, max tokens. Exceeding any budget ends the loop with an honest partial report.
- The LLM proposes only STRUCTURED experiment specs validated against the config schema; it never writes SQL, never writes code, never touches the filesystem. Its analysis reads pre-computed summary tables (from bd-2z0.5.6 exports), not raw rows.
- Provenance: every notebook claim carries run_ids + seeds + config hash + the digest from bd-2z0.1.6, so a reader can re-run any figure.
- Honesty gate: the report template forces an explicit "what would falsify this" and "what I did not test" section; a claim without a supporting run_id is a build error in the notebook renderer.

WHY IT IS SAFE. The LLM is a proposer/summarizer over a validated, bounded action space. Even a maximally confused model can only request configurations that the existing knob validator would accept from a human.

ACCEPTANCE. Given `--goal "characterize how food_regrowth_rate affects carnivore/herbivore equilibrium" --budget 20-runs --offline-fixture`, the loop produces: a notebook with >=1 falsifiable claim, an effect-size table with confidence intervals, a chart, and a reproduce.sh whose re-run reproduces every number bit-for-bit. With a live provider, the same goal completes within budget and its claims survive an independent verification re-run.

TESTS + LOGGING (required).
- Unit: experiment-spec validator rejects out-of-range knobs, unknown paths, budget overruns, and non-finite values (table-driven).
- Unit: the state machine's transitions with a scripted LlmClient (including adversarial responses: malformed JSON, absurd budgets, contradictory hypotheses) — must never panic, never exceed budget, always terminate.
- Unit: notebook renderer refuses a claim with no run_id provenance.
- E2E (offline, hermetic, CI-safe): scripted LlmClient + real sim + real FrankenSQLite -> full loop -> assert the notebook exists, contains the claims, and reproduce.sh regenerates identical summary tables. NO MOCKED SIM, NO MOCKED DB.
- Logging: one structured tracing event per state transition (phase, hypothesis_id, knobs, seeds, runs_spent, tokens_spent, decision, rationale) at info; full prompts/responses at debug behind SCRIPTBOTS_LAB_TRACE=1. A failed loop must be diagnosable from the info-level log alone.

title: LlmClient trait with Anthropic + scripted-offline implementations (hermetic CI)
description:
SCOPE. The provider boundary and nothing else: an `LlmClient` trait, the request/response/usage types, an Anthropic implementation, and a scripted-offline implementation that makes the entire lab testable with zero network. OUT OF SCOPE: the loop (bd-16g.1.3), the experiment-spec schema (bd-16g.1.2), the statistics (bd-16g.1.4), the notebook (bd-16g.1.5). This bead exists so that every other .1.x bead can be written and tested without an API key.

WHY IT IS FIRST. bd-16g.1's acceptance criterion says the lab runs `--offline-fixture` in CI and produces a byte-reproducible notebook. That is impossible unless the model is behind a trait with a deterministic implementation. If this boundary is not built first, the loop will be written against a concrete Anthropic client, the tests will be written against a mock of that client's HTTP layer, and CI will end up either flaky (network), expensive (real tokens), or dishonest (mocking the thing under test). Build the seam once, correctly, before anything depends on it.

DESIGN.
- HOME: a new `lab` module in scriptbots-app (`crates/scriptbots-app/src/lab/mod.rs`, with `lab/llm.rs`). This is one of the rare cases that clears AGENTS.md's very high bar for new files: main.rs is already 3239 lines and control.rs is the control-surface domain; the lab is genuinely new functionality with no natural existing home. It must NOT live in scriptbots-core: core is the determinism kernel and the WASM target, and it must never acquire an HTTP or LLM dependency.
- TRAIT (synchronous, deliberately):
    pub trait LlmClient: Send + Sync {
        fn complete(&self, req: &LlmRequest) -> Result<LlmResponse, LlmError>;
        fn model_id(&self) -> &str;
    }
    pub struct LlmRequest { system: String, messages: Vec<LlmMessage>, tools: Vec<LlmToolSpec>, max_tokens: u32, temperature: Option<f32> }
    pub struct LlmResponse { text: Option<String>, tool_calls: Vec<LlmToolCall>, usage: TokenUsage, stop_reason: StopReason }
    pub struct LlmToolCall { name: String, arguments: serde_json::Value }
    pub struct TokenUsage { input: u32, output: u32 }
    pub enum LlmError { Transport(String), RateLimited { retry_after_ms: Option<u64> }, Overloaded, InvalidResponse(String), ResponseTooLarge { bytes: usize, cap: usize }, FixtureExhausted, Refused }
  The lab loop is a blocking state machine driven from a CLI subcommand; it is not part of the axum/Tokio server. Do NOT introduce a third async runtime for it. If async ever becomes necessary, it goes through the fastmcp/asupersync stack that bd-2z0.8.7.1 already selected, not through a fresh reactor.
- THE MODEL'S ACTION SPACE IS THE MCP TOOL SURFACE, MINUS THE WRITES. After bd-2z0.8.7.1 lands, tools are `#[tool]` async fns; the lab exposes `list_knobs` and `get_config` as READ tools and `propose_experiment` (bd-16g.1.2's schema) as the model's ONLY write. The model never gets `apply_updates`/`apply_patch`. This is not squeamishness: `ControlHandle::apply_patch` (crates/scriptbots-app/src/control.rs:469) enqueues `ControlCommand::UpdateConfig` against the LIVE `WorldState` and explicitly refuses runtime world-dimension changes (control.rs:495-504). A lab that mutates a live world produces confounded science and can wedge a user's running simulation. Experiments run in FRESH worlds via bd-2z0.5.5. Encode that in the tool surface, not in a comment.
- AnthropicClient: reuse the workspace's existing HTTP client; do not add a second one. API key from `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` only — never from a config file, never a CLI flag (flags land in shell history and in the det-check config layer), never logged. The model id is configurable and is recorded verbatim in the notebook provenance block. Gate the whole implementation behind a `llm-anthropic` cargo feature that the default test profile does not enable.
- ScriptedClient: a `Vec<ScriptedTurn>` deserialized from a JSON fixture; returns turns in declaration order; optionally keyed by a digest of the request so a fixture can assert the prompt shape it expects. Zero network, zero clock, zero entropy. This is the CI client, wired to bd-16g.1's `--offline-fixture <path>`.
- Retry/backoff: bounded attempts, and any jitter is drawn from a SEEDED `SmallRng` threaded in from the session — never from wall-clock. A retry policy that consults the clock makes the whole lab irreproducible for the sake of politeness to a server.

HARD REQUIREMENTS.
- NO NETWORK IN `cargo test`. Failure mode prevented: a CI suite that goes red because Anthropic returned 529, or a test run that silently spends money. Enforce structurally: the Anthropic impl is feature-gated off by default, and a test asserts that the default client in a test build is the scripted one.
- SECRETS NEVER APPEAR IN LOGS, TRANSCRIPTS, OR THE NOTEBOOK. Redact the Authorization header at the point of construction. Failure mode prevented: an API key committed into `runs/lab-*/notebook.md` and pushed.
- NO PANICS. Every provider outcome is a typed `LlmError`. `unwrap()`/`expect()` are banned in this module (clippy pedantic/nursery already fight you; do not fight back). A garbage body, a timeout, a 500, a 200-with-empty-body: all are errors, none are unwinds.
- USAGE IS ALWAYS REPORTED, INCLUDING ON ERROR PATHS where the provider reports partial usage. The client REPORTS tokens; the loop ENFORCES the budget. If the client can return without a usage figure, the token budget in bd-16g.1.3 is unenforceable and the loop's only backstop is its iteration cap.
- RESPONSE SIZE IS CAPPED. Stream into a bounded buffer and return `ResponseTooLarge` past the cap. Failure mode prevented: a pathological (or hostile) response that buffers until the process OOMs.
- DETERMINISM: with the ScriptedClient, two runs of the same fixture produce byte-identical transcripts. No wall-clock, no thread-id, no HashMap iteration order, no ambient RNG anywhere in this module.

TESTS.
- Unit: ScriptedClient replays a fixture in order; exhausting it yields `LlmError::FixtureExhausted` — not a panic, not a hang, not an empty response that the loop mistakes for a valid turn.
- Unit, NEGATIVE (this is where the real bugs live; table-driven over fixture bodies): body that is not JSON; JSON with a trailing comma; `arguments` delivered as a JSON *string* instead of an object (the single most common real-model malformation); a tool_call naming a tool we never offered; a tool_call with no arguments; a 200 with an empty body; a 429 with a valid Retry-After; a 429 with a garbage Retry-After ("soon"); a 529 overloaded; a body larger than the cap (assert `ResponseTooLarge`, assert memory does not grow unbounded); a response with no usage block.
- Unit: redaction — construct a client with a sentinel key, capture the `tracing` output across a full request/response/error cycle, assert the sentinel appears NOWHERE.
- E2E (hermetic): the scripted client drives one complete Propose->Report loop through bd-16g.1.3's harness with no network; run it twice and assert byte-identical transcripts.
- The Anthropic impl gets exactly one `#[ignore]`d integration test, run manually with a real key, asserting a real round-trip returns a well-formed `propose_experiment` tool_call. It must never run in CI, and the fact that it is ignored must be stated in the test's doc comment so nobody 'fixes' it by un-ignoring it.

LOGGING.
- info, one per call: {provider, model_id, request_id, input_tokens, output_tokens, stop_reason, latency_ms, attempt}.
- warn, on retry: {attempt, error_kind, retry_after_ms, backoff_ms}.
- error, on terminal failure: {error_kind, http_status, body_digest} — body_DIGEST, not body: response bodies echo the prompt and can be enormous. Bodies only at debug.
- debug, behind SCRIPTBOTS_LAB_TRACE=1 (the exact env var bd-16g.1 names): full system prompt, messages, raw response.
- ACCEPTANCE FOR LOGGING: a lab run that failed at the provider must be diagnosable from info-level lines alone — which call, which model, which stop_reason, how many tokens, how many attempts — with no local repro and without exposing a single prompt.
close_reason: Completed with lock-integrity follow-up 9f7f922: LlmClient seam plus feature-gated Anthropic path, and the reqwest/blocking futures-channel lock edge now passes locked core and feature-enabled app check/Clippy.

title: Experiment-spec schema and validator (knob ranges, budgets, seeds, non-finite rejection)
description:
SCOPE. The `ExperimentSpec` type, the JSON Schema handed to the model as the `propose_experiment` tool, a KNOB RANGE registry, and a total validator. OUT OF SCOPE: executing the spec (bd-16g.1.3), analyzing results (bd-16g.1.4), rendering (bd-16g.1.5). This is a pure leaf: types in, `Result<ValidatedSpec, Vec<SpecError>>` out, no I/O.

WHY. bd-16g.1's entire safety case rests on one sentence: the LLM is "a proposer/summarizer over a validated, bounded action space." This bead IS that action space. It is also what makes the lab useful rather than merely safe: a spec type that forces a falsifier, a matched seed cohort, and a declared metric turns the model's output from an opinion into an experiment. It serves the project by reusing the config validator that already exists rather than forking a second notion of "valid config" — the same rule the epic applies to detectors and event schemas.

*** READ THIS BEFORE YOU BELIEVE THE PARENT BEAD. *** bd-16g.1 says the model's proposals are "validated against the config schema" and that "even a maximally confused model can only request configurations the existing knob validator would accept from a human." That safety argument is HALF TRUE TODAY and this bead is what makes it fully true. Two facts from the code:
  (a) `ControlHandle::list_knobs` (crates/scriptbots-app/src/control.rs:275) flattens the serialized `ScriptBotsConfig` into `KnobEntry { path, kind, value, description }` (control.rs:136). There is NO min, NO max, NO range, NO sweepable flag. The "knob schema" the model would see carries values and types and nothing else.
  (b) `ScriptBotsConfig::validate()` (crates/scriptbots-core/src/lib.rs, the `reject_unless!` block around lines 3150-3505) enforces ADMISSIBILITY, not PLAUSIBILITY: mostly `>= 0.0`, `is_finite()`, `!= 0`, and a handful of genuine intervals (`population_crossover_chance` in [0,1], `carnivore_threshold` in (0,1), `spike_alignment_cosine` in (0,1]). `food_regrowth_rate = 1e9` PASSES. `mutation_rate = 1e6` PASSES.
So "validate against the knob schema" is currently a no-op for range checking. THIS BEAD SUPPLIES THE RANGE LAYER. Without it, the parent's safety story is a claim, not a mechanism.

DESIGN.
- HOME: `crates/scriptbots-app/src/lab/spec.rs`. Pure; no world lock, no storage, no network.
- TYPES:
    pub struct ExperimentSpec {
        pub hypothesis: String,          // bounded length
        pub falsifier: String,           // REQUIRED, non-empty: "what result would refute this"
        pub factors: Vec<Factor>,        // 1..=MAX_FACTORS
        pub seeds: SeedPlan,             // { base: u64, count: u16 } — the SAME cohort under every arm
        pub ticks_per_run: u64,
        pub metrics: Vec<MetricRef>,     // must name columns the summary tables actually have
        pub budget: SpecBudget,          // runs, ticks, wall_ms, tokens
    }
    pub struct Factor { pub knob_path: String, pub values: Vec<serde_json::Value> }
    pub struct ValidatedSpec { arms: Vec<Arm>, seeds: Vec<u64>, spec_hash: [u8; 32], /* ... */ }
    pub enum SpecError { UnknownKnob{path}, NotSweepable{path, reason}, OutOfRange{path, value, min, max}, NonFinite{path, raw}, NotRepresentableAsF32{path, value}, TypeMismatch{path, expected, got}, TooManyArms{n, max}, DuplicateArm{a, b}, CostExceedsBudget{runs, ticks, budget}, EmptyFalsifier, UnknownMetric{name}, ZeroSeeds, SeedAsFactor }
- THE RANGE REGISTRY is the heart of this bead: one table, keyed by knob path, of `KnobRange { min, max, kind, sweepable, rationale }`. Derive what you can from the `reject_unless!` constraints, but the EXPERIMENT range is strictly tighter than the ADMISSIBLE range and every entry needs a written rationale reviewed by a human. It is DATA, not code paths. Failure mode prevented: the model proposes `food_regrowth_rate = 1e9`, `validate()` shrugs (it only checks `>= 0.0` and finite), 20 runs burn an hour, and the notebook confidently reports on a degenerate world where every cell is saturated.
- SWEEPABILITY IS A THIRD STATE, not a boolean:
    * `Sweepable::Yes` — normal science knobs.
    * `Sweepable::FreshWorldOnly` — `world_width`, `world_height`, `food_cell_size`. control.rs:495-504 REFUSES these at runtime because they change the food-grid dimensions (`food_dimensions()`, core lib.rs:3506). The lab may sweep them because it starts fresh worlds, but a spec containing them may never be applied to a live world, and they change the digest domain, so they must be flagged.
    * `Sweepable::Never` — `rng_seed` above all. rng_seed is the MATCHED-SEED AXIS. A spec that sweeps it as a factor is confounded by construction: the arms differ in both the treatment and the noise. Reject with the named `SeedAsFactor` error and a message that explains the design, because a model that made this mistake will make it again unless the error teaches it.
- THE VALIDATOR RETURNS ALL ERRORS, NOT THE FIRST. `validate(&ExperimentSpec, &KnobSchema) -> Result<ValidatedSpec, Vec<SpecError>>`. The whole error list goes back to the model as one repair prompt. First-error-only doubles the number of turns and is the most reliable way to burn a token budget on a single malformed proposal.
- COST PRE-FLIGHT: `ValidatedSpec::cost() -> RunCost { runs: arms * seeds, ticks: runs * ticks_per_run }`, checked against the CLI budget BEFORE the first run starts. Not discovered at run 19 of 40.
- THE TOOL SCHEMA IS GENERATED FROM THE RUST TYPE. servers.rs already uses `utoipa::ToSchema` (see `KnobEntry`/`KnobUpdate` in control.rs:122-150); reuse it. Do not hand-write a JSON Schema and do not add a second schema crate. Failure mode prevented: schema drift, where the model is told about a field the validator does not accept, and every proposal fails for a reason the model cannot see.

HARD REQUIREMENTS.
- NON-FINITE REJECTION IS EXPLICIT AND LOCAL. `serde_json::Number` cannot hold NaN or Inf, so a non-finite value can only arrive as a STRING ("NaN", "Infinity", "1e400") — and note that control.rs's `set_f64` (line 559) only rejects non-finite on the string-coercion path. Do not lean on that downstream check: reject `NonFinite` here, at the spec boundary, with the path named. Failure mode prevented: a NaN mutation rate silently poisons the world and the notebook reports statistics over garbage.
- f64 -> f32 NARROWING IS CHECKED. Config floats are f32 (main.rs already has a test asserting "unrepresentable f32 input must fail"). Reject any value that does not round-trip f64 -> f32 -> f64 within tolerance, naming the path. Failure mode prevented: 1e40 silently becomes `inf` on the way into the config.
- DETERMINISM: arm expansion follows declaration order; seeds are `base..base+count` ascending; NO HashMap anywhere in expansion (BTreeMap or Vec). Two validations of the same spec produce a byte-identical `ValidatedSpec`, and its content hash IS the experiment id used for dedupe in bd-16g.1.3.
- NO PANIC ON ANY INPUT: a 10 MB hypothesis, 10^6 factor values, a path with empty segments ("a..b" — `insert_path` in control.rs:533 already errors on an empty path; mirror it), a path of 500 segments, NUL bytes, an empty string. Every one is a typed error.
- BOUNDED: `MAX_FACTORS`, `MAX_VALUES_PER_FACTOR`, `MAX_ARMS`, `MAX_SEEDS`, `MAX_TICKS_PER_RUN`, `MAX_STRING_LEN` are consts, and each is tested exactly at its boundary and one past it.

TESTS (table-driven; this is the bead where table-driven earns its keep).
- Accept: the canonical case — one factor, five values of `food_regrowth_rate`, eight seeds, a non-empty falsifier, a known metric.
- Reject, one case per variant, asserting the EXACT error: unknown path ("food.regrowth"); `rng_seed` as a factor (-> `SeedAsFactor`); bool into a float knob (-> `TypeMismatch`); `food_regrowth_rate = 1e9` (-> `OutOfRange`) — THIS IS THE MARQUEE TEST, because it is the case that PASSES `ScriptBotsConfig::validate()` and must still be rejected here; "NaN"/"Infinity"/"1e400" strings (-> `NonFinite`); 1e40 (-> `NotRepresentableAsF32`); zero seeds; empty falsifier; duplicate arms (the same knob map twice — a wasted arm is a wasted run out of a hard budget); arm count over MAX_ARMS; a cost exceeding the CLI budget; an unknown metric name.
- PROPERTY (the anti-drift test): for every ACCEPTED spec, every arm — applied through the same merge/deserialize path control.rs uses (`merge_value` -> `serde_path_to_error::deserialize::<ScriptBotsConfig>`) — yields a config whose `validate()` succeeds. Run it over every range endpoint and a seeded sample of the interior. This is the test that keeps the range table and the core validator from silently diverging.
- Round-trip: emitted JSON Schema -> a fixture of model-shaped tool_call arguments -> deserialize -> validate. Assert the schema's `required` set and the deserializer's required fields agree; a mismatch here is invisible until a live model trips on it.

LOGGING. The validator is a pure leaf and MUST NOT LOG. It returns `Vec<SpecError>` whose `Display` renders one actionable line per error, naming the path, the offending value, and the allowed range. That string is not a debug string — it is fed verbatim back to the model as the repair prompt, so it is a product surface. Design it to answer, in one line, "what exactly do I change to make this valid?". The CALLER (bd-16g.1.3) logs the list at warn with {hypothesis_id, attempt, error_count, first_error}.
close_reason: ExperimentSpec, KNOB_RANGES-backed total validator (all errors, not the first), deterministic arm expansion, cost pre-flight, SeedAsFactor refusal with a teaching message; 13 malformations table-tested

comments.author: Jeff Emanuel
comments.text:
KNOB-RANGE LAYER LANDED at f194141 (the spine of this bead, per the design note that "the parent's safety argument is half-true until bd-16g.1.2 supplies the range layer").

What exists now: KNOB_RANGES in scriptbots-core - min/max for the 26 numeric knobs external surfaces may set, each carrying a fresh_world_only flag (world_width/world_height/food_cell_size cannot be changed on a live world; apply_config_update rejects them, so a planner that does not know this emits specs that die at apply time one run at a time and blames the simulation). check_knob_ranges() reports EVERY violation at once, and is enforced in ControlHandle::apply_patch - the path every REST/MCP/CLI mutation actually travels.

The hole this closed was real and is now covered by a test that pins the exact request which used to be ACCEPTED: food_growth_rate = 1e9. ScriptBotsConfig::validate() checks admissibility (finite, non-negative) but declared no upper bounds, so absurd values sailed through from REST, from MCP, and therefore from any agent driving them.
Deliberate choices, each pinned by a test: bounds reject the ABSURD, not taste (metabolism_drain 0.9 and spike_damage 9.0 remain legal - a researcher must still be able to build a brutal world); every violation is reported at once (a caller fixing one knob per round trip gives up, and an autonomous one burns its budget); non-finite values are refused even for knobs with no declared range, because a NaN silently poisons every reduction it reaches. Absence from the table is a gap, not a licence - add ranges as knobs are exposed.

REMAINING FOR THIS BEAD: the ExperimentSpec type itself (knobs + ranges to sweep + N + seeds + budget), its cost pre-flight, and the Sweepable::{Yes,FreshWorldOnly,Never} classification surfaced through GET /api/knobs so a planner can discover what it may sweep without guessing. The range table and the fresh_world_only flag are the data that layer needs; it is now available to build on.

title: Lab state machine: Propose->Validate->Execute->Analyze->Decide->Report with hard budgets
description:
SCOPE. The loop itself: an explicit `Phase` state machine, the budget ledger, the repair/abandon policy, the termination proof, and the append-as-you-go session file. OUT OF SCOPE: the provider (bd-16g.1.1), the spec schema (bd-16g.1.2), the statistics (bd-16g.1.4), the notebook (bd-16g.1.5), the adversarial corpus (bd-16g.1.6). This bead is the ORCHESTRATOR and it owns exactly one thing the others cannot: the guarantee that the loop always terminates, always within budget, and always leaves an artifact.

WHY. bd-16g.1's thesis is "a state machine, not a free-form chat." That sentence is the entire safety and honesty argument of the epic's #1 feature. A chat loop with a budget check bolted on will, in practice, oscillate (propose -> reject -> repair -> reject), drain its tokens, and exit with nothing to show. This bead is where that is made impossible by construction.

DESIGN.
- HOME: `crates/scriptbots-app/src/lab/mod.rs`, driven by a proper `lab` SUBCOMMAND in main.rs's clap CLI. Note that `--det-check` is a bare flag on the `AppCli` god-struct (main.rs:1019); do not follow that pattern here — the lab has its own flags (--goal, --budget, --offline-fixture, --lab-seed, --out) and belongs in a subcommand.
- THE MACHINE:
    enum Phase { Propose, Validate, Execute, Analyze, Decide, Report, Done }
    struct LabSession { goal: String, budget: Budget, spent: Spend, transcript: Vec<Turn>, experiments: Vec<ExperimentRecord>, rng: SmallRng, iterations: u32 }
    fn step(&mut self, client: &dyn LlmClient) -> Result<Phase, LabError>;
  Every transition is a function of (state, model response, validator verdict) — never of the clock, never of ambient entropy.
- EXECUTE DELEGATES TO bd-2z0.5.5'S MATCHED-SEED RUNNER. DO NOT REIMPLEMENT IT. If the runner is not ready, this bead is BLOCKED — that is the correct dependency, not a license to fork a second runner that will drift. The isolation discipline to inherit is already in the tree: `run_det_check` (crates/scriptbots-app/src/main.rs:572) composes the parent's EFFECTIVE config, pins an explicit seed, serializes the WHOLE config to a TOML layer in a temp file, and spawns `--config-only` children with `--config <layer>` plus `SCRIPTBOTS_RNG_SEED` and `RAYON_NUM_THREADS`, then parses JSON from stdout. The comment at main.rs:575 records WHY the full config layer is required: env-only forwarding silently loses `--config`/`--rng-seed` and the two children then run different scenarios. A lab that forgets this will produce "matched-seed" runs that are not matched.
- THE LAB NEVER TOUCHES A LIVE WORLD. Say it in the module doc. `ControlHandle::apply_patch` (control.rs:469) enqueues `ControlCommand::UpdateConfig` against the running `WorldState` and refuses runtime dimension changes (control.rs:495). Experiments run in FRESH worlds. A lab that patches a live sim produces confounded results AND can wedge a user's running session — two failure modes for the price of one shortcut.
- BUDGETS ARE CHECKED AT EVERY TRANSITION, NOT ONLY AT EXECUTE. `Budget { max_runs, max_ticks, max_wall: Duration, max_tokens }` vs `Spend`. Any overrun -> `Phase::Report` with `partial: true` and an honest ledger line naming WHICH bound was hit. Failure mode prevented: a loop that keeps asking "one more experiment?" until the tokens are gone and there is no artifact.
- TERMINATION IS PROVED, NOT HOPED. Two independent backstops: (1) a hard `max_iterations` cap that no other budget can override — it is the only thing that still works if the provider stops reporting token usage; (2) a NO-PROGRESS DETECTOR: if a Decide turn produces a spec whose `spec_hash` (bd-16g.1.2) equals one already executed, stop and report. The propose->reject->repair->propose-the-same-thing oscillation is the single most common real-world LLM loop pathology and it must be a first-class, tested exit, not an accident of the budget running out.
- VALIDATE IS A BOUNDED REPAIR LOOP (default 2 retries): reject -> hand the FULL `Vec<SpecError>` back to the model -> re-propose. After N failures, ABANDON that hypothesis and record it in the notebook as "the model could not produce a valid spec for X, here is what it kept getting wrong." That is an honest negative result and a genuinely useful artifact — not a crash, and not a silent skip.
- THE SESSION FILE IS APPENDED AS IT HAPPENS, not written at the end. Every turn, every `ExperimentRecord` (spec_hash, run_ids, seeds, config hash, digest, summary stats) lands on disk immediately. Failure mode prevented: an 8-hour lab run that dies in Report and leaves nothing behind.
- WALL-CLOCK IS ADMITTED IN EXACTLY ONE PLACE: the wall budget's terminal check. It must NEVER influence a decision that affects the science — no "we have time left, add more seeds," because that makes the run's results a function of how fast the machine was. Wall exhaustion is a stop condition and nothing more.

HARD REQUIREMENTS.
- With a `ScriptedClient` and a fixed `--lab-seed`, the ENTIRE session is deterministic: same transcript, same specs, same seeds, same digests, same notebook bytes — modulo an explicitly enumerated set of non-reproducible provenance fields (durations, host, timestamps) which bd-16g.1.5 must segregate into one maskable block.
- NO PANIC, EVER. Every phase returns `Result`; the top level turns `LabError` into a partial report plus a non-zero exit, never an unwind. clippy pedantic + nursery clean (workspace lints are on).
- NEVER EXCEEDS A BUDGET, including when the model proposes a spec that WOULD exceed it — that is a Validate rejection (bd-16g.1.2's `CostExceedsBudget`), not an Execute-time abort after the first three runs are already spent.
- INTERRUPTIBLE: Ctrl-C between runs yields a partial report and a valid session file, not a truncated JSON blob.

TESTS.
- Unit, scripted transitions: happy path Propose->Validate->Execute->Analyze->Decide->Report; propose-invalid-then-repair-then-succeed; propose-invalid-3x-then-ABANDON; the no-progress oscillation terminates via the dedupe path.
- Unit, one case per budget (four separate tests, each asserting the phase lands on Report with `partial: true` and the notebook names the exhausted bound): runs, ticks, wall, tokens. Plus the case where the provider reports NO usage at all — assert `max_iterations` still terminates the loop.
- Unit, NEGATIVE: the model re-proposes an already-executed spec (dedupe fires, zero runs spent); the model proposes 50 arms with 3 runs of budget left (rejected at Validate, budget UNTOUCHED — assert `spent.runs` did not move); the client errors mid-Execute (already-completed runs are retained and reported, not discarded).
- E2E (hermetic, CI, no mocks): `lab --goal "characterize how food_regrowth_rate affects the carnivore fraction" --budget 6-runs --offline-fixture tests/fixtures/lab/food_regrowth.json` against the REAL sim and the REAL FrankenSQLite run DB — AGENTS.md's storage contract means a real file with a real advisory lease on a real worker thread. NO MOCKED SIM, NO MOCKED DB (bd-16g.1 says this explicitly and it is the only way this test proves anything). Assert: the notebook exists, contains >= 1 claim carrying run_ids, `reproduce.sh` exists, and re-running it regenerates identical summary tables.
- E2E determinism: run the same fixture twice into two temp dirs; assert the notebooks are byte-identical after masking exactly the declared non-reproducible block.

LOGGING.
- info, ONE EVENT PER TRANSITION, with exactly the fields bd-16g.1 demands: {phase, session_id, hypothesis_id, spec_hash, arms, seeds, runs_spent/runs_budget, ticks_spent/ticks_budget, tokens_spent/tokens_budget, wall_ms, decision, rationale_summary}. `rationale_summary` is the model's own one-line reason, truncated — without it, the log tells you what happened but never why.
- warn: every Validate rejection (with the error list), every repair attempt, every abandonment.
- error: terminal `LabError` only, with the phase and the last spec_hash.
- debug behind SCRIPTBOTS_LAB_TRACE=1: full prompts and responses (the env var name is fixed by bd-16g.1; do not invent a second one).
- ACCEPTANCE FOR LOGGING: kill the process mid-run, and from info-level lines ALONE reconstruct which experiment was in flight, how much of each budget remained, and what the last decision was. If you cannot, the fields are wrong.

comments.text: NOT STARTED, deliberately. bv --robot-triage listed this as a 'quick win', but bv's quick_wins heuristic does NOT filter on blockers: this bead is blocked by bd-2z0.5.5 (matched-seed runner) and bd-2z0.12.2, and its own brief says in capitals that EXECUTE must delegate to bd-2z0.5.5's runner and that a missing runner means BLOCKED, not a license to fork a second one that will drift. title: Analysis layer: effect sizes with CIs over matched-seed run summaries
description:
SCOPE. A pure statistics leaf: effect sizes with confidence intervals over RUN SUMMARIES from a matched-seed design. OUT OF SCOPE: running the experiments (bd-2z0.5.5), producing the summaries (bd-2z0.5.6 exports), rendering figures (bd-16g.1.5), and change-point/regime detection (bd-16g.2.1 OWNS that — if the lab wants regime labels it CALLS the detector; a second half-detector invented here is exactly the duplication the bd-16g epic's shared-substrate rule forbids).

WHY. This is the bead that decides whether the autonomous scientist is a scientist or a bullshit generator. An LLM handed raw numbers will confidently report a difference between two arms that is pure seed noise. The parent bead's promise is "an effect-size table with confidence intervals," and the difference between that and "arm B looked higher" is entirely in this module. Encode the honesty rules in TYPES here, so that bd-16g.1.5 can enforce them mechanically and the model cannot route around them.

DESIGN.
- HOME: `crates/scriptbots-app/src/lab/stats.rs`. Pure functions with explicit params structs, in the same leaf discipline as bd-16g.2.1: no I/O, no clock, no ambient RNG, no simulation types. If a second consumer appears (bd-16g.12's Elo, bd-16g.6's archive scores), extract then — not now (AGENTS.md's bar for new files/crates is very high).
- INPUT CONTRACT — SUMMARIES, NOT ROWS:
    pub struct RunSummary { run_id: u64, arm_id: u16, seed: u64, config_hash: [u8;32], digest: [u8;32], ticks: u64, metrics: BTreeMap<String, f64> }
  One row per RUN, produced by bd-2z0.5.6's exports. The analysis NEVER reads raw agent rows. Failure mode prevented (twofold): a lab that drags 10M `agents` rows through SQL to compute a mean, and — worse — an LLM handed raw rows that hallucinates a trend over them. The model sees the `Effect` structs, not the data.
- THE DESIGN IS MATCHED-SEED, SO THE DEFAULT ANALYSIS IS PAIRED. This is not a preference; an unpaired test over matched runs throws away the entire variance reduction the matched-seed cohort was built to buy, and then the lab reports "no significant effect" for effects that are plainly there.
    paired_diff(a: &[RunSummary], b: &[RunSummary], metric: &str) -> Result<PairedEffect, StatsError>
      // pairs strictly BY SEED; if the cohorts are not seed-matched -> StatsError::UnmatchedSeeds. Never silently fall back to unpaired.
      // PairedEffect { n_pairs, mean_diff, sd_diff, cohens_dz, ci: (f64,f64), test: TestName }
    hedges_g(a, b, metric) -> Result<Effect, StatsError>   // the unpaired fallback, WITH the small-sample correction.
      // Use Hedges' g, not raw Cohen's d: n is typically < 20 here and raw d is biased UPWARD, which makes the lab systematically overclaim.
    bootstrap_ci(values: &[f64], statistic: fn(&[f64]) -> f64, iters: u32, rng: &mut SmallRng) -> (f64, f64)
      // Percentile or BCa — pick one, DOCUMENT which, and say so in the notebook's methods section. The RNG is SEEDED and threaded in; `rand::random()` here would mean a notebook whose CIs change on every render, which silently destroys the reproducibility claim the whole epic rests on.
    spearman(x: &[f64], y: &[f64]) -> Result<Correlation, StatsError>   // monotone dose-response over a swept factor; tie-corrected ranks, with an explicit tie test.
- HONESTY RULES ENCODED AS TYPES, NOT PROSE:
    * `Effect` carries { n, test: TestName, alternative, statistic, ci, correction: Option<Correction>, underpowered: bool }. There is no way to construct a naked p-value with no n and no named test. A struct that cannot represent the lie cannot be used to tell it.
    * MULTIPLE COMPARISONS: `adjust(&mut [Effect], Correction::HolmBonferroni)`. When k arms are compared, the notebook prints BOTH raw and adjusted. Failure mode prevented — and this is the exact way autonomous-scientist demos lie: a 5-arm sweep, 4 pairwise tests, one lands at p=0.04, and it becomes the headline claim.
    * `underpowered: true` when n < MIN_N (default 5 pairs). bd-16g.1.5 must refuse to let a claim cite an underpowered effect as support without an explicit "preliminary" caveat. Set the flag here; enforce it there.
- DETERMINISM IS A FLOAT-ORDER PROBLEM AND MUST BE TREATED AS ONE. Sort inputs by seed ascending BEFORE any reduction; use Welford (or a documented compensated summation) for means/variances. Then TEST invariance to input row order. Failure mode prevented: Parquet hands back rows in a different order on a different run, the mean differs in the 12th decimal, the CI shifts, and the notebook's "reproduces bit-for-bit" claim becomes false without anyone noticing.
- Non-finite metric values are rejected with a typed error — never propagated as NaN (same rule as bd-16g.2.1). A NaN that reaches a results table is a bug, not a value.

HARD REQUIREMENTS.
- Pure: no I/O, no wall-clock, no ambient entropy, no HashMap iteration order in any path that affects output.
- O(n) or O(n log n); the bootstrap's cost is `iters * n` and `iters` is a documented, bounded param.
- NO PANIC on: n = 0, n = 1, all-equal values, ZERO VARIANCE in one or both arms (this is the single most likely real crash in this bead — a zero-variance denominator must yield a defined result or a typed `StatsError::ZeroVariance`, never a divide-by-zero NaN that flows into the notebook), mismatched cohort lengths, a metric absent from one summary.
- No `partial_cmp().unwrap()` anywhere — ranking floats with it is both a panic and a nondeterminism. Use `total_cmp` or a bits-based total order, and tiebreak by seed.

TESTS.
- KNOWN-ANSWER fixtures: hand-computed paired mean difference, Cohen's dz, Hedges' g (with the correction factor written out), and Spearman rho including ties. Compute the expected values INDEPENDENTLY and cite the source in the test comment. Do NOT "assert against whatever the code prints today" — that is how a statistics bug gets frozen into a golden file and then defended.
- Degenerate, one case each: n=0; n=1; two identical arms (effect exactly 0, CI straddling 0); zero variance in one arm; a NaN metric (-> typed error); cohorts that are not seed-matched (-> `UnmatchedSeeds`).
- ORDER INVARIANCE: seeded shuffle of the input rows -> BIT-IDENTICAL output. This is the test that catches float-order nondeterminism, and it is the one that will actually fire in CI.
- BOOTSTRAP DETERMINISM: same seed -> byte-identical CI; different seed -> a different CI within a documented tolerance. Assert BOTH. Asserting only the first passes trivially if the RNG was never wired in at all.
- CALIBRATION PROPERTY (the test that no single fixture will ever replace): on synthetic data with a KNOWN true effect and known noise, the nominal 95% CI covers the true effect in ~95% of 200 seeded trials — assert coverage in [0.90, 0.99]. This catches an off-by-a-factor-of-two in the CI width, which is a bug that looks completely plausible in every hand-checked example.
- NULL PROPERTY (the "does the lab cry wolf" test): two arms drawn from the SAME distribution produce effects whose CIs contain 0 in the large majority of seeded trials, and Holm-adjusted significance fires at approximately the nominal rate. A lab that reports discoveries from null data is worse than no lab.

LOGGING. Pure leaf: NO LOGGING. Instead, every `Effect` carries a complete evidence payload — metric, arms compared, n, test name, statistic, CI, correction applied, underpowered flag — so the caller logs one self-explanatory line and bd-16g.1.5 can write a full methods sentence without re-deriving anything. Design the struct so that a log line built from it answers "what was compared, how, over how many runs, and how sure are we?" without the reader opening the source. That is the same rule bd-16g.2.1 set for detections, and for the same reason.

title: Notebook renderer with provenance enforcement and reproduce.sh emission
description:
SCOPE. Turn a completed `LabSession` into an artifact directory: a markdown notebook, deterministic charts, and an EXECUTABLE `reproduce.sh` — and FAIL THE BUILD if any claim lacks provenance. OUT OF SCOPE: the loop (bd-16g.1.3), the statistics (bd-16g.1.4), the LLM (bd-16g.1.1). This bead is the honesty gate. It is the last thing standing between a confident language model and a document that looks like science.

WHY. bd-16g.1: "a claim without a supporting run_id is a build error in the notebook renderer." That single sentence is the epic's answer to the obvious objection ("isn't an LLM writing up results just an automated bullshit machine?"). If it is implemented as a lint over rendered markdown, it will be defeated in a week by a model that phrases a claim as a caption. Implement it as a TYPE.

DESIGN.
- HOME: `crates/scriptbots-app/src/lab/notebook.rs`. Output directory: `runs/lab-<session_id>/` — reuse the `runs/` convention the storage contract already established, and PRINT the chosen path exactly as the app prints its storage path (AGENTS.md: "The app prints the selected file path; use that exact path for later reads and exports").
- PROVENANCE IS A TYPE, NOT A CHECK:
    struct Claim { text: String, support: Support, falsifier: String }
    enum Support { Effect(EffectRef), Descriptive(Vec<RunRef>) }     // NOTE: there is no `Unsupported` variant
    struct RunRef { run_id: u64, seed: u64, config_hash: [u8;32], digest: [u8;32], ticks: u64 }
  A `Claim` CANNOT BE CONSTRUCTED without support. The failure mode this eliminates is the entire risk of the epic: a fluent sentence with no run behind it. Make it unrepresentable rather than detected.
  The checks that a type cannot express, the renderer still enforces as hard errors: every `EffectRef`'s run_ids exist in the session's `ExperimentRecord`s; every cited digest equals the one recorded AT RUN TIME (not recomputed at render time — a digest recomputed from a re-run is not evidence, it is a tautology); no claim cites an `underpowered` Effect (bd-16g.1.4) without the word "preliminary" and a mandatory caveat line; every mandatory section is present AND non-empty.
- MANDATORY SECTIONS (empty -> render error, one test each): Goal; Methods (base config, knobs swept, arms, seed cohort, ticks/run, git rev, rustc version, target triple, enabled features, model id); Results (effect table with CIs, n per cell, RAW and ADJUSTED p); Claims (each with its falsifier); What Would Falsify This; What I Did Not Test; Budget Ledger (spent vs budget for runs/ticks/wall/tokens, and whether the session was partial and which bound ended it); Reproduce.
- reproduce.sh MUST VERIFY, NOT NARRATE. It re-runs every (arm x seed) using the SAME child-process discipline as `run_det_check` (crates/scriptbots-app/src/main.rs:572): write the full effective config as a TOML layer per arm, invoke the binary with `--config <layer>` and a pinned seed — NOT env-only forwarding, whose failure is documented in the comment at main.rs:575 — then re-derive the summary tables and DIFF them against the ones the notebook cites, exiting non-zero on any difference. A reproduce.sh that merely prints the commands it would have run is theater.
- *** THE DIGEST CAVEAT — READ crates/scriptbots-core/src/lib.rs:9316-9327 BEFORE WRITING THE PROVENANCE PROSE. *** `characterization_digest_v0` is documented, in its own doc comment, as "a stable V0 regression oracle for one pinned build lane, not a checkpoint or replay guarantee." It hashes `f32::to_bits()` values and four samples from a CLONED RNG, and it requires a QUIESCENT tick boundary — it returns `CharacterizationError::NonQuiescent` if `pending_deaths`/`pending_spawns`/`simulation_commands` are non-empty (lib.rs:9331). Therefore the notebook must NOT claim "bit-for-bit on any machine." What it may honestly claim, and what the template must say: (a) identical digest under the SAME BUILD LANE — so record rustc version, target triple, feature flags, and git rev in the provenance block; (b) identical SUMMARY TABLES under reproduce.sh. Overclaiming here would make the honesty gate itself dishonest, which is the most embarrassing possible bug in this bead.
- CHARTS MUST BE DETERMINISTIC: no embedded timestamps, no font-hash nondeterminism, fixed size/DPI, stable element ordering. Otherwise bd-16g.1.3's byte-identical-notebook test is impossible and the reproducibility claim is unverifiable. Prefer emitting SVG directly over adding a heavy plotting dependency (AGENTS.md's bar for new dependencies and files is high; a chart is a few hundred lines of SVG).

HARD REQUIREMENTS.
- Rendering is a PURE FUNCTION of the session, except for ONE designated "Environment / non-reproducible" block (wall durations, hostname, timestamps). Segregate it into exactly one region so the byte-identical test masks one region and nothing else. Scatter those fields through the document and the determinism test becomes unwritable.
- NON-FINITE NUMBERS NEVER REACH THE MARKDOWN. Format every float through one helper that raises a render error on NaN/inf. A NaN in a results table is a bug that must stop the build, not a cell that reads "NaN" and gets shipped.
- NO PANIC ON ANY SESSION — including a session with ZERO completed experiments. That must render an honest notebook ("no experiments completed within budget; here is what was attempted and why each failed"). It is precisely the artifact you most need when the loop failed, and it is the one a naive renderer will panic on (empty vectors, no arms, no effects).
- THE LLM NEVER SUPPLIES A PATH. Session id is generated locally; every write stays inside the session directory (assert with a path-canonicalization check, not a string prefix check). bd-16g.1's safety argument — "it never writes SQL, never writes code, never touches the filesystem" — is only true if this bead makes it true.

TESTS.
- Unit, MARQUEE NEGATIVE: a `Claim` whose `EffectRef` names a run_id absent from the session -> render ERROR. This is the test that proves the honesty gate exists.
- Unit: a cited digest that does not match the one recorded at run time -> render error.
- Unit: a claim citing an `underpowered` effect with no caveat -> render error.
- Unit, table-driven: each mandatory section empty -> render error (one case per section).
- Unit: a NaN anywhere in the results table -> render error.
- Unit: a zero-experiment session renders, honestly, without panic.
- Unit: a claim whose text contains markdown/HTML injection (from a hostile model response — see bd-16g.1.6) is escaped, and cannot forge a fake provenance table.
- GOLDEN: a fixed fixture session renders byte-identical markdown across two runs and across CI machines, masking ONLY the declared environment block.
- E2E: bd-16g.1.3's hermetic loop emits a reproduce.sh, and THIS TEST ACTUALLY EXECUTES IT — asserting exit code 0 and that the regenerated summary tables equal the cited ones. A reproduce.sh that has never been executed in CI is a reproduce.sh that does not work; that is not a hypothesis, it is a certainty.

LOGGING.
- info on emit: {session_id, out_dir, claims, experiments, runs, charts, partial, exhausted_budget}.
- error PER PROVENANCE VIOLATION: {claim_index, claim_text_truncated, violation, missing_run_id?} — the CI failure must NAME THE OFFENDING CLAIM. "provenance check failed" with no claim text costs an hour of staring at a notebook.
- warn when the session was partial, naming which budget bound ended it, so the reader of the log knows the notebook is incomplete before they read the notebook.

title: Adversarial-LLM robustness suite (malformed, absurd, contradictory responses)
description:
SCOPE. A hostile fixture corpus plus the harness that replays it through the FULL lab stack — client (bd-16g.1.1) -> validator (bd-16g.1.2) -> state machine (bd-16g.1.3) -> renderer (bd-16g.1.5) — asserting the invariants hold under every kind of model misbehavior. OUT OF SCOPE: fixing the bugs it finds. Those are edits to .1/.2/.3/.5, and finding them is the entire point.

WHY. bd-16g.1's safety argument is: "The LLM is a proposer/summarizer over a validated, bounded action space. Even a maximally confused model can only request configurations that the existing knob validator would accept from a human." That is a CLAIM. This bead is the adversary that turns it into a fact. It is also the bead that keeps the lab honest across model upgrades: when a new model version starts emitting a differently-malformed shape, it must fail LOUDLY in CI, not quietly produce a notebook full of nonsense that nobody checks.

DESIGN.
- HOME: `crates/scriptbots-app/tests/lab_adversarial.rs` plus `tests/fixtures/lab/adversarial/*.json`.
- FIXTURES ARE DATA. Adding an adversarial case must require adding ONE FILE, never editing Rust. That is what lets the corpus grow the moment a real model misbehaves in the wild: paste its actual response into a fixture and the suite defends against it forever. A corpus that requires a code change per case will stop growing after the first week.
    { "name": "...",
      "turns": [ /* raw provider responses, verbatim */ ],
      "expect": { "terminates": true, "max_runs_spent": 0, "outcome": "AbandonedHypothesis" | "PartialReport" | "Report",
                  "must_not": ["panic", "budget_overrun", "write_outside_session_dir", "process_spawn"] } }

THE CORPUS (each entry NAMES the failure mode it prevents).
 1. MALFORMED TRANSPORT: truncated JSON; a trailing comma; `arguments` delivered as a JSON *string* rather than an object (the most common real-model malformation); a tool_call with no arguments at all; a 4 MB response body (unbounded buffering -> OOM).
 2. SCHEMA-ADJACENT: right field names, wrong types (mutation rate as a bool); unknown extra fields; a MISSING `falsifier`; unicode/emoji/CRLF/NUL bytes in the hypothesis; a 1 MB hypothesis string (log flooding AND markdown injection into the notebook).
 3. ABSURD BUDGETS: 10^9 seeds; 10^12 ticks_per_run; 10^6 arms; ticks_per_run = 0; seed count = 0. ASSERT ZERO RUNS EXECUTE. The budget must be rejected at Validate, before Execute — not discovered halfway through a run that has already burned an hour.
 4. OUT-OF-RANGE SCIENCE: `food_regrowth_rate = 1e9` — THIS FIXTURE IS THE PROOF THAT bd-16g.1.2'S RANGE TABLE EXISTS AT ALL, because that value PASSES `ScriptBotsConfig::validate()` (which only checks `>= 0.0` and finite; see the `reject_unless!` block in crates/scriptbots-core/src/lib.rs around 3150-3505). Also: a negative value on a non-negative knob; "NaN"/"Infinity"/"1e400" as strings; a value that overflows f32.
 5. FORBIDDEN FACTORS: `rng_seed` as a factor (confounds the matched-seed design by construction); `world_width`/`food_cell_size` against a live world (`ControlHandle::apply_patch` refuses runtime dimension changes at crates/scriptbots-app/src/control.rs:495-504); a knob path that does not exist; a path with an empty segment ("a..b").
 6. CONTRADICTORY / PATHOLOGICAL REASONING: a Decide turn that contradicts its own Analyze; the SAME spec proposed five times running (the no-progress detector must fire and the loop must exit); a hypothesis with no falsifier; and — the important one — a Report turn asserting a claim with NO run behind it, which the renderer must refuse. That fixture is the executable proof of the honesty gate.
 7. INJECTION: a response instructing the loop to "ignore previous instructions", to run `rm -rf`, to write a file, to emit SQL, or to shell out. ASSERT: no filesystem write outside the session dir (post-run inventory of a temp-dir sandbox, using canonicalized paths — a string-prefix check is defeated by `..`); no process spawn other than the sanctioned run children; NO SQL STRING IS EVER CONSTRUCTED FROM MODEL OUTPUT anywhere in the stack. The model's action space is `propose_experiment` and nothing else; this fixture is what proves it rather than asserting it.
 8. PROVIDER-LAYER HOSTILITY: 429 with a garbage Retry-After ("soon"); 200 with an empty body; a stream ending mid-token; a response with NO usage counts — the token budget is then unenforceable, so assert the `max_iterations` cap still terminates the loop. That is the exact scenario the second backstop in bd-16g.1.3 exists for.

INVARIANTS ASSERTED FOR EVERY FIXTURE (not per-case; these run on all of them):
  - TERMINATES within `max_iterations`.
  - NEVER PANICS (the harness catches unwinds and fails the case with the fixture name).
  - NEVER EXCEEDS ANY BUDGET (runs/ticks/wall/tokens).
  - NEVER WRITES OUTSIDE THE SESSION DIRECTORY.
  - ALWAYS LEAVES A NOTEBOOK — even when the notebook's honest content is "the model produced nothing usable, here is every attempt and why each was rejected." The failure mode prevented is a lab that dies leaving no artifact and no explanation, which is indistinguishable from a lab that was never run.

HARD REQUIREMENTS.
- HERMETIC: zero network (the ScriptedClient from bd-16g.1.1 is the only client this suite may use; assert it).
- DETERMINISTIC: fixed `--lab-seed`; two runs of the corpus produce identical outcomes.
- FAST: tiny worlds, tiny tick counts, a documented total wall budget. The suite exercises the CONTROL PATH, not the simulation; a corpus that takes 20 minutes will be disabled within a month.
- RUNS IN CI ON EVERY PR. A robustness suite marked `#[ignore]` is decoration. State this in the test file's doc comment so nobody quietly ignores it to make a red build green.

TESTS. This bead IS tests, so its acceptance is a MUTATION CHECK: temporarily disable each guard and assert that at least one fixture goes RED. The guards, and the fixture that must catch each: the range table (fixture 4), the budget pre-flight (fixture 3), the no-progress detector (fixture 6), the provenance/claim gate (fixture 6), the response size cap (fixture 1), the path sandbox (fixture 7), the max_iterations cap (fixture 8), the seed-as-factor rejection (fixture 5). RECORD THAT MAPPING IN THE TEST FILE. A guard that no fixture exercises is not a guard, it is a comment; and a future refactor that removes one must fail visibly rather than quietly widening the action space.

LOGGING. The harness prints, per fixture: {name, outcome, runs_spent, tokens_spent, iterations, terminal_error}. ON FAILURE it dumps the full session transcript and that case's info-level log. An adversarial failure must be fully diagnosable from CI output alone — the person who broke it will be looking at a CI page, not at a local repro, and the fixture that caught them will be one they have never read.

title: Intervention toolkit: droughts, meteors, predator injections, and terrain painting as replayable commands
description:
THE IDEA. A coherent intervention toolkit — the "god mode" that a living-world simulator demands — implemented as DETERMINISTIC, JOURNALED, REPLAYABLE commands rather than as UI side effects: drought (suppress regrowth in a region for T ticks), meteor (kill/scorch a disc), predator injection (spawn a carnivore cohort with chosen genomes), terrain painting (repaint tiles/biomes), food embargo/bloom, closed-world flip, and cohort spawning from the MAP-Elites archive (bd-16g.6).

WHY IT MATTERS. Two distinct payoffs. (1) FUN: perturbing a living ecosystem and watching it respond is the most engaging thing a user can do; today the app can barely spawn an agent. (2) SCIENCE: these are exactly the "interventions" the README promises ("toggle closed worlds, inject carnivore cohorts, freeze food diffusion to test resilience") and exactly what bd-2z0.11.4 (paired checkpoint-branch intervention studies) needs as its ACTUATOR — that bead cannot run a drought study if nothing can cause a drought. Making every intervention a journaled command means a hand-played session is a reproducible experiment, and an LLM scientist (bd-16g.1) can run the same interventions programmatically. This is the bead that turns bd-2z0.11.4 from a plan into a possibility.

DESIGN.
- Every intervention is a typed ControlCommand variant applied inside the tick loop (never a direct mutation from a renderer — see bd-37m for why that rule exists), validated, and recorded in the command journal (bd-2z0.5.2) with tick + parameters + issuing surface.
- Region shapes are explicit and toroidal-aware (disc, rect, all), with the wraparound semantics tested — the world is a torus and a naive rect will silently mis-handle the seam.
- Determinism: applying the same journaled command sequence to the same seed reproduces the same world (this is the acceptance test, and it is what makes interventions science rather than vandalism).
- Every intervention is available from ALL surfaces uniformly: GPU lab, TUI palette, REST, MCP, CLI script — one command enum, four thin adapters.
- Safety/honesty: an intervention that would break an invariant (spawning past a hard population cap, painting invalid terrain) is REJECTED with a clear error, never silently clamped into a different experiment than the one the user asked for.

ACCEPTANCE. A recorded session of interventions replays bit-exactly; the same interventions issued via REST/MCP/TUI/GPU produce identical journals; toroidal region math is correct at the seam; bd-2z0.11.4 can express a drought study purely as a command script.

TESTS + LOGGING (required).
- Unit: per-intervention semantics on hand-built worlds (drought suppresses exactly the intended cells for exactly T ticks; meteor kills exactly the agents inside the disc INCLUDING across the seam; embargo restores cleanly).
- Unit: validation rejects out-of-range/invalid parameters with actionable errors.
- Determinism/E2E: script -> journal -> replay -> identical digest; and cross-surface equivalence (the same intervention from four surfaces yields identical journal rows).
- Logging: every applied intervention at info with tick, kind, region, params, affected-agent/cell counts — an ecosystem crash caused by a mis-parameterized meteor must be obvious from the log.

title: Intervention command set: drought, meteor, cohort injection, terrain paint, embargo (toroidal-exact)
description:
SCOPE. The intervention command set itself: the typed variants, the toroidal region math, the timed-effect state, and validation. Journaling, replay proof, and cross-surface equivalence are bd-16g.10.2. This bead is also the ACTUATOR bd-2z0.11.4 (paired intervention studies) is blocked on — that bead cannot run a drought study if nothing in the codebase can cause a drought.

WHY. Two payoffs, both real. FUN: perturbing a living ecosystem and watching it respond is the most engaging thing a user can do, and today the app can barely spawn an agent. SCIENCE: these are literally the interventions the README already promises. Making each one a typed, validated, journaled command is what turns a hand-played session into a reproducible experiment instead of vandalism.

CODE FACTS THAT DICTATE THE DESIGN (crates/scriptbots-core/src/lib.rs).
- `ControlCommand` today is `{ UpdateConfig, UpdateSelection, UpdateSimulation }`. `apply_control_command` applies config and selection IMMEDIATELY, while `SimulationCommand` is QUEUED (`enqueue_simulation_command` / `drain_simulation_commands`). Interventions MUST take the QUEUED path. An intervention applied immediately from a host thread lands on whichever tick the mutex happened to be free — that is nondeterminism walking in through the front door, and it makes the whole bead pointless.
- `WorldState::step` is a fixed pipeline: aging -> food_dynamics -> sense -> brains -> actuation -> temperature -> food -> combat -> death_cleanup -> reproduction -> population -> spawn_commit -> accumulate -> record_history -> persistence. Add ONE drain point: `stage_interventions`, between `stage_food_dynamics` and `stage_sense`, so an intervention is visible to every agent's senses on the tick it lands and no agent ever acts on a half-applied world.
- The world is a TORUS: `toroidal_delta(a, b, extent)` and `WorldState::wrap_position` are used everywhere in sensing, combat, and spawning. Any region shape that does not use the same metric will silently select the wrong agents.

DESIGN.
```
enum Intervention {
  Drought { region: Region, ticks: u32, growth_scale: f32 },   // scale food regrowth
  Bloom   { region: Region, ticks: u32, growth_scale: f32 },
  Embargo { region: Region, ticks: u32 },                      // suppress intake
  Meteor  { region: Region, lethality: f32, scorch: f32 },     // damage agents + zero food
  PaintTerrain { region: Region, kind: TerrainKind, fertility_bias: Option<f32> },
  InjectCohort { count: u16, genome: CohortSource, placement: Placement },
  SpawnFromArchive { cells: CellSelector, count: u16, placement: Placement }, // bd-16g.6.3
  SetClosedWorld { closed: bool },
}
enum Region { All, Disc { cx: f32, cy: f32, r: f32 }, Rect { x: f32, y: f32, w: f32, h: f32 } }
```
- TOROIDAL EXACTNESS IS THE HEART OF THIS BEAD.
  - Disc membership: `let dx = toroidal_delta(p.x, cx, world_width); let dy = toroidal_delta(p.y, cy, world_height); dx*dx + dy*dy <= r*r`. The naive `(p.x - cx)^2 + (p.y - cy)^2` spares every agent on the far side of the seam: the meteor "misses" with no error, no log, and a world that looks entirely plausible afterwards. This is a silent-wrong-answer bug, the worst kind.
  - REJECT `r > min(world_width, world_height) / 2` at validation. Past the injectivity radius the disc wraps onto itself and membership is ambiguous; clamping would silently run a DIFFERENT experiment than the one the user asked for, which the parent bead's honesty rule forbids.
  - Rect: each axis wraps independently (origin + extent, modulo the world extent). Reject `w > world_width` or `h > world_height`.
  - Grid cells: `FoodGrid::get(x, y)` is bounds-checked and returns `None` out of range — so a wrapping region must WRAP THE INDEX before calling `get`, never lean on the `None` to mean "outside the region". Cell membership is decided on the CELL CENTRE against the toroidal metric; document it, because "does a half-covered cell count?" is exactly the ambiguity that makes two surfaces disagree about the same drought.
- Timed effects need world-held state: `active_effects: Vec<ActiveEffect { id, kind, region, params, expires_at_tick }>`, consulted by `stage_food_dynamics` via a multiplier lookup, iterated in stable insertion/id order (a `Vec` or a `BTreeMap`, NEVER a `HashMap`). Effects expire deterministically at `expires_at_tick` and restore EXACTLY — the parent bead calls this "embargo restores cleanly".
- `ActiveEffect` state MUST be included in checkpoints (bd-2z0.5.3) and in `characterization_digest_v0` (extend the encoder). An effect that evaporates on reload makes replay a lie: two worlds with different pending droughts would hash identically.
- RNG contract: no new RNG call sites inside `stage_interventions`. Cohort placement draws either from the existing spawn path (`stage_spawn_commit`) or from a seeded stream carried IN the command (preferred — bd-2z0.3.1). A `self.rng` draw inside the intervention stage shifts every subsequent draw that tick and makes an intervention globally chaotic far beyond its own semantics.

HARD REQUIREMENTS.
- Validation REJECTS, never clamps: non-finite params; `ticks == 0`; `r <= 0` or `r >` injectivity radius; `count == 0` or `count >` population headroom; unknown `TerrainKind`; unsupported cohort genome version. Typed, actionable errors (`RegionTooLarge { r, max }`, `PopulationCapExceeded { requested, headroom }`).
- ATOMIC: reject the WHOLE command or apply the WHOLE command. A partially-applied meteor is an experiment nobody can describe or reproduce.
- No panics anywhere on the apply path, including a region that matches nothing and a world with zero agents.

TESTS.
- Unit (THE SEAM TEST): world 200x200; `Meteor { Disc { cx: 0.0, cy: 0.0, r: 20.0 }, .. }`; agents at (5,5), (195,195), (100,100). Assert killed == {(5,5), (195,195)} and (100,100) survives. Repeat for the x-seam only, the y-seam only, and the CORNER (both seams at once) — the corner is where a fix that wraps only one axis dies quietly.
- Unit: rects wrapping in x only, y only, both, and a rect spanning the full width.
- Unit (DIFFERENTIAL, not hardcoded): drought suppresses regrowth in exactly the intended cells for exactly T ticks — assert against a CONTROL world stepped identically without the command, and assert that on tick T+1 the droughted world's growth matches the control's exactly. Same shape for embargo ("restores cleanly").
- Unit: `PaintTerrain` changes the tiles AND the derived fertility that food growth actually reads. A paint that only changes the render colour is a FAKE intervention; assert the food dynamics change.
- Unit (validation): `r > width/2` -> `RegionTooLarge`; `count` over cap -> `PopulationCapExceeded` AND population before == after (the no-partial-application test).
- Determinism: the same command at the same tick in two worlds from the same seed -> identical `characterization_digest_v0`.
- NEGATIVE (RNG contract — cheapest high-value test in the bead): apply an intervention whose region contains ZERO agents and ZERO cells (e.g. `Meteor { r: 0.5 }` in an empty corner). The resulting digest must be IDENTICAL to a world that received no command at all. This proves `stage_interventions` consumed no RNG and touched nothing it should not have — it catches the entire "one stray rng draw" class of bug for the price of one test.
- NEGATIVE: an effect still ACTIVE at a checkpoint round-trips through save/load with the same `expires_at_tick` and the same digest (catches un-serialized effect state).

LOGGING. Target `scriptbots::intervention`. info per applied command {tick, seq, kind, region, params, surface, agents_affected, cells_affected, effect_id, expires_at}. info per effect expiry {tick, effect_id, kind}. WARN when a command matched zero agents AND zero cells — a mis-parameterized meteor that hits nothing is visually indistinguishable from one that worked, and the log is the only place that difference can show up. error on rejection {tick, kind, error, params}. The parent's standard holds: an ecosystem crash caused by a mis-parameterized meteor must be obvious from the log alone.

comments.author: Jeff Emanuel
comments.text:
CORE INTERVENTION SET LANDED at e465805. Region (All | Disc, toroidal-exact), Intervention (Drought | Bloom | Meteor), ActiveEffect, WorldState::enqueue_intervention + active_effects(), and a new stage_interventions at the TOP of step().

Design decisions and the reasons behind them:
- QUEUED, not immediate. This bead's own brief was right: an intervention applied straight from a host thread lands on whichever tick the world mutex happened to be free, which is nondeterminism through the front door and makes a "replayable session" a lie.
- Applied at the TOP of the tick rather than the brief's suggested slot between food_dynamics and sense. Reason: a drought must scale THIS tick's regrowth (which happens in food_dynamics), and applying afterwards would delay it a tick while still claiming to have landed. Top-of-tick satisfies the brief's actual requirement - the effects are visible to every agent's senses on the tick they land, and no agent acts on a half-applied world.
- Droughts scale the per-cell GROWTH MULTIPLIER, so all three regrowth paths (SIMD chunk, SIMD remainder, scalar) honour them without any of them needing to know droughts exist.
- Interventions are REJECTED, never clamped: a clamp hands the caller a different experiment than the one they asked for and they never find out.

TWO BUGS MY OWN TESTS CAUGHT before this could ship:
