- ONE rail model, shared: the mapping from `EventKind` to colour/glyph/priority lives in ONE place (core or a shared app module), not twice. Two surfaces with two private copies of the colour table WILL drift, and the drift will be silent.
- Bounded work per frame: the rail renders at most the retained events (<= narrative_capacity). No allocation per frame in the hot path; reuse the buffer.

HARD REQUIREMENTS.
- READ-ONLY. Rendering the rail must not change the simulation, must not consume RNG, and must not perturb any digest. A UI that changes what it observes is not an instrument.
- NO PANIC on an empty narrative, a single event, a full ring, or a selection index that outlives a wrap (the ring can drop the very event the user has selected — handle it by clamping and saying so, never by indexing into a dropped slot).
- The rail must be honest about what it cannot do (see THE SEEK CONTRACT).

TESTS.
- TUI, buffer-inspecting (use the harness added in bd-2z0.1.4: `TerminalRenderer::render_frame_to_buffer` returns the real ratatui buffer): assert the rail actually PAINTS — one glyph per event, the selected event's text present in the detail pane, and the truncation marker present when the ring has wrapped and ABSENT when it has not. Asserting "the frame rendered without panicking" is exactly the ceremonial testing bd-2z0.1.4 removed; do not reintroduce it.
- Selection: left/right moves the selection and the detail pane follows; selection at either end does not wrap silently past the end (or if it wraps, that is deliberate and asserted).
- THE WRAP TEST: select an event, then push enough new events to force the ring to drop the selected one, then render. Assert no panic, assert the selection clamps to a live event, and assert the UI says the selected event aged out. A rail that indexes into a dropped slot is a crash in a long-running session — i.e. exactly the session a user cares about.
- Empty-narrative and single-event rails render without panicking and without claiming events exist.
- READ-ONLY PROOF: capture `characterization_digest_v0` before and after rendering the rail many times; assert it is unchanged. This is the test that proves the instrument does not disturb the experiment.
- E2E: run a seeded world until the narrative has produced >= 20 events, render both surfaces, and assert both rails show the SAME events in the SAME order with the SAME colours (the anti-drift test for the shared rail model).

LOGGING. Target `scriptbots::timeline`.
- info once when the rail is first shown: `{retained_events, dropped_events, capacity, oldest_tick, newest_tick}` — a reader must be able to tell from one line whether they are looking at a complete history or a tail.
- debug on selection: `{event_index, event_tick, event_kind}`.
- warn, once, when a selected event is dropped by the ring: `{event_tick, dropped_count}` — the user's attention was on something the system then discarded, and that is worth saying out loud.
- The core narrative module does NOT log (core has no tracing dependency and must not acquire one). The app/render layer logs, using the counters `RunNarrative` exposes.
acceptance_criteria: Rail renders in BOTH TUI and GPU lab from RunNarrative, read-only (digest unchanged across many renders, proven by test); one shared EventKind->colour/glyph model, not two copies; truncation is VISIBLE (an 'N earlier events dropped' marker whenever the ring has wrapped, absent when it has not); selection survives the selected event being dropped by the ring (clamps, says so, never panics); the seek control does not imply rewind before replay exists; TUI tests inspect the real ratatui buffer (not 'it rendered without panicking'); E2E asserts both surfaces show the same events in the same order with the same colours.

title: EventRecord schema, deterministic human_text, and the ONLINE in-memory event stream (no storage dependency)
description:
WHY THIS BEAD EXISTS (split out of bd-16g.2.2 on 2026-07-12). bd-16g.2.2 originally bundled two unrelated things: the EventRecord TYPE + templates (pure data, no I/O) and PERSISTENCE of those records (storage). The persistence half is blocked on bd-2z0.5.2 (the sequenced command/domain journal), which in turn sits in storage that is being actively rebuilt right now (bd-2z0.8.9.4 persistence worker, bd-2z0.8.9.4.2 recovery identity). Bundling them meant the narrated timeline — the single highest-leverage consumer of the detector kernel — was blocked behind a storage rebuild it does not actually need.

This bead delivers everything that needs no storage: the typed record, the deterministic prose, and a bounded in-memory stream produced live from the world's history ring. bd-16g.2.2 then becomes purely "write these records to the run DB" once the journal lands, and bd-16g.2.4 (timeline UI) can consume the in-memory stream TODAY rather than waiting.

SCOPE (in): EventRecord + EventKind; deterministic templated human_text; an online detector that runs the bd-16g.2.1 kernel over the world's TickSummary history at a fixed cadence; a bounded ring of recent events on WorldState with an accessor; dedupe so a sliding window cannot re-emit the same detection.
SCOPE (out): persistence (bd-16g.2.2), UI (bd-16g.2.4), speciation confirmation (bd-16g.3.3), LLM narration (bd-16g.1).

DESIGN.
- Placement: an inline `narrative` module in scriptbots-core/src/lib.rs, following the existing `map_sandbox` precedent. It may use TickSummary; detect.rs stays a PURE leaf (statistics only, no simulation types) — do not let the narrative layer leak back into it.
- EventRecord { tick, kind, severity (0..1), magnitude, window: (start,end), metric: &'static str, before, after, score, human_text: String }.
- EventKind: PopulationCrash, PopulationBoom, Extinction, EnergyCollapse, EnergyRecovery, CombatSurge, RegimeChange { from, to }. (SpeciationHint arrives with bd-16g.3; do not stub it here.)
- human_text is TEMPLATED and DETERMINISTIC — never LLM-authored. The stream must be diffable across runs/builds, and an LLM reading these events must not be reading its own prose fed back to it (a hallucination loop). Numbers use fixed precision so the text is byte-stable; no locale-dependent formatting.
- Cadence: run detectors every `narrative_interval` ticks (config, default 30) over the history ring rather than every tick. Justify the cadence in a comment: the ring is bounded (history_capacity, default 600) so a full pass is cheap, but a per-tick pass is pure waste at 60+ ticks/second.
- DEDUPE is load-bearing: as the window slides, the same underlying change re-detects every pass. Track the last emitted tick per (kind, metric) and only emit strictly newer detections. Without this the timeline becomes a stutter of duplicates and users stop reading it.
- RING is bounded (`narrative_capacity`, default 256) so a long run cannot grow memory without bound.
- Determinism: same seed -> byte-identical event list including human_text. No wall clock, no RNG, no map iteration order.

HARD REQUIREMENTS. Zero allocation on ticks where the cadence does not fire. No panics on an empty/short history. The detector must never observe or mutate simulation state — it reads TickSummary only, so it cannot perturb the run (assert this: enabling the narrative layer must leave characterization_digest_v0 byte-identical).

TESTS (required).
- Unit: template rendering is byte-stable for a fixed detection; number formatting is locale-independent.
- Unit: dedupe — a sustained change detected on many consecutive passes emits exactly ONE event.
- Unit: ring is bounded — 10k events on a 256-capacity ring keeps the newest 256, in order.
- Unit (observational neutrality): a seeded run with the narrative layer enabled produces the SAME characterization digest as with it disabled. This is the test that proves the storyteller is not changing the story.
- Unit: determinism — two runs of the same seed produce byte-identical event lists.
- E2E: a seeded headless run over a curated boom/crash seed emits the expected kinds within tolerance and NOTHING on a quiet equilibrium seed (the false-positive budget from bd-16g.2.3, applied to the online path).
LOGGING. Each emitted event logs once at info with tick, kind, severity, metric, before->after, and human_text — that log alone must let a reader reconstruct the run's story without opening the code.
close_reason: Landed: EventRecord/EventKind + RunNarrative online stream in an inline narrative module; deterministic templated prose; per-kind dedupe; bounded ring; cadence-driven. 6 tests incl. observational neutrality (digest identical with narration on/off) and seed determinism. clippy clean. bd-16g.2.4 (timeline UI) unblocked.

title: FTS5+BM25 narrative event search in scriptbots-storage (zero new deps)
description:
WHY. bd-16g.2.2/bd-16g.2.5 turn detector output into a persisted narrative stream of EventRecords with deterministic human_text. Searching that stream ("what happened around tick 12000", "show all extinctions after the drought") currently means SQL LIKE or eyeballing. FrankenSQLite ALREADY ships FTS5 with BM25 ranking, and our exact feature set compiles it in today: the facade `native` feature enables fsqlite-core/native which transitively enables the extensions (JSON/FTS5/R-tree) — verified against the pinned fsqlite workspace 2026-07-12. This is the cheapest capability unlock in the whole franken program: ZERO new dependencies, ZERO Cargo.lock changes, pure schema+query work inside scriptbots-storage.

OWNERSHIP BOUNDARY (read bd-16g.2.2 first). bd-16g.2.2 owns the RELATIONAL persistence of EventRecords and will decide between a new `run_events` table or typed-column extension of the existing `events` table — THIS bead does not name or create the relational table. This bead owns exactly two things: (1) the FTS5 virtual table indexing whatever relational home 2.2 decides (human_text + kind columns), created in a follow-on migration through the same MigrationRunner (crates/scriptbots-storage/src/lib.rs:215-221; V1 :57-166, V2 :168-192), and (2) the search/reader API. If 2.2 has not landed when this starts, do 2.2 first — it blocks this bead for exactly this reason.

DESIGN.
- DECISION (recorded here so nobody re-derives it): PLAIN CONTENT fts5 table, NOT external-content and NOT contentless. Post-materiality-floor event volume is tiny (~27 events/10k ticks after the 853->26.7 floor fix, commit 77d6a91), so duplicated text is negligible, and we avoid external-content trigger plumbing and contentless-mode delete restrictions. Revisit only if event volume grows 100x.
- fts rowid = the relational event row's PK so hits JOIN back for tick/severity/window/subject columns; tick-range filtering happens on the JOIN, not inside FTS.
- Writes happen in the SAME worker-thread transaction that inserts the relational event row (rides the PersistenceBatch path exactly as 2.2 specifies). Single-writer invariant is sacred: only the "scriptbots-storage-worker" thread (lib.rs:4425) ever touches the Connection (fsqlite Connection is !Send+!Sync; AGENTS.md storage contract).
- Reader API on StorageReader (alongside top_predators :1764, recent_metrics :1793): search_narrative(query, tick_range: Option<(u64,u64)>, limit) -> Vec<NarrativeHit{tick, kind, severity, human_text, rank}> ordered by bm25(); and narrative_around_tick(tick, window) -> Vec<NarrativeHit> (pure tick-window scan, no FTS, for "around tick N" without a query string).
- Hostile input: FTS5 query syntax errors must surface as a typed StorageError, never a panic; either sanitize to a phrase query by default or expose a raw-syntax flag.
- MAINTENANCE: INSERT INTO <fts>(<fts>) VALUES('optimize') only on clean shutdown or the maintenance cadence — NEVER in UI paths (UI paint reads only the lock-free ArcSwap<AnalyticsSnapshot>, lib.rs:1050-1128).

TESTS (all with tracing spans: parsed query, row counts, durations).
- Migration: fresh-create AND upgrade-from-prior-version paths; idempotence; schema_version assertions.
- Search: insert synthetic EventRecords across kinds/ticks; assert hit sets, bm25 ordering stability, tick-range filtering, limit semantics; unicode + quote + operator-injection queries return typed errors or sane phrase matches.
- Durability: events staged through the outbox and replayed by crash recovery (recover_outbox, lib.rs:2952) are searchable afterwards — extend the existing lease/crash-recovery test family.
- Consistency: FTS hit count == relational row count for every kind (index completeness identity, run after the durability test).
- Bench guard: search on a 10k-event DB completes < 10ms p95 (log the numbers; no hard CI gate yet).

ACCEPTANCE. Ranked, tick-filterable search over a seeded run DB; no SQL from UI paint paths; both migration paths proven; index-completeness identity green; `git diff Cargo.lock` empty for this bead.

title: Narrative search surfaces: control_cli, REST, MCP (+TUI rail hook)
description:
WHY. The FTS index (sibling bead: FTS5+BM25 narrative search) is only as valuable as its surfaces. Users and agents ask "what happened?" from four places: the terminal, REST, MCP tools, and the TUI timeline rail (bd-16g.2.4). All surfaces must answer identically.

SCOPE.
1. control_cli (crates/scriptbots-app/src/bin/control_cli.rs): `narrative search "<query>" [--from-tick N] [--to-tick N] [--limit K] [--json]` and `narrative around <tick> [--window W]`. Human output = aligned table with tick, kind, severity, text; --json = stable schema for scripting.
2. REST (crates/scriptbots-app/src/servers.rs, axum 0.8 + utoipa): GET /api/narrative/search?q=&from=&to=&limit= and GET /api/narrative/around/{tick}?window=. OpenAPI schemas, input validation (query length caps, limit caps), consistent error envelope with the existing endpoints (servers.rs:999-1020 route table).
3. MCP: narrative_search tool mirroring REST semantics. IMPLEMENTATION NOTE: bd-2z0.8.7.1 replaces mcp-protocol-sdk with fastmcp_rust — write this tool against a thin internal facade (one function both MCP layers call) so that migration does not rewrite it.
4. TUI: the bd-16g.2.4 scrubable event rail gains a search box that calls the same reader API. That bead owns the rail; this bead only guarantees the reader API is rail-friendly (cheap repeated queries, cursor pagination). Linked related, not blocking.

DESIGN CONSTRAINT. REST handlers must not block tokio workers on storage (bd-134 documents the same failure class against the world mutex): route DB-touching reads through spawn_blocking or the async-api lane once the sibling async-api bead lands; log p95 handler latency either way.

TESTS.
- Unit per surface: arg/query parsing, validation rejects (oversized query, negative ticks), JSON schema snapshot tests.
- E2E script scripts/e2e_narrative_search.sh with VERBOSE logging: (1) run headless sim with fixed seed until >=1 known event fires (pick a seed+scenario in the script and assert the exact expected human_text substring), (2) control_cli search finds it (table + json modes), (3) curl the REST endpoint — same hits, valid per OpenAPI, (4) MCP tool call — same hits, (5) dump all transcripts to the CI artifact dir. Any mismatch across surfaces = failure.
ACCEPTANCE. Identical hits across all three programmatic surfaces for identical queries; e2e green in CI with uploaded logs; OpenAPI docs render.

title: Live phylogeny: ancestry DAG, speciation detection, and extinction/radiation timeline
description:
THE IDEA. Make evolution VISIBLE. Build the ancestry DAG from birth/death records, cluster living agents into species by phenotype+genome distance, and render a living phylogenetic tree: branches thicken with population, fork on speciation, and terminate on extinction — with a time axis you can scrub. Click a branch to inspect its founder, its descendants, and the mutations that separated it from its sibling clade.

WHY IT RANKS #3. ScriptBots is an EVOLUTION simulator whose evolution is currently invisible: you watch dots move and take it on faith that lineages are diverging. The phylogenetic tree is the canonical, instantly-legible artifact of the entire field, and this project has none. It is also the payoff for data the sim ALREADY records (AgentRuntime.lineage = [parent_a, parent_b], BirthRecord{parent_a, parent_b, generation, is_hybrid, brain_key}, DeathRecord{cause, age}) — the graph is sitting in the run DB unexploited. It complements rather than duplicates bd-2z0.11.1 (which computes lineage FITNESS numbers but neither segments species nor visualizes anything).

DESIGN.
- Ancestry store: an append-only edge list (child_uid, parent_a_uid, parent_b_uid, birth_tick, brain_kind, is_hybrid) keyed on the stable AgentUid from bd-2z0.3.1 — slotmap keys are REUSED after death and are therefore unusable for ancestry; this dependency is hard, not cosmetic.
- Species segmentation: cluster living agents in the phenotype space defined by bd-2z0.11.2 (+ optional genome distance from bd-2z0.3.2) at a fixed cadence; a species is a labeled cluster with a founder set. Speciation = a cluster splits and the split persists for K consecutive samples AND the two sub-clusters are reproductively separated in practice (measure realized cross-cluster mating rate — the sim already gates sexual reproduction on same brain-kind; genuine allopatric/phenotypic separation is the interesting case, especially with bd-16g.5 islands).
- Species get stable auto-generated names (deterministic from founder UID + tick, e.g. "Swiftgiver-14") so humans and the LLM can talk about them across a run.
- Tree layout must be deterministic and incremental (recomputing a 100k-node layout every frame is a non-starter): maintain the layout, extend it as births arrive, and cap rendered detail with LOD (collapse extinct/minor clades until zoomed).
- Pruning policy: keep the full edge list in the DB (cheap, append-only), but the LIVE in-memory tree keeps ancestors of living agents + a configurable window of extinct clades. Document the memory bound.

ACCEPTANCE. A 50k-tick run renders a tree whose leaves match the living population exactly; speciation events cross-validate against bd-16g.2's bimodality hints (each confirmed speciation has a preceding hint; each hint is either confirmed or explicitly rejected); the tree is scrubable and stays under a documented memory bound at 10k agents; and the same seed produces a byte-identical species/event list.

TESTS + LOGGING (required).
- Unit: ancestry DAG construction from a synthetic birth/death log (including hybrid two-parent births and reused slot keys — assert the stable-UID path prevents mis-parenting; a test that PROVES the slotmap-key approach would corrupt the tree is worth writing once as documentation).
- Unit: clustering determinism (same input -> same labels, same names) and stability (a single agent's death must not relabel unrelated species).
- Unit: extinction/radiation event emission with hand-built fixtures.
- E2E: seeded 50k-tick headless run -> persist ancestry -> rebuild the tree offline from the DB alone -> assert it equals the in-memory tree (this proves the run DB is genuinely sufficient for offline science, which is the whole point of the storage layer).
- Logging: per-sample species table (id, name, size, founder, mean phenotype) at debug; speciation/extinction events at info with founder UIDs; log the layout node/edge count and rebuild timing so the tree cannot silently become a hot path.

title: Ancestry store: stable-UID edge list, append-only persistence, offline rebuild
description:
SCOPE. The ancestry substrate for all of bd-16g.3: (a) a stable-UID-keyed ancestry graph type in scriptbots-core, (b) ingestion from BirthRecord/DeathRecord, (c) append-only persistence in scriptbots-storage, (d) an offline rebuild that reconstructs the identical graph from the run DB alone, (e) a documented, enforced memory bound for the live in-memory graph. OUT OF SCOPE: species clustering (bd-16g.3.2), event emission (bd-16g.3.3), layout (bd-16g.3.4), any rendering (bd-16g.3.5), and any phenotype math (bd-2z0.11.2 owns phenotype features).

WHY. bd-16g.3 makes evolution visible; nothing else in the idea can be built on sand. The sim ALREADY records everything the DAG needs — AgentRuntime.lineage ([Option<AgentId>; 2], crates/scriptbots-core/src/lib.rs:925), BirthRecord{parent_a, parent_b, generation, is_hybrid, brain_key} (lib.rs:1553), DeathRecord{cause, age} (lib.rs:1568) — and persists births/deaths to FrankenSQLite (crates/scriptbots-storage/src/lib.rs:132-166). The graph is sitting in the run DB unexploited. This bead exploits it, once, correctly, so that .2/.3/.4/.5 and bd-16g.13 (genome diff) all consume ONE ancestry store instead of three private ones.

THE FAILURE MODE THIS BEAD EXISTS TO PREVENT (read this before writing code). AgentId is a slotmap key: a (version, slot) pair. Slots are REUSED after death. Three consequences, each of which silently corrupts a phylogeny:
  1. Dead-parent lookup returns nothing. runtime.get(parent_id) is None once the parent dies — an ancestry builder that resolves parents lazily from the live world simply LOSES the edge, and every long lineage becomes a forest of orphan roots.
  2. Handles are not stable across identity boundaries. Storage writes AgentId::data().as_ffi() (crates/scriptbots-storage/src/lib.rs:5321, :5350) — a per-process SlotMap handle, not a logical identity. It does not survive a checkpoint restore, a world rebuild, an island migration (bd-16g.5), or a second run. Any offline join on it can fuse two different agents onto one node. The project already ADMITS this in its own honesty record: CharacterizationLimitationsV0.agent_identity = \"AgentId::data().as_ffi(), not stable AgentUid\" (crates/scriptbots-app/src/lib.rs:195).
  3. The control API round-trips raw ffi integers from untrusted clients (KeyData::from_ffi(raw_id), crates/scriptbots-app/src/control.rs:1115) — a stale int names whatever agent now occupies that slot.
Therefore bd-2z0.3.1 (stable AgentUid) is a HARD dependency, not a cosmetic one. Do not start this bead by keying the graph on AgentId \"for now\" and swapping later; the swap will be a rewrite and the intermediate artifacts will be wrong in a way nobody notices. NOTE: bd-16g.3.1 currently has no beads dependency edge on bd-2z0.3.1 — wire it.

DESIGN.
- Home: a new `ancestry` module inside scriptbots-core (same reasoning as bd-16g.2.1: prefer a module, extract a crate only if a second consumer appears; AGENTS.md sets a very high bar for new files).
- Types (deterministic containers only — BTreeMap/Vec, never HashMap; iteration order is part of the contract):
    pub struct AncestryEdge { pub child: AgentUid, pub parents: [Option<AgentUid>; 2], pub birth_tick: Tick, pub generation: Generation, pub brain_key: Option<u64>, pub is_hybrid: bool }
    pub struct AncestryNode { pub uid: AgentUid, pub birth_tick: Tick, pub death_tick: Option<Tick>, pub death_cause: Option<DeathCause>, pub parents: [Option<AgentUid>; 2], pub children: Vec<AgentUid> }
    pub struct AncestryGraph { nodes: BTreeMap<AgentUid, AncestryNode>, roots: Vec<AgentUid>, living: usize, retained_extinct: usize }
- API:
    pub fn apply_birth(&mut self, record: &BirthRecord) -> Result<(), AncestryError>
    pub fn apply_death(&mut self, record: &DeathRecord) -> Result<(), AncestryError>
    pub fn parents_of(&self, uid: AgentUid) -> [Option<AgentUid>; 2]
    pub fn lineage_path(&self, uid: AgentUid, max_depth: usize) -> Vec<AgentUid>   // bounded, never unbounded recursion
    pub fn prune(&mut self, policy: PrunePolicy) -> PruneReport
    pub fn canonical_digest(&self) -> u64   // stable hash of the sorted node/edge set; the offline-rebuild oracle
- BirthRecord/DeathRecord must gain uid fields (agent_uid, parent_a_uid, parent_b_uid) alongside the existing AgentId fields. AgentRuntime.lineage keeps [Option<AgentId>; 2] for in-tick use; the RECORD is what carries logical identity out of the tick.
- Persistence: extend the existing schema with a SCRIPTBOTS_SCHEMA_V3 block (storage already versions schemas as V1/V2 constants, crates/scriptbots-storage/src/lib.rs:57,169) adding agent_uid/parent_a_uid/parent_b_uid to `births` and agent_uid to `deaths`, with UNIQUE(agent_uid) on births. The birth row IS the edge — do not duplicate it into a second table unless a second parent-set source ever appears. Add `Storage::load_ancestry_edges() -> Result<Vec<AncestryEdge>>` returning rows ordered by (birth_tick, child_uid), and the matching death loader.
- MUST NOT COUPLE TO: fsqlite or any storage type inside core (core ingests records, it does not read a DB); the detector kernel; any UI crate; layout. AncestryGraph is a leaf data structure with no I/O.
- PrunePolicy: keep all ancestors of living agents, plus extinct clades within a configurable tick window / node budget. Pruned parents become a `PrunedAncestor` sentinel edge — NEVER a dangling parent reference, and never a panic in a consumer.

HARD REQUIREMENTS.
- Determinism: same record sequence -> same graph -> same canonical_digest, bit-for-bit, on every platform and every feature combination. No HashMap iteration, no wall clock, no RNG.
- No panic on any malformed log: unknown parent uid, duplicate child uid, out-of-order births, a death for an unknown uid, a birth whose tick precedes its parent's birth — each returns a typed AncestryError, never an unwrap/expect/index panic.
- DAG invariants, checked on insert: no cycles; child.birth_tick > parent.birth_tick for every present parent; parents are either present in the graph, a PrunedAncestor, or explicitly None (seeded/respawned agents are legitimate roots — the world respawns agents at the population floor and those are NOT descendants of anything).
- apply_birth/apply_death are O(1) amortized. Memory bound is DOCUMENTED and ASSERTED: live nodes = O(ancestors_of_living + retained_extinct); state the bytes/node and the budget at 10k living agents in the module doc and assert it in a test.
- clippy pedantic + nursery clean; no unsafe.

TESTS.
- Table-driven graph construction from a synthetic birth/death log covering: asexual birth (one parent), sexual birth (two parents), hybrid birth (is_hybrid), seeded root (no parents), floor-respawn root, and a full three-generation chain.
- THE SLOT-REUSE TEST (write it once, keep it forever as executable documentation): build a log where an agent dies and its slot is reused by an unrelated agent. Build the graph twice — once keyed on AgentUid, once on a deliberate AgentId-keyed foil constructed inside the test — and assert the UID graph is correct while the foil MIS-PARENTS. A test that only proves the happy path does not protect anyone from the thing that actually went wrong.
- Negative tests, each asserting a typed error and no panic: cycle (A parent of B parent of A), duplicate child uid, unknown parent uid, out-of-order tick, death for an unknown uid, death recorded twice.
- Prune: after pruning, every remaining node's parents resolve to a present node or PrunedAncestor; no dangling uid; PruneReport counts match the node delta; the ancestors of living agents are never pruned.
- Memory bound: construct 100k births, assert node count and heap estimate stay within the documented bound after prune.
- E2E (the point of the whole bead): seeded 50k-tick headless run -> persist -> reopen the DB -> load_ancestry_edges() -> rebuild the graph offline -> assert canonical_digest() equals the in-memory graph's. This proves the run DB is genuinely sufficient for offline science, which is the entire justification for the storage layer.

LOGGING. scriptbots-core has NO tracing dependency and must not acquire one (see its Cargo.toml) — the graph is a pure leaf and returns typed reports; the app/storage layer does the logging, exactly as bd-16g.2.1 requires of the detector kernel.
- info at ancestry store open/rebuild: edge count, node count, tick range, uid range, canonical_digest, rebuild duration.
- info per prune: nodes dropped, nodes retained, living, estimated bytes, policy in effect.
- warn for EVERY rejected record: the error variant, the child uid, the offending parent uid, the tick. A rejected birth must be fully diagnosable from the log line alone, without re-running the sim.
- debug per persisted batch: births/deaths admitted, running edge total.
close_reason: Complete, and verified by the STRONGEST form of its acceptance criterion. A graph rebuilt from nothing but the persisted origin+death rows is now BIT-IDENTICAL to the graph the live run held: crates/scriptbots-storage/tests/ancestry_offline_rebuild.rs now asserts rebuilt.canonical_digest() == live_graph.canonical_digest() (and equal node counts), with NO agents-table founder inference and no test-only repair path. 3/3 green (run on APFS; exFAT breaks storage open, see bd-15c8). The work: (a) AncestryGraph in scriptbots-core, keyed on stable AgentUid, pure leaf, cycle/dangling-parent checked on insert (b4d7b37); (b) ingestion from BirthRecord/DeathRecord; (c) persistence where the birth row IS the edge (69ab3fd) — which UNCOVERED that founders and population-floor injections emitted no origin row, so the rebuild was strictly larger than the record stream. That gap was the bead's blocker (bd-3m5l), now closed by aa83efb 'make ancestry lifecycle scientifically exact', which made every agent emit an origin row and upgraded this test from 'assert the gap' to 'assert equality'. This is a genuinely collaborative close: I built the substrate and the test that found the defect; whoever did bd-3m5l closed the defect. Nothing ceremonial — the identity is proven, not asserted.

comments.author: Jeff Emanuel
comments.text:
PARTS 1 AND 2 LANDED (b4d7b37 core substrate; 69ab3fd storage rebuild). Bead stays OPEN — blocked on bd-3m5l, the defect this work uncovered.

DONE:
- (a) AncestryGraph in scriptbots-core, keyed on AgentUid. Pure leaf: no I/O, no clock, no RNG, no storage types, no tracing. BTreeMap/Vec only, so canonical_digest() is stable across platforms and feature sets.
- (b) Ingestion from BirthRecord/DeathRecord. Invariants CHECKED ON INSERT: no cycles (structurally — a child's birth tick must strictly exceed every parent's, so an ancestor is always strictly older and no chain can return to its start), no dangling parents (a pruned ancestor is TOMBSTONED as a sentinel), parentless agents are legitimate ROOTS. Every malformed row is a typed AncestryError; nothing panics; lineage walks are depth-bounded and refuse to revisit a node.
- (c) Persistence: already sufficient. Codex's SCHEMA_V3 (create_stable_agent_uid_schema) put agent_uid + parent_a + parent_b + generation + brain_key + is_hybrid on . THE BIRTH ROW IS THE EDGE, exactly as the brief predicted — no second table needed.
- (d) Offline rebuild: StorageReader::load_ancestry_births/_deaths/_founders + rebuild_ancestry(), ordered by (tick, agent_uid) so a parent always precedes its child and the digest is reproducible.
- (e) Memory bound documented (~80 bytes/node, ~8 MB at 100k nodes) and ASSERTED by test.
- THE SLOT-REUSE TEST, kept forever as executable documentation: an agent dies, its slot is reused by a stranger, and the same log is built twice — once keyed on AgentUid, once on a deliberate slot-handle foil. The foil FUSES the stranger onto the dead agent's node and inherits its children. The UID graph does not.

WHAT THE E2E FOUND — and why this bead is not closed: the birth-record stream is INCOMPLETE. Founders and population-floor injections emit no BirthRecord at all (bd-3m5l). Measured: DB rebuild 31 agents, record stream 25. I did NOT paper over it by making the two graphs match; the E2E asserts the superset relationship, asserts internal soundness and rebuild determinism, and ASSERTS THE GAP STILL EXISTS with a message explaining that the assertion failing means the defect is fixed.

REMAINING SCOPE: once bd-3m5l lands, delete load_ancestry_founders(), and change the E2E from asserting the gap to asserting canonical_digest equality between the live and rebuilt graphs. That is the assertion the brief actually asks for, and it becomes TRUE rather than arranged.

title: Species segmentation: phenotype clustering, deterministic labels, stable auto-names
description:
SCOPE. Segment the LIVING population into species: cluster agents in the phenotype space at a fixed cadence, assign deterministic and STABLE labels across samples, and mint stable human-readable auto-names. Deliverable is a SpeciesTable: a deterministic, serializable snapshot of (species id, name, founder set, member uids, centroid, spread) at a tick. OUT OF SCOPE: the phenotype feature definition itself (bd-2z0.11.2 owns it — CONSUME it, do not invent an eighth private feature vector; the epic explicitly forbids three children each inventing their own clustering), event emission (bd-16g.3.3), layout (bd-16g.3.4), UI (bd-16g.3.5).

WHY. A phylogenetic tree without species is just a birth log. Segmentation is what turns the ancestry DAG from bd-16g.3.1 into something a human — or the bd-16g.1 LLM assistant — can TALK about: "Swiftgiver-14 split off around tick 31k and took over the north." Stable ids and stable names are what make cross-tick, cross-session, cross-tool conversation possible at all. bd-16g.3.3 (events), bd-16g.6 (MAP-Elites), bd-16g.7 (comms lab) and bd-16g.12 (tournament) all key off this table.

DESIGN.
- Home: the `ancestry`/`phylo` module family in scriptbots-core (see bd-16g.3.1). Pure function; no I/O, no UI, no storage types.
- Signature:
    pub fn segment_species(samples: &[(AgentUid, PhenotypeVector)], prev: &SpeciesTable, params: &SpeciesParams) -> SpeciesTable
  Pure and total: given the same (samples, prev, params) it returns the same table, always.
- Types:
    pub struct SpeciesId(u64);                        // monotone counter, NEVER reused, even after extinction
    pub struct Species { pub id: SpeciesId, pub name: SpeciesName, pub founders: Vec<AgentUid>, pub members: Vec<AgentUid>, pub centroid: PhenotypeVector, pub spread: f32, pub first_tick: Tick, pub last_seen_tick: Tick }
    pub struct SpeciesTable { pub tick: Tick, pub species: Vec<Species>, pub next_id: SpeciesId }   // Vec sorted by SpeciesId; never a HashMap
- Clustering: prefer a deterministic threshold-based agglomerative / leader clustering over k-means, so that k is not a magic number that quietly caps the number of discoverable species. If k-means is chosen anyway, it must be seeded from `prev`'s centroids (not randomly), run a FIXED iteration count, and break ties by AgentUid ordering. Accumulate centroid sums in AgentUid order with documented summation — float addition is not associative and a reordered sum is a different centroid.
- FEATURE SCALING IS THE TRAP. Standardize each phenotype dimension against FIXED, config-declared ranges (declared in SpeciesParams and versioned), NOT against per-sample z-scores. With per-sample scaling, the same population clusters differently depending on who happens to be alive that tick, and species will appear and vanish for no biological reason. Write this down in the module doc; it is the single most likely way this bead ships broken.
- LABEL STABILITY IS THE OTHER TRAP. Map new clusters to previous species by MAXIMUM MEMBER-UID OVERLAP (Jaccard over member uid sets), never by centroid index or cluster ordinal. A new SpeciesId is minted only when a cluster matches no previous species above `params.continuity_threshold`. One agent dying must not renumber anything.
- Naming: SpeciesName is derived deterministically from (founder_uid, first_tick) — a fixed, in-repo wordlist indexed by a fixed hash (FNV-1a over the uid bytes and tick; no DefaultHasher, whose output is not stable across releases), producing e.g. "Swiftgiver-14". Names are assigned ONCE and never change. No locale, no wall clock, no RNG.
- Cadence: segmentation runs off the hot path at a configured interval (default e.g. every 500 ticks). It is NOT part of step()'s inner loop.
- MUST NOT COUPLE TO: the detector kernel (bd-16g.2.1 — bimodality is a HINT consumed in bd-16g.3.3, not an input here), tree layout, any frontend, storage.

HARD REQUIREMENTS.
- Determinism: byte-identical SpeciesTable for identical inputs, including ids and names. ORDER INVARIANCE: shuffling the input `samples` slice must not change the output — assert it (this catches accidental order dependence, which is the quiet killer of reproducibility here).
- No panic: empty population, a single agent, all-identical phenotypes, or a non-finite phenotype component -> typed error or an explicitly empty/singleton table; never a NaN centroid propagated into a name or a distance.
- Complexity: O(n*k) per sample with bounded allocation; document the cost at 10k agents and assert it stays under a stated budget. Segmentation must never make step() slower on ticks when it does not run.
- clippy pedantic + nursery clean.

TESTS (table-driven).
- Ground-truth fixtures: two well-separated phenotype Gaussians -> exactly 2 species. ONE blob of pure noise -> exactly 1 species (the "do not invent species from noise" test — this is the false-positive budget, and it matters as much as detection). A blob that separates gradually over samples -> species count goes 1 -> 2 exactly at the documented threshold and NOT before.
- LABEL STABILITY NEGATIVE TEST: segment; kill one member of species A; resegment -> species B's id AND name are unchanged, and A keeps its id. Then do the same with the members permuted. A centroid-index labeling scheme fails this; that is the point.
- Determinism: same input twice -> identical table (compare a canonical digest). Shuffled input order -> identical table.
- Naming: same (founder_uid, first_tick) -> same name across processes and builds; two different founders -> different names; assert the wordlist hash is stable by pinning a few expected names as golden values.
- Scaling regression: the same two-cluster fixture, once with a third far-outlier agent added -> the two clusters keep their ids and their members (proves fixed-range scaling; per-sample z-scoring would move every point and relabel everything).
- Degenerate: empty samples, single sample, all-identical phenotypes, NaN component -> typed error / empty table, never a panic.

LOGGING. Core stays log-free (scriptbots-core has no tracing dependency and must not gain one); segment_species returns a SpeciesTable plus a SegmentReport, and the caller logs.
- debug, per sample: the full species table — id, name, size, founder uid, centroid (all dims), within-cluster spread — plus the params digest and the scaling ranges in effect. "Why did it split" must be answerable from this line alone.
- info whenever a new SpeciesId is minted: id, name, founder uid, size, distance to the nearest existing centroid, and the continuity_threshold it failed to meet.
- info whenever a species is lost from the table: id, name, last size, last seen tick (bd-16g.3.3 turns this into an Extinction event; the LOG must exist even before that bead lands).
- debug: segmentation duration and allocation count, so this can never silently become a hot path.

title: Speciation/extinction/radiation event emission cross-validated against detector hints
description:
SCOPE. Turn the species table (bd-16g.3.2) plus the ancestry graph (bd-16g.3.1) into an append-only, tick-indexed stream of typed phylogeny events — Speciation, Extinction, Radiation — and CROSS-VALIDATE every one of them against the bimodality/change-point hints produced by the detector kernel (bd-16g.2.1). Every hint gets a verdict; every event carries its evidence. OUT OF SCOPE: the detector primitives themselves (bd-16g.2.1 owns them — call them, do not reimplement them), clustering (bd-16g.3.2), layout (bd-16g.3.4), rendering (bd-16g.3.5).

WHY. This is where the phylogeny either becomes science or becomes a lie. Clustering ALWAYS produces clusters; a bimodal histogram ALWAYS looks like speciation to an enthusiastic renderer. bd-16g.2.1 already writes the honesty rule for its bimodality primitive: "This is a HINT for speciation; bd-16g.3.3 confirms or rejects it with ancestry. Do not claim speciation from bimodality alone." This bead IS that confirmation step. Without it, bd-16g.3 ships a beautiful tree that announces speciation events that never happened, and the bd-16g.1 LLM assistant will faithfully narrate the fiction.

DESIGN.
- Home: the `phylo` module family in scriptbots-core, alongside .1/.2. Pure function of (species table history, ancestry graph, birth records, detector hints) -> events. No I/O, no UI, no RNG, no clock.
- Types:
    pub enum PhyloEvent {
      Speciation { parent: SpeciesId, children: [SpeciesId; 2], founders: Vec<AgentUid>, separation: SeparationKind, cross_mating_rate: f32, persisted_samples: u32, hint: Option<HintId>, tick: Tick },
      Extinction { species: SpeciesId, last_member: AgentUid, peak_size: usize, cause_histogram: BTreeMap<DeathCause, u32>, tick: Tick },
      Radiation { species: SpeciesId, from_size: usize, to_size: usize, window: TickRange, score: f32, hint: Option<HintId>, tick: Tick },
    }
    pub enum SeparationKind { Phenotypic, BrainKindGated, Allopatric, Mixed }
    pub enum HintVerdict { Confirmed(EventId), Rejected { reason: RejectReason, evidence: HintEvidence } }
    pub enum RejectReason { Transient, Interbreeding, BelowMinSize, NoAncestralSupport, BrainKindArtifact }
- CONFIRMATION RULE for Speciation (all must hold, and each is a separate, logged predicate):
    (a) PERSISTENCE — a cluster split holds for K consecutive samples (K configurable, default documented);
    (b) REPRODUCTIVE SEPARATION — realized cross-cluster mating rate over the window is below `params.max_cross_mating`. Compute it from BirthRecords: for each two-parent birth, look up BOTH parents' species via the ancestry graph. Not a model, not an assumption: the OBSERVED rate.
    (c) MIN SIZE — both sub-clusters have >= params.min_species_size members.
- THE ARTIFACT YOU WILL OTHERWISE "DISCOVER": the sim already gates sexual reproduction on brain kind — spawn_crossover_agent computes `kind_match = parent_kind.is_some() && parent_kind == partner_kind` (crates/scriptbots-core/src/lib.rs:7113-7114) and only crosses over same-family brains. Two clusters that never interbreed BECAUSE they carry different brain kinds are a mechanical consequence of the mating gate, not evolution. Classify these as SeparationKind::BrainKindGated and report them as such; the interesting cases (Phenotypic, Allopatric — the latter becoming real with bd-16g.5 islands) must be distinguishable in the event, in the log, and in the UI. Reporting a brain-kind partition as a speciation event is the headline failure mode of this bead.
- Also note `reproduction_partner_chance` defaults to 0.15 (lib.rs:2848) — most births are asexual. A cross-mating rate computed over a window with almost no two-parent births is not evidence of separation; require a minimum number of two-parent births in the window, else return RejectReason::NoAncestralSupport rather than "confirming" separation from an empty denominator. Dividing by a near-zero denominator and calling it isolation is the second failure mode.
- Extinction: threshold_crossings (bd-16g.2.1) to zero on the species-size series, CONFIRMED against the ancestry graph (zero living members). A species with zero clustered members but living agents is a clustering bug, not an extinction — emit a warn, not an event.
- Radiation: change_points_cusum (bd-16g.2.1) on the species-size series, direction=up, magnitude >= threshold, over a documented window.
- HINT RECONCILIATION: every hint from bd-16g.2.1 must terminate in a HintVerdict — Confirmed or Rejected with a reason. An unresolved hint is a BUG and must fail the E2E assertion. Conversely, a Speciation with no preceding hint is ALLOWED but is tagged `hint: None` and counted as `events_unhinted` — allowed, but never invisible.
- MUST NOT COUPLE TO: layout, any frontend, storage internals. Events are values; persistence rides the existing event journal (bd-2z0.5.2).

HARD REQUIREMENTS.
- Determinism: events are emitted in a total order — sorted by (tick, kind discriminant, species id) — and are byte-identical for the same seed. No HashMap iteration (BTreeMap for the cause histogram). No wall clock, no RNG, no float-order dependence in the rate computations.
- Append-only: an event is never retracted or mutated. A later disconfirmation is a NEW event/verdict record, never an edit — this is what makes the stream replayable and what keeps the timeline (bd-16g.2.4) honest.
- No panic: empty species history, a single sample, a species that appears and vanishes within one sample, zero two-parent births in the window, division by zero -> typed errors / explicit Rejected reasons.
- O(samples * species) with bounded memory; runs at the segmentation cadence, never in step().

TESTS (table-driven, hand-built fixtures — one row per failure mode).
- (a) Clean split persisting K samples with zero cross-mating -> exactly one Speciation, hint Confirmed, separation=Phenotypic.
- (b) Split that reverts after K-1 samples -> NO event, hint Rejected{Transient}.
- (c) Split with high observed cross-cluster mating -> NO event, hint Rejected{Interbreeding}. THIS IS THE TEST THAT STOPS THE FEATURE FROM LYING; write it first.
- (d) Split entirely explained by brain-kind gating -> event emitted with separation=BrainKindGated, and an assertion that it is NOT reported as Phenotypic.
- (e) Window containing zero two-parent births -> Rejected{NoAncestralSupport}, not Confirmed (the empty-denominator test).
- (f) Sub-cluster below min_size -> Rejected{BelowMinSize}.
- (g) Species size -> 0 -> exactly ONE Extinction, and no further events ever emitted for that SpeciesId (idempotence of extinction).
- (h) Species size doubling inside the window -> one Radiation with the correct from/to and score.
- (i) Clustering drops a species that still has living members -> no Extinction, a warn, and a typed anomaly counter.
- Determinism: the same seeded fixture twice -> byte-identical event list and verdict list.
- E2E: seeded 50k-tick headless run -> assert (1) every emitted hint has exactly one verdict, (2) every Speciation's evidence payload can be RECONSTRUCTED from the run DB alone (ancestry edges + species samples + birth records), and (3) a second run at the same seed produces a byte-identical event list. Assert the false-positive budget on a deliberately QUIET run (stable single-species world): ZERO speciation events.

LOGGING. Core returns values; the app logs them (scriptbots-core has no tracing dependency and must not gain one).
- info per emitted event, with the COMPLETE evidence inline: event kind, tick, species ids AND names, founder uids, persisted_samples/K, observed cross_mating_rate and its numerator/denominator, min-size check, separation kind, hint id and score. A reader must be able to answer "why did it fire?" from this one line without opening the source — the same rule bd-16g.2.1 imposes on its evidence payload.
- info per Rejected hint: hint id, reason code, and the specific predicate that failed with its numbers. "Why did it NOT fire" must be equally answerable.
- debug per sample: the running confirmation counters per candidate split (samples held, current cross-mating rate, sizes).
- warn on anomalies: species with zero clustered members but living agents; a birth whose parents resolve to different species during a confirmed-isolated window.
- Counters at info on run end: events_emitted (by kind), hints_confirmed, hints_rejected (by reason), events_unhinted.

title: Incremental tree layout with LOD and documented memory bound
description:
SCOPE. The pure geometry layer: turn the ancestry graph (bd-16g.3.1) and species table (bd-16g.3.2) into 2D coordinates, INCREMENTALLY (extend on birth/speciation, never relayout from scratch every frame), with level-of-detail collapse and a DOCUMENTED, ASSERTED memory bound. Deliverable is a TreeLayout plus an LOD query. OUT OF SCOPE: all drawing (bd-16g.3.5 owns gpui/ratatui), clustering, event emission, ancestry storage.

WHY. bd-16g.3 says it plainly: "recomputing a 100k-node layout every frame is a non-starter." A phylogeny view that recomputes its layout every frame is not a feature, it is a framerate regression with a picture on it — and, worse, the moment the layout becomes expensive somebody will "fix" it by sampling or by caching non-deterministically, and the tree will stop being a function of the run. Layout is separated into its own bead precisely so it can be tested headlessly, without a GPU, against exact coordinates.

DESIGN.
- Home: the `phylo` module family in scriptbots-core (pure math, no UI deps). Coordinates are plain f32. This module MUST NOT reference gpui, bevy, ratatui, wgpu, or wasm-bindgen types — the frontends own drawing, and a layout that knows about a renderer cannot be tested headlessly or reused by the other three frontends.
- Two scales, one type:
    * DEFAULT SCALE = the SPECIES tree — O(#species) nodes, not O(#agents). This is what is laid out continuously.
    * AGENT SCALE = a subtree of the ancestry DAG, materialized ON DEMAND for a zoomed clade only: `fn expand(&mut self, root: SpeciesId | AgentUid, depth_budget: usize, node_budget: usize) -> ExpandReport`. Never materialize the agent-level tree for the whole run.
- Types:
    pub struct LayoutNode { pub key: PhyloKey /* SpeciesId | AgentUid */, pub parent: Option<LayoutIdx>, pub x: f32 /* tick-derived */, pub y: f32, pub thickness: f32 /* population */, pub first_tick: Tick, pub last_tick: Option<Tick>, pub collapsed: bool, pub peak_population: u32 }
    pub struct TreeLayout { nodes: Vec<LayoutNode>, index: BTreeMap<PhyloKey, LayoutIdx>, bounds: Rect, budget: LayoutBudget }
    pub struct LayoutDelta { pub added: Vec<LayoutIdx>, pub moved: Vec<LayoutIdx>, pub full_relayout: bool }
- API:
    pub fn extend(&mut self, delta: &PhyloDelta) -> LayoutDelta            // incremental; O(new nodes + affected siblings)
    pub fn lod(&self, viewport: TickRange, y: Range<f32>, budget: usize) -> impl Iterator<Item = &LayoutNode>   // at most `budget` nodes
    pub fn hit_test(&self, x: f32, y: f32, tol: f32) -> Option<PhyloKey>   // used by bd-16g.3.5; lives here so it is testable without a GPU
- Geometry: x is the TICK axis (so scrubbing is a viewport translation, not a relayout). y is a deterministic tidy-tree assignment (Reingold-Tilford-style ordering) with leaves ordered by founder AgentUid — so the same run always draws the same shape, and two people looking at the same seed see the same picture.
- LOD: rank clades by (peak_population, duration) with a tie-break on founder uid, collapse the tail until <= budget nodes remain. The collapse decision must be a pure function of the layout and the budget — NEVER of iteration order, hover state, or frame timing.
- Pruning interaction: a node whose parent was pruned by bd-16g.3.1's PrunePolicy reattaches to an explicit `PrunedAncestor` sentinel node. Never a dangling parent index; never a panic; never a silent reroot to the wrong ancestor.

HARD REQUIREMENTS.
- Determinism: the same delta sequence produces bitwise-identical coordinates. No HashMap iteration, no wall clock, no RNG, no float accumulation whose order depends on container iteration.
- INCREMENTAL == FROM-SCRATCH. This is the invariant the whole bead rests on and it must be asserted, not assumed.
- No panic on: empty tree, single node, a node whose parent was pruned, a viewport entirely outside the tick range, budget = 0, or scrubbing past the last tick.
- Perf: extend() is O(new + affected siblings), NOT O(total). A full relayout is a FALLBACK, never the steady state, and every occurrence is logged at warn with a reason.
- Memory: state the bytes/node in the module doc and assert the bound in a test — at 10k living agents and the corresponding species tree, TreeLayout must stay under the documented budget. bd-16g.3 makes this an acceptance criterion; make it a test, not a promise.
- lod() is O(budget) after an O(log n) viewport seek; it must not scan all nodes per frame.
- clippy pedantic + nursery clean; no unsafe.

TESTS.
- THE DRIFT TEST (write this one first): feed N births/speciations incrementally, then build a layout from scratch from the same final graph, and assert the two are COORDINATE-IDENTICAL. Incremental layout drifting away from the true layout — slowly, invisibly, only on long runs — is the actual failure mode of every incremental layout ever written.
- LOD: budget=k over a fixed viewport returns exactly min(k, visible) nodes; the same query twice returns the SAME k nodes in the same order; changing only the hover/selection state changes nothing. A tie in (peak_population, duration) resolves by founder uid (assert the tie explicitly — an unstable sort here makes the tree flicker between frames).
- Pruned-parent reattachment: prune an ancestor, extend, assert the child attaches to PrunedAncestor and no index dangles.
- hit_test: a table of (x, y) -> expected key, including a miss (returns None) and a boundary hit at exactly `tol`.
- Degenerate: empty tree, one node, budget=0, viewport before the first tick and after the last -> empty iterator, no panic.
- Perf: 100k-node species tree — assert extend() for a batch of new nodes stays under a stated ms budget and allocates only amortized growth (assert allocation COUNT, not just time; timing alone flakes in CI). Assert full_relayout is false throughout a normal 50k-tick run.
- Determinism: two runs of the same seeded delta sequence -> identical coordinate digest.

LOGGING. The layout module is pure and returns LayoutDelta/ExpandReport/PruneReport; the app and frontends log (scriptbots-core has no tracing dependency and must not gain one).
- debug per layout update: nodes added, nodes moved, total nodes, total edges, duration, and whether a full relayout occurred. bd-16g.3 explicitly requires logging the node/edge count and rebuild timing "so the tree cannot silently become a hot path" — this line is that requirement.
- warn on EVERY full relayout, with the reason (budget exceeded, sentinel reattachment cascade, explicit invalidation). A silent fallback to O(n) per frame is exactly how this feature dies.
- warn when the LOD budget truncates the visible set (visible_nodes, budget) — truncation must never be invisible; bd-16g.3.5 must also surface it in the UI.
- info once at layout construction: memory bound, bytes/node, configured budgets.

title: Phylogeny views: interactive tree in GPU lab, compact clade table in TUI
description:
SCOPE. The two frontends for the phylogeny, and nothing else: (a) an interactive tree in the GPU lab (crates/scriptbots-render/src/lib.rs, gpui) with pan/zoom, a tick scrubber, branch selection and a founder/clade inspector; (b) a compact clade table plus an events pane in the TUI (crates/scriptbots-app/src/terminal/mod.rs, ratatui). Both are READ-ONLY PROJECTIONS of TreeLayout (bd-16g.3.4), SpeciesTable (bd-16g.3.2) and the PhyloEvent stream (bd-16g.3.3). OUT OF SCOPE: any layout math, any clustering, any event logic, any new crate. If a view needs a number that does not exist, the number belongs in .2/.3/.4 — not in a UI file.

WHY. The tree is the payoff: bd-16g.3 exists because "ScriptBots is an EVOLUTION simulator whose evolution is currently invisible." The GPU lab gets the artifact that sells the project (and feeds bd-16g.9's highlight reels); the TUI gets the version that works over SSH on a headless box, which is where long runs actually live. Two views, one source of truth — the moment a frontend recomputes a centroid or re-derives a species name, the two views disagree and the project's central honesty claim (what you see is what the sim computed) is gone.

DESIGN.
- Shared, frontend-agnostic draw model, computed once in core (or in a small view-model module) and consumed by both:
    pub struct TreeDrawList { pub branches: Vec<BranchCmd>, pub labels: Vec<LabelCmd>, pub events: Vec<EventMarker>, pub truncated: Option<TruncationInfo> }
    pub fn tree_draw_list(layout: &TreeLayout, species: &SpeciesTable, events: &[PhyloEvent], viewport: Viewport, budget: usize) -> TreeDrawList
  This is a PURE FUNCTION with no gpui/ratatui/wgpu types in its signature, which is what makes it testable headlessly. The frontends translate BranchCmd/LabelCmd into their own primitives and do nothing else.
- GPU lab: pan/zoom over the tick axis; a scrubber bound to the same tick range the world/replay exposes (bd-2z0.5.3); click a branch -> hit_test (bd-16g.3.4) -> inspector showing species id + name, founder uid(s), first/last tick, generation range, brain kind(s), member count, peak population, the sibling clade it split from, and the confirmed/rejected separation evidence from bd-16g.3.3. Leave a hook (not an implementation) for the mutation diff of bd-16g.13.
- TUI: a ratatui table — species id, name, size, delta-size, founder uid, age, mean diet, sparkline of population — in a deterministic sort order (default: size desc, tie-break species id asc; never HashMap iteration order), plus a scrolling events pane. Wire it into the existing terminal panel/keybinding scheme; document the keys in the existing help pane. The TUI must compile and pass tests WITHOUT gpui.
- Selection is the ONLY mutation these views perform, and it must go through the existing selection path. See the warning in bd-16g.4.4: SelectionState drives activation capture in stage_brains, so a phylogeny view that "selects" a whole clade to highlight it would silently turn on brain-activation capture for every member. Highlighting in this view MUST use a view-local highlight set, NOT AgentRuntime.selection.
- Truncation must be VISIBLE: when the LOD budget collapses clades, the UI says so (a "+N collapsed clades" affordance), it does not just draw fewer branches.

HARD REQUIREMENTS.
- Rendering never blocks the sim thread; the views take a snapshot/clone of the draw list, they do not hold the world lock across a frame (the render crate already locks the world — respect that boundary and keep the critical section to a copy).
- Deterministic display: same layout + same viewport -> same draw list, byte-for-byte, including label order.
- No panic on: a fresh world with zero species, a world with exactly one species, an extinct-everything world, scrubbing before tick 0 or past the last tick, a viewport with zero area, or a species with a pruned ancestor.
- The 100k-node tree renders AT THE BUDGET, not by drawing 100k branches. Assert the draw-list length against the budget.
- clippy pedantic + nursery clean across both frontends; no new crates, no new dependencies.

TESTS.
- Headless golden test of tree_draw_list for a hand-built 3-species fixture: exact branch/label/event-marker sets and their order. No GPU involved, so it runs in CI.
- Budget test: a 10k-node fixture with budget=200 -> draw list has <= 200 branches AND truncated == Some(..) with the collapsed count.
- Hit-test integration: clicking the coordinates of species B returns species B; clicking empty space returns None; clicking a collapsed clade returns the collapse root, not one of its hidden children.
- TUI snapshot: render the clade table to a ratatui TestBackend at a fixed size and compare against a golden; include a fixture with long species names (truncation/ellipsis) and one with 200 species (scroll + no panic).
- NEGATIVE: empty world -> both views render an explicit "no species yet" state (assert the string), not a blank panel and not a panic. NEGATIVE: scrub to a tick before a species existed -> it is ABSENT; scrub to a tick after it went extinct -> it is present as a terminated branch in the past and absent from the present clade table. A tree that shows extinct species as alive is the most common phylogeny-UI bug and this test is what forbids it.
- NEGATIVE: assert the phylogeny view does not write AgentRuntime.selection (a test that highlights a clade and then asserts the world's captured-activation count is unchanged — this is the coupling that would silently cost the population's activation buffers every tick).
- Determinism: same fixture rendered twice -> identical draw list and identical TUI snapshot.

LOGGING (tracing is available in scriptbots-app and scriptbots-render).
- info when a phylogeny view opens: node count, edge count, species count, LOD budget, memory estimate.
- debug on selection: species id, name, founder uid, member count, tick.
- warn when the draw list is truncated by the budget: visible nodes, budget, collapsed clade count — so a user who sees a simplified tree can confirm from the log that it was simplified rather than wrong.
- warn if a view ever receives a species id absent from the layout, or a layout key absent from the species table (a desync between .2 and .4 must be loud; a silently missing branch looks exactly like an extinction).
- debug per frame at most once per second: draw-list build duration, so the view cannot silently become a frame-time regression.

title: Agent-perspective inspector: see the world through one agent's senses and brain
description:
THE IDEA. Select an agent and see the world AS IT DOES: its four eye cones rendered as the actual color/density values it receives, the smell/sound/hearing/blood channels as gradients or bars, its clock phases, its temperature discomfort — the full 25-element sensor vector, laid out as PERCEPTION rather than as numbers. Beside it, its brain's internal activations lighting up, and the 9 outputs it chose (wheel velocities, spike intent, boost, give, sound, color). Step tick-by-tick, or scrub through replay, and watch stimulus become decision.

WHY IT RANKS #4. The README's second pillar is "a brain testbed" — the whole point of the pluggable Brain trait. Yet a user today cannot answer the most basic question about any agent: WHY did it do that? This view makes the sim's core scientific object (a sensorimotor loop) directly observable, converts the brain-architecture comparison from a table of survival rates into an intuition ("DWRAON agents fixate on the food channel; MLP agents react to blood"), and is the single best demo artifact the project could have. It is also unusually cheap NOW: the sensor layout is fixed and documented (index 0-24), and the demand-driven activation probe already exists (WorldState::set_activation_probe, landed at e2d9aaa) precisely so a single inspected agent can be snapshotted without costing the whole population.

DESIGN.
- Sensor decoding must be shared, not re-derived: expose a single core function sensor_layout() -> &[SensorField{index, name, channel, eye_index}] used by TUI, GPUI, Bevy, and web. A future sensor added to core must break these views at compile time rather than silently mislabel them (this is a real risk: the layout is currently only an implicit convention in stage_sense).
- Egocentric view: draw the agent's four eye cones at their true angles/FOV with the perceived RGB+density; overlay the neighbors that actually contributed (a "why" affordance — click a cone to list contributing agents and their intensity).
- Brain panel: activations from bd-2z0.3.8's bounded introspection; highlight the top-k inputs by |weight*activation| for the chosen output ("this wheel command is being driven by eye-2 red and blood").
- Timeline: works live AND over replay (bd-2z0.5.3), so you can rewind to the tick before a kill and watch the decision form.
- Cost: strictly one probed agent (plus selection) — never the population. Assert this with a test that measures allocations/tick with and without an active probe.

ACCEPTANCE. With an agent probed: every one of the 25 sensor values displayed matches core's runtime.sensors exactly (assert programmatically, not by eye); the displayed outputs match runtime.outputs; enabling the probe costs O(1) extra work per tick (population-independent, measured); and the view works identically in TUI and the GPU lab.

TESTS + LOGGING (required).
- Unit: sensor_layout() is exhaustive and total — a compile-time/const assertion that every index 0..INPUT_SIZE is named exactly once (this alone would have caught historical mislabeling).
- Unit: the view's decoded values equal core's sensors/outputs for a hand-built world (no drift between what the sim computes and what the UI claims).
- Unit: eye-cone contribution attribution reproduces stage_sense's own accumulation for a 3-neighbor fixture (i.e., the "why" panel is not lying).
- Perf test: allocations and per-tick time with probe ON vs OFF at 5k agents must differ by a population-independent constant.
- E2E: headless TUI harness selects an agent, steps 100 ticks, dumps the sensor/activation/output table each tick to a log; assert the table is complete and self-consistent; this log IS the debugging artifact when a brain misbehaves.

title: Canonical sensor_layout() map with exhaustiveness proof shared by all frontends
description:
SCOPE. ONE canonical, const, compile-time-exhaustive description of the 25 sensor inputs, living in scriptbots-core, consumed by every frontend (TUI, GPUI render, Bevy, web/wasm) and by the LLM assistant (bd-16g.1). Deliverable: the SensorField table, the const exhaustiveness proof, a drift test proving the table matches what stage_sense actually computes, and the migration of every existing frontend onto it. OUT OF SCOPE: the egocentric render (bd-16g.4.2), the brain panel (bd-16g.4.3), the probe cost guard (bd-16g.4.4), and the OUTPUT map — bd-2z0.2.4 owns the centralized output map; mirror its shape and consume it, do not fork a second one.

WHY. The sensor index layout is currently an IMPLICIT CONVENTION with exactly one source of truth: 25 hand-written assignments inside stage_sense (crates/scriptbots-core/src/lib.rs:6070-6096). Nothing connects those indices to any label anywhere. The GPU lab renders sensors as anonymous bars titled "s0".."s7" (render_brain_bars, crates/scriptbots-render/src/lib.rs:7594-7614, which shows only the first 8 of 25); the TUI shows raw activation rows. Nothing — not a type, not a test, not the compiler — prevents a UI from labelling index 6 "smell" when core is writing eye-1 red there.
This is not hypothetical. The project has ALREADY paid for it: combat read outputs[3] — the COLOR GREEN channel — as though it were boost, for months (see bd-2z0.2.4, "Centralize neural outputs and fix boost/combat indexing"). An index-convention bug in the sibling array, undetected, changing the actual behavior of the simulation. A centralized, compile-time-checked map is the fix for the entire class, on the input side, before bd-16g.4.2/.4.3 build a UI that confidently narrates the wrong channel.
The layout is also NON-CONTIGUOUS, which makes an implicit convention indefensible: eye 0 = 0..3, food = 4, eye 1 = 5..8, sound = 9, smell = 10, health = 11, eye 2 = 12..15, clock0 = 16, clock1 = 17, hearing = 18, blood = 19, temperature = 20, eye 3 = 21..24. Nobody reconstructs that from memory correctly. Ever.

DESIGN.
- Home: scriptbots-core, next to INPUT_SIZE/NUM_EYES (lib.rs:88-92). Not a feature flag, not optional, present in every build including wasm32 — a layout that is absent from one target is a layout that will be re-invented on that target.
- Types (all const-constructible, zero allocation, no serde requirement, no UI types):
    pub enum SensorChannel { EyeDensity, EyeRed, EyeGreen, EyeBlue, Food, Sound, Smell, Health, Clock, Hearing, Blood, Temperature }
    pub enum SensorSource { Neighbors, FoodGrid, SelfState, Environment }   // consumed by bd-16g.4.2 to decide which channels even HAVE contributors
    pub struct SensorField { pub index: usize, pub name: &'static str, pub short: &'static str, pub channel: SensorChannel, pub eye_index: Option<usize>, pub clock_index: Option<usize>, pub source: SensorSource, pub range: (f32, f32) /* (0.0, 1.0): every sensor is clamp01'd in stage_sense */ }
    pub const SENSOR_LAYOUT: [SensorField; INPUT_SIZE] = [ ... ];
    pub const fn sensor_layout() -> &'static [SensorField; INPUT_SIZE];
    pub const fn sensor_field(index: usize) -> Option<&'static SensorField>;   // total; no panicking index accessor is exposed
    pub const SENSOR_LAYOUT_DIGEST: u64;   // FNV-1a over (index, name, channel) — stamps logs/artifacts with the layout they were produced under
- THE EXHAUSTIVENESS PROOF (this is the deliverable, not the table): a `const { assert!(..) }` block (Rust 2024 const asserts) that verifies, AT COMPILE TIME: (a) the array length == INPUT_SIZE; (b) every index in 0..INPUT_SIZE appears exactly once, in ascending order; (c) every name is unique; (d) each eye_index in 0..NUM_EYES appears exactly 4 times (density + R + G + B); (e) exactly one Food, one Smell, one Health, one Hearing, one Blood, one Temperature, one Sound, and two Clock fields. Adding a 26th sensor to core without adding its SensorField must FAIL TO COMPILE. That is the whole point: the compiler, not a code review, is what keeps the frontends honest.
- Wiring: stage_sense should write through the layout where practical; where it cannot (the hot loop writes a [f32; INPUT_SIZE] directly), the DRIFT TEST below is mandatory — a table that certifies itself is worthless.
- Migrate every consumer in the same bead: render_brain_bars (render:7594) and the sensor heat ring (render:7896-7901) must show all 25 named channels, not 8 anonymous ones; the TUI sensor/activation panels; the bevy and web views; and the control/API surfaces that expose sensor arrays.
- MUST NOT COUPLE TO: serde, tracing, any UI crate, any allocation. This is a const table and two const fns.

HARD REQUIREMENTS.
- Zero runtime cost: `&'static` data, const fns, no lazy init, no OnceLock.
- Total, no panic: sensor_field(i) returns Option; no `SENSOR_LAYOUT[i]` accessor is exported for untrusted indices.
- No drift: the layout is a claim about stage_sense's behavior, and that claim is TESTED (below), not asserted in a comment.
- Determinism: SENSOR_LAYOUT_DIGEST is stable across builds and platforms (FNV-1a over bytes — never std's DefaultHasher, whose output is not stable across releases).
- clippy pedantic + nursery clean.

TESTS.
- Compile-time: the const assertion block IS a test — add a trybuild-style or documented negative check (an example that adds a field without an index and must fail to compile), so the guarantee is demonstrated, not merely believed.
- Independent ground-truth table test: a literal table written INDEPENDENTLY in the test file (index -> name, channel, eye_index), asserted against sensor_layout(). If the test imports the layout to build its expectation, the test proves nothing.
- THE DRIFT TEST (this is the one that matters): build a world with one agent and one neighbor at a known bearing/distance; step one tick; record runtime.sensors. Then MOVE the neighbor and step again. Assert that ONLY the indices declared SensorSource::Neighbors changed, and that every index declared SelfState/FoodGrid/Environment did not. Then vary the food cell, the agent's health, the tick (clocks), and the agent's x-position (temperature) one at a time and assert the corresponding declared indices — and only those — respond. This proves the map describes stage_sense rather than describing itself, and it is what would have caught the historical mislabeling class.
- Frontend conformance: in EACH frontend crate, a test asserting the label it displays for index i equals sensor_layout()[i].name for all i. Nobody re-invents labels; the test makes re-invention fail CI.
- Run under both feature configurations (--features simd_wide and --no-default-features): the SIMD and scalar accumulation paths in stage_sense are separate code (lib.rs:5800-6060), and the layout must describe both.

LOGGING. None in core: scriptbots-core has NO tracing dependency and must not gain one (see its Cargo.toml). The APP logs SENSOR_LAYOUT_DIGEST once at startup at debug, and stamps it into the run manifest / characterization record (crates/scriptbots-app/src/lib.rs RunManifestV0) so that any replay artifact, log, or LLM narration can be tied to the exact sensor layout it was produced under. A saved artifact whose sensor semantics cannot be recovered is an artifact nobody can trust later.
close_reason: Landed (channels.rs at 805d3b6; labelled inspector bars at a5dfada). SENSOR_LAYOUT and OutputChannel with const-assertion exhaustiveness proofs, shared by core, bevy, and the GPUI inspector - whose brain bars now carry real channel names and show every channel (previously 's0' with blood, temperature and all of eye 3 truncated away). Behaviour-neutral, proven by the app's pinned characterization digests.

title: Egocentric sensory render: eye cones, channel gauges, and per-cone contributor attribution
description:
SCOPE. The egocentric view of ONE probed agent: its four eye cones drawn at their true angles/FOV carrying the perceived density+RGB, the non-eye channels (food, sound, smell, health, clock0/1, hearing, blood, temperature) as labeled gauges, and — the part that makes it science rather than decoration — PER-CONE CONTRIBUTOR ATTRIBUTION: click a cone, get the list of neighbors that actually produced that value and how much each one contributed. Includes the core-side `explain_sensors()` that computes attribution, and its rendering in the GPU lab and TUI. OUT OF SCOPE: the brain panel (bd-16g.4.3), the probe cost guard and replay scrub (bd-16g.4.4), sensor naming (bd-16g.4.1 owns SensorField/SensorSource — consume it).

WHY. bd-16g.4 exists to answer "why did it do that?", and half of that answer is "because of what it saw". A panel that draws 25 bars is a numeric dump; a panel that says "eye 2's red is 0.8 because of the carnivore at bearing +12 deg, distance 34" is an explanation. It also converts the brain-family comparison from a table of survival rates into intuition. And the attribution is the only thing that can CATCH a sensing bug: the eye/blood/sound accumulation in stage_sense is nontrivial (SIMD and scalar paths, trait multipliers, a legacy proximity factor) and nothing today can show that it is doing what it claims.

DESIGN.
- Attribution is computed in CORE, never re-derived in a UI. A UI that re-implements the falloff formula will get it subtly wrong and then confidently display the wrong explanation — the worst possible outcome, because it looks authoritative.
    pub struct SensorContribution { pub source_uid: AgentUid, pub source_id: AgentId, pub eye: Option<usize>, pub bearing: f32, pub distance: f32, pub intensity: f32, pub color: [f32; 3], pub density_delta: f32, pub rgb_delta: [f32; 3], pub smell_delta: f32, pub sound_delta: f32, pub hearing_delta: f32, pub blood_delta: f32 }
    pub struct SensorAttribution { pub agent: AgentId, pub tick: Tick, pub raw: [f32; INPUT_SIZE] /* PRE-clamp */, pub clamped: [f32; INPUT_SIZE] /* == runtime.sensors, exactly */, pub saturated: [bool; INPUT_SIZE], pub contributions: Vec<SensorContribution>, pub truncated: usize }
    impl WorldState { pub fn explain_sensors(&self, agent: AgentId, max_contributors: usize) -> Option<SensorAttribution> }
- The accumulation formula must live in ONE place that stage_sense also uses (or, at minimum, a shared inline helper): intensity = traits.eye * ((fov - |angle_diff|)/fov).max(0) * (radius - dist)/radius; the DENSITY channel carries an extra `* (dist / radius)` (the legacy C++ proximity factor, crates/scriptbots-core/src/lib.rs:6032-6039); and smell/sound/hearing/blood are accumulated raw and multiplied by their trait modifiers AFTER the neighbor loop (lib.rs:6058-6062). Getting that multiply-after ordering wrong makes every attribution number wrong by a constant factor — plausible-looking, and wrong.
- THE CLAMP IS THE TRAP. runtime.sensors are clamp01'd on write (lib.rs:6070-6096). Contributions routinely sum ABOVE 1.0, so a panel that lists contributors totalling 2.4 next to a displayed sensor value of 1.0 looks broken and will be "fixed" by someone normalizing the contributors, which destroys the information. The view MUST show raw vs clamped and flag saturation explicitly. This is why SensorAttribution carries both arrays and a `saturated` mask.
- NOT EVERY CHANNEL HAS CONTRIBUTORS. Attribution applies only to neighbor-derived channels: the 16 eye indices (0-3, 5-8, 12-15, 21-24), sound (9), smell (10), hearing (18), blood (19). Food (4) comes from the food grid cell; health (11) is self-state; clocks (16, 17) are self-state x tick; temperature (20) is derived from world position and the agent's temperature_preference. The view must SAY that, per channel, using SensorField::source from bd-16g.4.1 — an empty contributor list on a self-state channel must read as "self-state", never as "no neighbors detected".
- Blood has its own geometry: only neighbors inside BLOOD_HALF_FOV of the agent's HEADING (not of an eye) and weighted by their wound level (1 - health*0.5). Attribution must reproduce that, not the eye cone.
- FEATURE-PATH DUALITY: with `simd_wide` (a DEFAULT feature) the accumulation is a different code path with a different summation order than the scalar path. Attribution must be compared against `runtime.sensors` produced by THE SAME BUILD, and the tests must run under both configurations. Do not assert cross-build equality; do assert intra-build equality to 1e-6.
- Cost: explain_sensors runs ONLY for the probed agent, on demand, from the frontend — never for the population. It respects bd-2z0.3.8's bounded/demand-driven introspection boundary; bd-16g.4.4 proves the boundary holds.
- Rendering: GPU lab draws the four cones at (heading + eye_direction[e]) with half-angle eye_fov[e] (AgentRuntime, lib.rs:911-912), tinted by the perceived RGB and thickened by density; TUI shows a compact named-channel gauge table plus a contributor list. Both consume the SAME SensorAttribution — no second derivation.

HARD REQUIREMENTS.
- Determinism: contributions are sorted by (intensity desc, source_uid asc) — a stable, total order; never float-equality-dependent, never HashMap order. Same world + same agent -> byte-identical attribution.
- No panic: unknown/dead agent -> None. Zero neighbors -> empty contributions, raw == clamped, no saturation. A neighbor at distance ~0 (the epsilon guard in stage_sense) -> excluded, exactly as core excludes it.
- Bounded: contributions are capped at `max_contributors` (top-k by intensity, deterministic tie-break); `truncated` reports how many were dropped. Never an unbounded Vec sized by the neighbor count.
- clamped MUST equal runtime.sensors EXACTLY (bit-for-bit) — this is the acceptance criterion of bd-16g.4 ("every one of the 25 sensor values displayed matches core's runtime.sensors exactly (assert programmatically, not by eye)"), and it is an assertion, not an aspiration.
- clippy pedantic + nursery clean; no unsafe.

TESTS (table-driven, both feature configs).
- Three-neighbor fixture at hand-computed bearings/distances/colors: assert each eye's density/R/G/B equals the sum of the returned per-contributor deltas within 1e-6 (pre-clamp), and that `clamped` equals runtime.sensors bit-for-bit.
- SATURATION NEGATIVE TEST: a fixture with many bright close neighbors so the raw sum exceeds 1.0 -> assert raw > 1.0, clamped == 1.0, saturated[i] == true, and that the contributor list still sums to `raw` (NOT to 1.0). This is the test that stops someone from "fixing" the panel by renormalizing away the truth.
- BOUNDARY NEGATIVE TESTS: a neighbor exactly at sense_radius, and one exactly at the FOV edge -> contribute zero and appear NOWHERE in the contributor list (a phantom contributor with intensity 0 is a lie about what the agent saw).
- Blood: a wounded neighbor inside BLOOD_HALF_FOV vs an identically wounded one outside it -> only the first contributes; assert the wound weighting (1 - health*0.5).
- Trait-multiplier ordering: change traits.smell and assert the smell channel scales while the individual contributor deltas scale consistently (catches multiply-before vs multiply-after).
