- Self-state channels: assert food/health/clock/temperature have EMPTY contributor lists and are reported with their SensorSource, not as "no neighbors".
- Truncation: 100 neighbors, max_contributors=8 -> exactly 8 returned, truncated == 92, and the 8 are the top-8 by intensity with the documented tie-break.
- Determinism: same fixture twice -> identical attribution (compare a digest).
- E2E: probe an agent in a live 200-tick run; every tick, assert attribution.clamped == world.runtime[agent].sensors.

LOGGING. Core returns the struct and logs nothing (scriptbots-core has no tracing dependency and must not gain one); the frontends log.
- debug per probed tick: agent uid, per-eye (density, R, G, B) raw AND clamped, the saturation mask, contributor count, truncated count, and the top contributor (uid, bearing, distance, intensity).
- warn if `clamped[i]` differs from world.runtime[agent].sensors[i] for ANY i — an internal-consistency alarm. If attribution and core ever disagree, the panel is lying and the operator must find out from the log, not from a paper written on bad data.
- debug on cone selection: eye index, its FOV/direction, and the full contributor list actually shown.

comments.author: Jeff Emanuel
comments.text:
CORE HALF LANDED at 3d3ad3b: WorldState::explain_sensors(agent, max_contributors) -> Option<SensorAttribution>, with SensorContribution carrying per-eye density/RGB deltas, smell/sound/hearing/blood deltas, bearing, distance and colour. Bounded top-k with a reported truncated count; total order (intensity desc, then stable agent identity) so a world always explains itself the same way; None for a dead agent; empty contributions for a lone agent (self-state channels still carry values, so an empty list never reads as "senses nothing").

BEAD REQUIREMENT CORRECTED - this bead demanded "clamped MUST equal runtime.sensors EXACTLY (bit-for-bit)". That requirement is WRONG and I did not implement it. stage_sense runs BEFORE actuation, so runtime.sensors describe the positions agents held before they moved; the world that produced them no longer exists, and recomputing attribution from current positions cannot reproduce them. Faking agreement would have produced an authoritative-looking lie, which is the exact failure this bead exists to prevent.
The honest contract implemented instead: explain_sensors describes the world AS IT STANDS (what the next sensing pass will see), and the test PROVES it - explain, step once, and require core's own runtime.sensors to match the prediction across all 25 channels within 1e-5. That is a stronger claim than the original and it holds under BOTH feature paths (simd_wide default and the scalar/WASM lane), which also resolves the bead's SIMD/scalar duality worry: attribution is compared against the same build's sensors, never across builds.

Other traps the bead named, all handled: trait multipliers are applied to accumulated totals AFTER the neighbour loop (folding them in per-neighbour is plausible-looking and wrong by a constant factor); the DENSITY channel alone carries the legacy proximity factor (dist/radius); blood uses the heading cone with wound weighting, not an eye cone; saturation is reported explicitly (raw + clamped + saturated mask), tested with a 40-agent crowd that oversaturates smell, because a panel listing contributors totalling 2.4 beside a displayed 1.0 invites someone to "fix" it by normalising, destroying the information.
Implementation note: explain_sensors does a full O(n) scan rather than querying the spatial index, because the index holds whichever stage last rebuilt it and an explanation computed against stale buckets would silently omit real contributors. It runs for one agent on demand, so O(n) is the right trade.

REMAINING FOR THIS BEAD: the rendering half - eye cones drawn at (heading + eye_direction[e]) with half-angle eye_fov[e], tinted by perceived RGB and thickened by density, plus the click-a-cone contributor list in the GPU lab, and the compact named-channel gauge table in the TUI. Both must consume this SensorAttribution; neither may re-derive the falloff.

title: Brain panel: activations plus top-k input attribution for each chosen output
description:
SCOPE. The brain half of the inspector: render the probed agent's BrainActivations (layers + connection weights) and, for each of the 9 chosen outputs, the TOP-K INPUT ATTRIBUTION ("this left-wheel command is being driven by eye-2 red and blood"). Includes the pure attribution function in core and its panels in the GPU lab and TUI. OUT OF SCOPE: the introspection plumbing itself (bd-2z0.3.8 owns bounded/demand-driven activation capture — consume its snapshot, do not widen it), the probe cost proof (bd-16g.4.4), sensor names (bd-16g.4.1), and the output index map (bd-2z0.2.4 owns it).

WHY. The README's second pillar is "a brain testbed" — the entire justification for the pluggable Brain trait — and today a user cannot answer the most basic question about any agent: why did it do that? The data already exists: BrainActivations { layers: Vec<ActivationLayer{name,width,height,values}>, connections: Vec<ActivationEdge{from,to,weight}> } (crates/scriptbots-core/src/lib.rs:19-37), captured on demand in stage_brains (lib.rs:6124-6135) and already surfaced as an anonymous heatmap in the GPU lab (render_activation_heatmaps, crates/scriptbots-render/src/lib.rs:7632) and a raw row viewer in the TUI (terminal/mod.rs:1081-1090). What is missing is MEANING: which named sensor drove which named output.

DESIGN.
- Attribution is a pure function in core, not UI code:
    pub enum AttributionMethod { OneHopWeightActivation, PathProduct { depth: usize }, Unavailable(AttributionUnavailable) }
    pub enum AttributionUnavailable { NoActivations, NoConnections, IdentityPassthrough, UnsupportedTopology }
    pub struct InputAttribution { pub input_index: usize, pub sensor_name: &'static str /* from bd-16g.4.1 */, pub contribution: f32, pub weight: f32, pub activation: f32 }
    pub struct OutputExplanation { pub output_index: usize, pub output_name: &'static str /* from bd-2z0.2.4 */, pub raw_value: f32, pub effective: EffectiveOutput, pub method: AttributionMethod, pub inputs: Vec<InputAttribution>, pub non_finite_skipped: u32 }
    pub fn attribute_output(act: &BrainActivations, output: usize, k: usize) -> Result<OutputExplanation, AttributionError>
- Method: |weight * activation| along the connection graph — one hop for directly-connected topologies (DWRAON), a documented depth-bounded path-product for layered MLPs. STATE THE METHOD IN THE STRUCT. An attribution that quietly claims more than its method can support is worse than no attribution, because it will be believed. If the topology is not supported, return Unavailable(UnsupportedTopology) and say so in the UI.
- THE OUTPUT MAP IS NOT YOURS TO INVENT. decode_outputs (crates/scriptbots-core/src/lib.rs:6219-6240) destructures the 9 outputs as [left, right, color_r, color_g, color_b, spike, boost_raw, sound_level, give_intent]. Use bd-2z0.2.4's centralized map for names. Do NOT hand-roll a second index table in a UI file — that is precisely the bug bd-2z0.2.4 exists to fix (combat read outputs[3], the GREEN COLOR channel, as if it were boost, for months).
- BOOST IS THRESHOLDED. `boost: boost_raw > 0.5` (lib.rs:6236). The actuator sees a BOOL, the brain emitted a FLOAT. The panel must show BOTH (raw 0.49 -> boost OFF is the whole story of a near-miss), hence EffectiveOutput { Continuous(f32) | Thresholded { raw: f32, active: bool, threshold: f32 } | Clamped { raw: f32, applied: f32 } }. Showing only the raw float, or only the bool, hides the decision.
- THE UNBOUND-BRAIN TRAP. If an agent's BrainBinding has no runner, stage_brains calls default_outputs, which COPIES THE FIRST 9 SENSORS STRAIGHT INTO THE OUTPUTS (crates/scriptbots-core/src/lib.rs:6107-6112). Such an agent has perfect-looking "attribution" — output i is trivially driven by input i — that means absolutely nothing. The panel MUST detect this and display Unavailable(IdentityPassthrough) with an explicit "unbound brain: outputs are an identity copy of sensors 0..8" note. Fabricating an explanation here is the single most embarrassing way this bead can ship.
- Similarly, BrainBinding::snapshot_activations() returns Option (lib.rs:692-707) and some brain families return None -> Unavailable(NoActivations). The UI states the reason; it never renders an empty panel with no explanation.
- Panels: GPU lab replaces/extends render_activation_heatmaps with named layers plus a per-output attribution list; the TUI extends its existing layer viewer with a named-output table and top-k rows. Both consume the SAME OutputExplanation.
- MUST NOT COUPLE TO: forcing capture for all agents (see bd-16g.4.4 — SelectionState already triggers capture, and select-all makes it population-wide); holding the world lock across a frame; re-deriving sensor names or output names.

HARD REQUIREMENTS.
- Pure, deterministic: inputs sorted by (|contribution| desc, input_index asc) — an explicit total order. An unstable or float-equality-dependent sort makes the panel flicker between frames on ties, which is both a UX bug and a determinism smell.
- No panic: empty layers, a single layer, an out-of-range output index (typed AttributionError), zero connections, or NaN/inf activations (EXCLUDE them and report non_finite_skipped; never propagate NaN into a displayed contribution, and never let NaN poison the sort).
- Bounded cost: O(connections touching the output) for one-hop; the path-product depth is CAPPED and the cap is documented. Attribution runs for the probed agent only, on demand.
- clippy pedantic + nursery clean; no unsafe.

TESTS.
- Hand-built BrainActivations fixture with known weights and activations -> assert top-k is exactly the expected set AND the expected ORDER, including a deliberate |contribution| tie -> assert the input_index tie-break resolves it (this is the flicker test).
- NEGATIVE, unbound brain: an agent with no runner, stepped one tick -> assert runtime.outputs == first 9 sensors AND that the panel reports Unavailable(IdentityPassthrough) with ZERO attribution rows. The panel must refuse to explain a passthrough.
- NEGATIVE, no activations: a brain family whose snapshot_activations() returns None -> Unavailable(NoActivations); the UI shows the reason string (assert it).
- NEGATIVE, non-finite: an activation vector containing NaN and +inf -> those inputs are excluded, non_finite_skipped == 2, no panic, and the remaining order is unchanged.
- NEGATIVE, no connections: a brain that reports layers but no ActivationEdges -> Unavailable(NoConnections), not a silently empty top-k that reads as "nothing drives this output".
- Round-trip against reality: step a real MLP agent one tick with the probe on; assert every displayed output value equals runtime.outputs[i] EXACTLY, and that the displayed boost state equals (outputs[6] > 0.5). Assert the panel's name for output 6 is "boost" and for output 3 is the green color channel — a regression test for the historical mislabeling.
- Determinism: same fixture twice -> identical OutputExplanation for all 9 outputs.

LOGGING (tracing in the app/render crates; core returns values and does not log).
- debug per probed tick: agent uid, brain kind, layer names + widths + heights, all 9 NAMED outputs with raw value and effective value (including the boost bool), and the top-3 attribution rows per wheel output. This line is the artifact you read when a brain misbehaves; it must stand alone.
- warn ONCE per (agent, brain kind) when attribution is Unavailable, with the reason variant. "The panel is empty" must be diagnosable from the log without attaching a debugger.
- warn when non_finite_skipped > 0, with the count and the layer name — NaN in a brain's activations is a real bug in the brain, and the inspector is the thing most likely to see it first.

title: Probe cost guard: O(1) population-independent overhead test and replay-scrub integration
description:
SCOPE. Make the inspector's cost PROVABLY population-independent, and make it work over replay. Three deliverables: (a) a hard capture budget in core so activation snapshotting can never scale with population; (b) a perf test that measures allocations/time with the probe ON vs OFF at multiple populations and asserts the SLOPE w.r.t. population is ~0; (c) probe integration with replay scrubbing (bd-2z0.5.3) with a determinism proof that probing does not perturb the run. OUT OF SCOPE: the panels themselves (bd-16g.4.2, bd-16g.4.3), the introspection API (bd-2z0.3.8).

WHY. bd-16g.4's acceptance criterion is "enabling the probe costs O(1) extra work per tick (population-independent, measured)". Today that is FALSE, and the code says so:
    let capture = probe == Some(agent_id) || runtime.selection != SelectionState::None;   // crates/scriptbots-core/src/lib.rs:6128
Capture is triggered by SelectionState, and SelectionState is set per-agent by the renderer — including `select_all_agents`, which sets SelectionState::Selected on EVERY agent in the world (crates/scriptbots-render/src/lib.rs:3074-3090). One keystroke in the GPU lab therefore makes the world call snapshot_activations() for the entire population, every tick, allocating a fresh Vec<ActivationLayer> per agent per tick. The comment right above that line says activation capture "for every agent allocates layer buffers across the whole population every tick" — and then nothing prevents it. This bead is the enforcement that the comment promises. The same coupling is why bd-16g.3.5 is forbidden from using AgentRuntime.selection to highlight a clade.

DESIGN.
- Core: a BOUNDED capture path.
    pub struct CaptureBudget { pub max_agents: usize }        // default small (e.g. 4); configurable, never unbounded
    pub struct ProbeStats { pub captured: usize, pub budget: usize, pub dropped: usize, pub explain_calls: u64 }
    impl WorldState {
      pub fn set_capture_budget(&mut self, budget: CaptureBudget);
      pub fn probe_stats(&self) -> ProbeStats;                // last tick
    }
  In stage_brains, capture in DETERMINISTIC handle order until the budget is exhausted; count and report the drops. The explicit activation_probe agent is ALWAYS captured first (it is the inspector's subject); selection-driven capture fills the remaining budget. A world with 10k Selected agents captures `budget` of them and reports dropped = 10k - budget. It never allocates 10k layer buffers.
- Probe lifecycle: `set_activation_probe(Some(id))` (crates/scriptbots-core/src/lib.rs:9590) must auto-clear when the probed agent dies, and the frontends must render "agent died at tick T" rather than a stale panel. A dangling probe on a reused slotmap slot would silently start inspecting a DIFFERENT agent — the same identity hazard bd-16g.3.1 documents; key the probe's identity check on AgentUid (bd-2z0.3.1).
- REPLAY SCRUB (bd-2z0.5.3): to inspect tick T of a recorded run, re-simulate from the nearest checkpoint with the probe set, then step to T. Activations are NOT persisted and MUST NOT be — per-agent-per-tick activation persistence is explicitly out of scope and would blow up the run DB. The inspector's scrub is therefore "re-derive under probe", which is only sound if probing is observationally neutral — which is what the determinism test below proves.
- OBSERVATIONAL NEUTRALITY IS THE LOAD-BEARING CLAIM. Setting a probe must not touch the RNG stream, must not change any world state that a digest or replay comparison covers, and must not mutate the brain (an evaluator that caches state during snapshot_activations() would silently make probed runs diverge from unprobed ones — and then every conclusion drawn from the inspector would be about a different simulation than the one that ran).
- MUST NOT COUPLE TO: any frontend (the budget lives in core), storage (nothing new is persisted), or the panels.

HARD REQUIREMENTS.
- Population-independence, asserted on the SLOPE, not on an absolute number: measure per-tick allocation count and wall time at populations {1k, 5k, 10k} with probe OFF and probe ON, and assert that (delta_allocs at 10k) - (delta_allocs at 1k) is within a documented tolerance of zero. Absolute timing thresholds flake in CI and teach everyone to ignore the test; a slope assertion does not.
- Determinism: a run with the probe active and the same run without must produce IDENTICAL world digests and IDENTICAL replay event streams (the project already has a replay/diff harness — crates/scriptbots-app/src/main.rs run_replay_cli / diff_event_stream — reuse it rather than inventing a second comparison).
- No panic: probing a dead/unknown agent (probe clears, returns None), probing during a replay before the agent is born, budget = 0 (capture nothing, report dropped), budget > population.
- Capture order is deterministic (handle order), so which agents get captured under a saturated budget is reproducible.
- clippy pedantic + nursery clean.

TESTS.
- THE REGRESSION TEST THAT CATCHES TODAY'S BUG: mark 500 agents Selected (exactly what select_all_agents does), step, and assert probe_stats().captured == budget (NOT 500) and dropped == 500 - budget (adjusting for the probe). Then assert the per-tick allocation count is unchanged vs. zero selected agents. Without this test the O(N) path returns the first time someone adds a multi-select feature.
- Allocation-slope table: a counting allocator in the test harness; table over {1k, 5k, 10k agents} x {probe off, probe on, probe on + 1 selected}; assert the probe-on minus probe-off allocation delta is constant in population within tolerance; LOG the measured slope and intercept so a CI failure prints the actual numbers rather than "assertion failed".
- Determinism/neutrality: a seeded 5k-tick headless run with the probe set on ticks 100..200 vs a run with no probe -> identical world digest AND identical replay event stream. Repeat with a brain family whose snapshot_activations() is non-trivial (this is where a caching evaluator would be caught).
- Probed-agent-death: probe an agent, kill it, step -> probe auto-clears, probe_stats().captured drops, no panic, and the frontend receives an explicit "died at tick T" state.
- Replay scrub E2E: record a run; scrub to tick T; assert the re-derived sensors/outputs at T equal the recorded ones for the probed agent (using the existing replay comparison), proving the scrub shows the run that actually happened.
- E2E inspector artifact (the bd-16g.4 acceptance test): a headless TUI harness selects an agent and steps 100 ticks, dumping one JSONL row per tick containing all 25 NAMED sensors (bd-16g.4.1), the raw/clamped/saturated attribution summary (bd-16g.4.2), the activation layer digest and the 9 NAMED outputs with effective values (bd-16g.4.3). Assert every row is complete and self-consistent: clamped == world.runtime[agent].sensors, outputs == runtime.outputs, boost == (outputs[6] > 0.5). THIS LOG IS THE DEBUGGING ARTIFACT when a brain misbehaves — it is a deliverable, not a test byproduct.

LOGGING.
- info when a probe is set or cleared: agent uid, agent id, tick, reason (user selection / replay scrub / agent death).
- warn whenever the capture budget drops agents: captured, budget, dropped, and the trigger (selection count). A silently truncated capture is invisible otherwise, and an operator who selected 500 agents and sees 4 inspectors deserves to know why.
- debug every 100 ticks: ProbeStats (captured, budget, dropped, explain_calls).
- The perf test logs its measured slope, intercept, and tolerance at info, so a CI failure is a diagnosis and not a mystery.

title: Island archipelago: parallel worlds with migration, allopatric speciation, and linear scaling
description:
THE IDEA. Run N independent worlds ("islands") in one process with a deterministic migration schedule between them: every M ticks, K agents (selected by a documented rule) emigrate from island i to island j along a configurable topology (ring, fully-connected, custom graph). Present them as a tiled archipelago view; allow per-island config overrides (island 3 is arctic; island 5 has no carnivores).

WHY IT RANKS #5. This is the rare idea that is simultaneously a SCIENCE upgrade, a PERFORMANCE story, and a FUN feature:
 (a) Science: the island model is the classic mechanism for maintaining genetic diversity and producing ALLOPATRIC speciation — populations diverge in isolation, then meet. It converts ScriptBots from "one soup that converges" into a system where the most interesting phenomenon in evolutionary biology (speciation by geographic isolation) can actually happen and be observed via bd-16g.3. Migration rate becomes a first-class experimental knob for bd-16g.1 to sweep.
 (b) Performance: worlds are independent between migration barriers — this is embarrassingly parallel. N islands on N cores scales linearly, which is a far better use of a 32-core machine than fighting for intra-tick parallelism inside one world (where our profiling shows 8 threads is already the sweet spot). The archipelago is the honest answer to "how do we use big machines?"
 (c) Fun: watching a red predator strain cross a strait and collapse a naive island is the best story this simulator can tell.

DESIGN.
- Requires the sole-owner host (bd-2z0.4.5): an archipelago is N HostCores plus a deterministic Migrator. Do NOT implement this against the current Arc<Mutex<WorldState>> shape — it would have to be rebuilt.
- Determinism is the hard part and the whole value: migration must be a barrier with a fixed order (islands stepped to the same tick, then emigrants selected/applied in ascending (island_id, agent_uid) order), and each island's RNG must be domain-separated (bd-2z0.3.10) so island 3's draws never depend on island 1's population. The digest of an archipelago run must be reproducible across thread counts — assert this exactly as the current 1-thread-vs-N-thread det-check does.
- Emigrant selection rules (config): random, fittest, youngest, or "wanderer" (highest realized speed). Each documented, each deterministic.
- Migration must be replayable: emigration is an event in the journal (bd-2z0.5.2), not a hidden side effect.
- Per-island config overrides reuse the scenario schema (bd-2z0.10.1) — an island IS a scenario.

ACCEPTANCE. 8 islands x 5k ticks with ring migration: (a) bit-identical digest at 1 thread vs 8 threads vs 8 islands-on-4-threads; (b) near-linear throughput scaling up to core count (report the measured curve; >=0.7 efficiency at 8 islands is the bar); (c) with migration DISABLED, islands provably diverge (different species per island via bd-16g.3); with migration ENABLED at a moderate rate, gene flow is measurable (founder contributions cross islands per bd-2z0.11.1).

TESTS + LOGGING (required).
- Unit: migrator selection rules (deterministic ordering, correct counts, no duplication, no loss — an agent that emigrates must exist on exactly one island afterward; assert conservation of population across the barrier).
- Unit: domain-separated RNG — island k's tick sequence is unchanged by adding/removing other islands (this is the test that catches accidental shared-RNG coupling).
- Determinism test: archipelago digest stable across thread counts (extend the existing det-check to the archipelago).
- Perf test: throughput vs island count curve, recorded as an artifact so regressions are visible.
- E2E: 8-island run, migration on, persist per-island metrics + migration events to one run DB with island_id columns; assert offline reconstruction of each island's history and of the migration graph. Log per-barrier: tick, island pairs, emigrant UIDs, selection rule, populations before/after — a migration bug must be diagnosable from the log alone.

title: Archipelago host: N HostCores, tiled config, per-island scenario overrides
description:
SCOPE. The `Archipelago` type: it owns N islands, steps every one of them to a common tick, validates cross-island compatibility, and hands the barrier to the Migrator. OUT OF SCOPE: migration rules (bd-16g.5.2), RNG domain separation (bd-16g.5.3), the CI gates (bd-16g.5.4), persistence and the tiled view's data path (bd-16g.5.5).

WHY. This is the load-bearing bead of bd-16g.5: without a host that owns N independent worlds and steps them to a common tick, there is no migrator to write, no per-island RNG to separate, and nothing for the gates to gate. It serves the project twice over. Scientifically, it is what makes allopatric speciation possible at all (bd-16g.3 can then SEE it, and bd-16g.1 can sweep migration rate as a first-class knob). Architecturally, it is the honest answer to "how do we use a 32-core machine?" — islands are embarrassingly parallel between barriers, whereas intra-tick parallelism inside one world tops out around 8 threads. And it is a stress test of bd-2z0.4.5's sole-owner host: if HostCore cannot be instantiated N times and stepped independently, it is not actually sole-owner.

*** BLOCKED ON bd-2z0.4.5, AND THAT IS NOT NEGOTIABLE. READ THIS BEFORE WRITING A LINE. ***
There is no HostCore in the tree today (grep it: nothing). The world is reached through `SharedWorld = Arc<Mutex<WorldState>>` — see `ControlHandle` and `lock_world` at crates/scriptbots-app/src/control.rs:185-226 — and EVERY control surface (REST, MCP, CLI, TUI) takes that lock. An archipelago built on that shape means N mutexes, N lock orders, a Migrator that must hold two of them at once, and a determinism story that dies the first time a control surface interleaves with a barrier. It would have to be thrown away when bd-2z0.4.5 lands. bd-16g.5 says this explicitly and it is the single most expensive mistake available in this sub-epic: DO NOT IMPLEMENT THE ARCHIPELAGO AGAINST `Arc<Mutex<WorldState>>`. If you find yourself reaching for a second mutex, stop and go finish bd-2z0.4.5.

DESIGN.
- HOME: an `archipelago` module in scriptbots-core, sitting next to the host module bd-2z0.4.5 creates. It must be HEADLESS — usable from `--config-only`/headless runs with no renderer, because bd-16g.5.4's determinism gate spawns exactly those.
    pub struct IslandId(pub u16);
    pub struct IslandSpec { id: IslandId, config: ScriptBotsConfig, label: String }
    pub enum Topology { Ring, FullyConnected, Custom(Vec<(IslandId, IslandId)>) }   // normalized: sorted, deduped, self-edges rejected
    pub struct ArchipelagoConfig { islands: Vec<IslandSpec>, topology: Topology, migration: MigrationConfig, master_seed: u64 }
    pub struct Archipelago { cores: Vec<HostCore>, cfg: ArchipelagoConfig, tick: Tick }
    impl Archipelago {
        pub fn step_to_barrier(&mut self) -> Result<BarrierReport, ArchipelagoError>;  // every island reaches the SAME tick
        pub fn islands(&self) -> &[HostCore];
    }
- AN ISLAND IS A SCENARIO. Per-island config = base config + scenario override, merged through the SAME path `ControlHandle::apply_patch` uses (`merge_value` -> `serde_path_to_error::deserialize::<ScriptBotsConfig>` -> `ScriptBotsConfig::validate()`; control.rs:469-510) and reusing bd-2z0.10.1's scenario schema. Do NOT invent a second config merge. Failure mode prevented: island 3's override quietly accepts a knob the main validator would reject, and only island 3 is nonsense — which you will discover four hours into a run, in an analysis, as a "surprising result."
- WHAT MUST BE UNIFORM ACROSS ISLANDS, validated AT CONSTRUCTION with a named error: anything that changes the MEANING of an emigrating agent — brain kind and topology, genome layout, sensor/actuator arity, and any per-agent cached state whose interpretation depends on config. Islands MAY differ in world size, food regrowth, terrain/scenario knobs, carnivore rules, population caps. An agent that crosses a strait into a world where its brain has a different input arity is a panic in the best case and silent garbage in the worst. Enforce it with `ArchipelagoError::IncompatibleIslands { island, field, a, b }` at BUILD time, not at migration time — the migration is 250 ticks and one barrier later, and by then the error message will point at the wrong thing.
- HETEROGENEOUS WORLD SIZES REQUIRE A DOCUMENTED POSITION REMAP. If island A is 2000x2000 and island B is 1000x1000, an emigrant's position must be re-mapped by a deterministic rule (proposed: preserve normalized (x/w, y/h), then clamp into bounds; or spawn at a deterministic coastal cell). Whatever the rule, it is CONFIG and it is TESTED. The crash this prevents: an agent teleported outside the destination's food grid, or to (NaN, NaN).
- PARALLELISM AND THE NESTED-RAYON PROBLEM. Islands are independent BETWEEN barriers — that is the entire performance thesis — so they step in parallel across a rayon scope. But scriptbots-core ALREADY uses rayon INSIDE `step` (`par_iter` at crates/scriptbots-core/src/lib.rs:60, `par_chunks_mut` at 5419). Running islands as rayon tasks that themselves fan out via rayon is NESTED PARALLELISM: decide the pool topology, DOCUMENT it, and expose it as a dial (proposed: one global pool; islands are the outer tasks; intra-island `par_iter` thresholds raised or disabled once island_count >= thread_count, since there is no work left to steal). Getting this wrong does not corrupt anything — it just delivers 0.3 efficiency and a baffling profile, and bd-16g.5.4's scaling gate will catch it only if the dial's state is recorded in the artifact.
- ONE STORAGE PIPELINE, NOT N. AGENTS.md's storage contract: `fsqlite::Connection` is deliberately `!Send + !Sync`, is constructed/used/closed on the storage worker thread, and "never place a connection or connection-owning `Storage` inside cross-thread `Arc<Mutex<_>>` state." N islands must NOT open N connections. Islands emit their per-tick batches; the Archipelago funnels them into the SINGLE pipeline at the barrier, in ascending island_id order (bd-16g.5.5 owns the schema). State this HERE so that nobody "solves" the contention by handing each island its own connection — that path violates the contract, breaks batch identity, and is very hard to walk back.

HARD REQUIREMENTS.
- NO SHARED MUTABLE STATE BETWEEN ISLANDS BETWEEN BARRIERS. No shared RNG (bd-16g.5.3), no shared counters, and — the one people miss — NO SHARED AGENT-UID ALLOCATOR. If UIDs come from one atomic counter bumped by parallel islands, UID assignment becomes a function of thread scheduling, and every downstream ordering rule (the Migrator sorts by uid!) becomes nondeterministic. Allocate from a per-island domain: `(island_id, local_uid)` or a high-bit-tagged u64. This is the second-most-likely determinism killer after the RNG, it is invisible at one thread, and it only appears when you scale.
- ISLANDS AND TOPOLOGY EDGES ARE ALWAYS ITERATED IN ASCENDING ID ORDER. `Topology::Custom` is normalized (sorted, deduped, self-edges rejected) at construction. HashMap/HashSet of islands is BANNED in any path that touches state.
- Every island reaches tick T before ANY migration is applied. A partially-stepped archipelago must never be observable — not by the migrator, not by the storage layer, not by a view.
- NO PANIC: an island that faults (`WorldStepError`, a brain fault, a storage `NotAdmitted`) fails the whole archipelago with a TYPED error naming the island. It must not poison a mutex and hang its neighbors.
- BOUNDED: a documented `MAX_ISLANDS`, and every island's config validated UP FRONT — a 64-island run must not die on island 63 after an hour of stepping.

TESTS.
- Unit: construction REJECTS incompatible islands (brain arity mismatch) with the named error; ACCEPTS legal heterogeneity (different world sizes, different food rates).
- Unit: an N=1 archipelago is bit-identical to a plain single-world run of the same config — compare `characterization_digest_v0` after T ticks. This proves the wrapper itself adds no drift, and it is the cheapest possible early warning.
- Unit, THE INDEPENDENCE TEST: with migration DISABLED, island k's digest is IDENTICAL whether it runs alone or inside an 8-island archipelago. This is the strongest available proof of independence and it fails LOUDLY the instant someone shares a counter or an RNG. (bd-16g.5.3 owns the RNG half of this and states it as its marquee test; assert it here too, because it also catches shared UID allocators and shared scratch buffers, which are not RNG bugs.)
- Unit: permute island STEP order (step them in reverse) -> identical per-island digests with migration off.
- E2E: 4 heterogeneous islands (different food regrowth rates), 2k ticks, migration off, headless. Assert per-island digests, no panic, exactly ONE storage file, and matching tick counts across islands.
- NEGATIVE: an island whose `step` errors mid-barrier -> typed `ArchipelagoError` naming the island; the archipelago does not hang, and does not leave the storage pipeline wedged with a retained batch nobody will retry.

LOGGING.
- info at construction, once: {island_count, topology, migration_interval, uniform_fields_checked} plus one line per island {id, label, config_hash, world_w, world_h}. Every "why did island 3 behave strangely" investigation starts by asking what island 3's config actually was; if it is not in the log, that investigation starts with a guess.
- Per-barrier logging is owned by bd-16g.5.2.
- error on any island fault: {island_id, label, tick, cause}. A user must be able to answer "which island died, what was it configured as, and at what tick" from the log alone.

title: Deterministic Migrator: barrier, ordered emigrant selection rules, population conservation
description:
SCOPE. The barrier protocol, the emigrant selection rules, and population conservation. OUT OF SCOPE: RNG domain separation (bd-16g.5.3), the digest/perf gates (bd-16g.5.4), persistence (bd-16g.5.5), the host itself (bd-16g.5.1).

WHY. This is the bead where the archipelago's determinism is won or lost. Everything else in bd-16g.5 is bookkeeping around it. bd-16g.5 states the requirement in one sentence — "migration must be a barrier with a fixed order (islands stepped to the same tick, then emigrants selected/applied in ascending (island_id, agent_uid) order)" — and every plausible implementation shortcut violates it.

DESIGN — THE BARRIER, PRECISELY.
    pub struct MigrationConfig { interval_ticks: u64, emigrants_per_edge: u16, rule: SelectionRule, replace: bool }
    pub enum SelectionRule { Random, Fittest, Youngest, Wanderer }
    pub struct Emigrant { agent_uid: u64, from: IslandId, to: IslandId, tick: Tick, rule: SelectionRule, key_value: f32, rank: u16 }
    pub struct BarrierReport { tick: Tick, moves: Vec<Emigrant>, pop_before: Vec<u32>, pop_after: Vec<u32> }
    fn migrate(islands: &mut [HostCore], cfg: &MigrationConfig, edges: &[(IslandId, IslandId)], rng: &mut MigrationRng) -> Result<BarrierReport, MigrationError>;

ORDER IS THE CONTRACT. Write this sequence into the module doc comment, because it is exactly what a future "harmless" refactor will break:
  1. EVERY island has been stepped to the same tick T. No island may be at T-1. (bd-16g.5.1 guarantees this; assert it here anyway — a cheap assert at the top of `migrate` is worth a week of bisecting.)
  2. SELECTION runs over islands in ASCENDING island_id, and within an island over agents in ASCENDING agent_uid. Never slotmap handle order (handles are reused — `slotmap` is the project's agent store and its iteration order is an implementation detail), never HashMap order, never "whatever the spatial index returns."
  3. ALL selections for the whole barrier are computed BEFORE ANY are applied. Two-phase: select-all, then apply-all, reading a FROZEN pre-barrier population snapshot.
  4. APPLICATION runs in ascending (to_island, from_island, agent_uid).
Any deviation — for instance, selecting from island 2 after island 1 has already received an immigrant — makes the outcome depend on edge iteration order, and the archipelago is no longer reproducible. It will still LOOK fine at one thread.

TWO-PHASE ALSO FIXES THE SUBTLE BUG that a per-edge loop cannot: in a fully-connected topology, island 1's fittest agent would otherwise be selected for the edge to island 0 AND the edge to island 2 — emigrating twice, i.e. being DUPLICATED. Equally, an immigrant that has just landed must not be re-selected as an emigrant in the same barrier. Selection reads the frozen snapshot; both bugs become unrepresentable.

TIE-BREAKING IS TOTAL, ALWAYS.
  - `Fittest` sorts by (energy DESC, agent_uid ASC). The uid tiebreak is not optional garnish; without it, two agents with identical energy are ordered by whatever the sort did last, and the sort is only stable if you kept it stable.
  - Ranking floats: use `f32::total_cmp` or a bits-based total order. `partial_cmp().unwrap()` is BANNED — it is simultaneously a panic (on NaN) and a nondeterminism, which is an impressive amount of damage for one method call.
  - `Youngest`: (age ASC, uid ASC). `Wanderer` (highest realized speed): (speed DESC, uid ASC).
  - `Random`: draws from the MIGRATION RNG stream owned by bd-16g.5.3 — seeded from (master_seed, MIGRATION, barrier_index), NOT from any island's stream, or the draw would depend on how many agents happened to reproduce on island 0 that epoch. Sample by a deterministic index-based method (partial Fisher-Yates over a uid-SORTED vec), never `choose_multiple` over an unordered iterator.

CONSERVATION IS AN INVARIANT, NOT A TEST. After a barrier: `sum(pop_after) == sum(pop_before)` when `replace = true`, and every emigrant uid exists on EXACTLY ONE island. Check it in code (a cheap count check in release, plus `debug_assert`) and return `MigrationError::PopulationNotConserved { before, after, moves }` rather than proceeding. A DUPLICATED agent is the worst bug available here: the population silently inflates, the genetics are garbage, the science is wrong, and NOTHING CRASHES. You would find it in a paper, not in a stack trace.

EMIGRATION IS A JOURNAL EVENT (bd-2z0.5.2), NOT A HIDDEN SIDE EFFECT. If a migration is not in the journal, the run is not replayable, and bd-2z0's entire replay story is broken BY THIS FEATURE. Honor it on day one; retrofitting replay onto a mutation that was never journaled means reconstructing history from a digest mismatch.

DEGENERATE POPULATIONS, all documented and all legal:
  - An island with fewer agents than `emigrants_per_edge` sends what it has. It does not wait, does not error, does not fabricate.
  - An empty island sends nothing and can still RECEIVE.
  - An island reduced to ZERO by emigration is legal and must be visible in the log — that is a scientifically interesting event (emigration-driven extinction), not an error.
  - A destination at its population cap: the immigrant STILL LANDS, and cap enforcement happens on the destination's own next step by its own rules. Do NOT invent a special-case death at the barrier. A special case at the barrier is a place for nondeterminism to hide, and it also silently changes the science (you would be adding a novel mortality source that no config knob describes).

HARD REQUIREMENTS.
- Zero `partial_cmp().unwrap()`. Zero HashMap/HashSet iteration in selection or application. Zero wall-clock. Zero thread-id dependence. Zero `rand::random()`.
- The barrier is a hard synchronization point: no island observes another island's post-barrier state during selection.
- The IDENTICAL `BarrierReport` — same moves, same order — must be produced at 1 thread and at N threads. bd-16g.5.4 proves it; this bead makes it true.
- NO PANIC on: 0 agents, 1 agent, emigrants > population, a self-edge (rejected at config validation in bd-16g.5.1, not silently no-op'd here), duplicate edges (normalized away), an out-of-range island id.

TESTS.
- Unit, one per rule: a fixed 10-agent island with hand-chosen energies/ages/speeds and an exact expected uid list — INCLUDING two agents TIED on the sort key. Assert the uid tiebreak decides, and that swapping their insertion order does not change the outcome. THIS IS THE TEST THAT CATCHES AN UNSTABLE SORT, and an unstable sort is the most common source of "it was deterministic on my machine."
- Unit, TWO-PHASE DISCIPLINE: fully-connected topology where island 1's fittest is eligible for two edges. Assert the agent moves EXACTLY ONCE and the second edge selects the next-fittest. A naive per-edge select-and-apply duplicates it; this test is what stops that implementation from ever landing.
- Unit, CONSERVATION as a property test: 200 seeded cases over random topologies, populations, and rates. Assert total population invariant, no uid on two islands, no uid lost.
- Unit, EDGE-ORDER INVARIANCE: seeded shuffle of the edge list before the barrier -> IDENTICAL `BarrierReport` (edges are normalized and sorted). This catches the "it worked because my HashSet happened to iterate that way today" bug, which is the bug that will actually happen.
- Unit, degenerate: emigrants_per_edge > population; empty island; an island emptied BY emigration; a destination at its population cap.
- E2E: 8 islands, ring, 5k ticks, migration every 250 ticks. Assert conservation at EVERY barrier, and that the journal's migration events, replayed, reconstruct the same per-island populations tick-for-tick.

LOGGING. bd-16g.5 requires that "a migration bug must be diagnosable from the log alone." This bead's log IS the debugging tool; design it that way.
- info per barrier: {tick, rule, interval, edges, total_moves, pop_before: [..], pop_after: [..], conserved: bool}.
- info (drop to debug only if volume genuinely bites) per move: {tick, from, to, agent_uid, rule, rank, key_value}. `key_value` is the energy/age/speed that got the agent selected — with it, "why did THIS agent leave?" is answerable from the log; without it, that question needs a debugger and a reproduction.
- warn: an island sending fewer than requested (with its population); an island reaching 0 by emigration; a destination at cap.
- error: `PopulationNotConserved` with the FULL `BarrierReport` — before, after, and every move. That error must never be a one-line "migration failed"; it is the one error where the payload is the whole investigation.

title: Domain-separated per-island RNG with cross-island independence proof
description:
SCOPE. Per-island RNG stream derivation, and the PROOF that islands are independent. OUT OF SCOPE: bd-2z0.3.10 owns the DOMAIN taxonomy (environment, food, population, lineage/agent, mutation, crossover) and the generator choice. This bead ADDS THE ISLAND AXIS to that design and proves it. Do NOT fork a second RNG scheme; if bd-2z0.3.10 has not landed, this bead is blocked on it, not licensed to invent.

WHY. bd-16g.5 names this as "the hard part and the whole value": an archipelago whose islands share an RNG is either eight copies of one world (no science) or a nondeterministic mess (no reproducibility). Both outcomes destroy the feature, and neither one crashes. This bead serves the parent by making island independence a PROVEN property rather than an assumed one, and it serves the project by extending bd-2z0.3.10's domain separation along the one axis that sub-epic did not anticipate — and by forcing the master seed to be explicit, which every long archipelago run will thank it for.

*** THE CURRENT STATE, so nobody is surprised by what they find. ***
`WorldState` holds ONE `rng: SmallRng` field (crates/scriptbots-core/src/lib.rs:5089), seeded once from `ScriptBotsConfig::seeded_rng()` (lib.rs:3515) via `SmallRng::seed_from_u64(seed)`, and it is handed out as `&mut SmallRng` through `WorldState::rng()` (lib.rs:9724) to every consumer — terrain generation, spawns, mutation, crossover, food. That is a SINGLE SHARED STREAM whose sequence at any moment depends on how many draws every OTHER consumer has made. Construct N islands from this design and you get one of two fatal outcomes: identical islands (same seed -> same everything, which makes the archipelago scientifically pointless — 8 copies of one world is not an island model), or arbitrarily coupled islands (a shared generator -> island 3's draws depend on island 1's population, and determinism dies the moment thread scheduling changes). There is no third option. This bead is the fix.

DESIGN.
- SEED DERIVATION IS A PURE, DOCUMENTED FUNCTION, not an accident of construction order:
      stream_seed = kdf(master_seed, DOMAIN_TAG, island_id)
  Fixed-width, byte-order-explicit. The house style already exists and should be followed: `characterization_digest_v0` (lib.rs:9316-9327) hashes "explicit little-endian integers and `f32::to_bits()` values with domain-separated FNV-1a 64." Use that discipline, or whatever generator bd-2z0.3.10 selects — but SPECIFY THE BYTE LAYOUT in the doc comment. Every field entering the KDF is written explicitly. NO `std::hash::Hash`, NO `DefaultHasher`: its output is explicitly not stable across Rust versions, and using it would mean a toolchain bump silently changes every result the project has ever published.
- *** DO NOT DERIVE SEEDS BY ADDITION. *** `master_seed + island_id` is the obvious thing and it is wrong: PRNGs seeded with adjacent integers can produce correlated early output, and `SmallRng` (xoshiro-family via `seed_from_u64`) is not immune enough to bet a science project on it. Eight islands that are supposed to be independent replicates but whose food/mutation streams are correlated is a bug that produces PLAUSIBLE, PUBLISHABLE, WRONG results. The KDF must diffuse.
- THE ISLAND ID ENTERS EVERY DOMAIN. Island 3's food stream, mutation stream, and population stream are each independent of island 1's. And the MIGRATION stream is ITS OWN domain, owned by the Migrator, seeded from (master_seed, MIGRATION, barrier_index) — NOT drawn from any island's stream. If migration draws from island 0's generator, the choice of emigrants on the island-4-to-island-5 edge depends on how many agents happened to reproduce on island 0 that epoch. That is the exact coupling this bead exists to eliminate, hiding in the one place people forget to look.
- THE PROPERTY, stated so it can be tested: an island's RNG sequence is a function of (master_seed, island_id, its own draw history) AND NOTHING ELSE. Not the island COUNT. Not the thread count. Not the scheduling. Not whether a neighbor went extinct. ADDING A 9TH ISLAND MUST NOT PERTURB ISLANDS 0-7 BY ONE BIT. That sentence is this bead's acceptance criterion.
- MIGRATION MUST NOT SMUGGLE RNG STATE ACROSS THE BARRIER. An immigrating agent carries its genome and its phenotype — never a generator, never a generator's state. If any per-agent RNG state exists at all, it is RE-DERIVED ON ARRIVAL from (destination island's stream, agent_uid) by a documented rule. Failure mode prevented: agent-carried RNG state makes island B's future draws a function of island A's history; the independence property dies silently, every existing test still passes, and the archipelago's determinism gate keeps going green because it only varies thread counts, not island counts.

HARD REQUIREMENTS.
- NO `rand::random()`, no `thread_rng`, no entropy source anywhere below the top-level master seed. NOTE: `ScriptBotsConfig::seeded_rng()` currently FALLS BACK to `rand::random()` when `rng_seed` is None (lib.rs:3519). In an archipelago config, a missing master seed is a HARD ERROR at construction, not a silent entropy draw. An unreproducible 8-hour, 8-island run is a uniquely painful way to learn this lesson, and you only get to learn it once per run.
- STREAM DERIVATION IS STABLE across platforms, endianness, and Rust versions. Freeze it with a GOLDEN TEST: `kdf(0xDEAD_BEEF, FOOD, 3)` equals a hard-coded constant checked into the repo. If a refactor changes it, that test goes red and someone has to make a DELIBERATE decision to bump a version tag — which is exactly the friction you want, because that change invalidates every prior run's reproducibility.
- NO SHARED MUTABLE RNG ACROSS THREADS. Each island owns its streams BY VALUE inside its HostCore. `Arc<Mutex<Rng>>` is banned outright: it reintroduces scheduling dependence at precisely the point we are trying to eliminate it, and it would pass a single-threaded test suite perfectly.

TESTS.
- THE INDEPENDENCE PROOF (the marquee test; bd-16g.5 names it as the one that "catches accidental shared-RNG coupling"): run island k ALONE for T ticks and record `characterization_digest_v0`. Then run it inside a 2-island, a 4-island, and an 8-island archipelago with migration DISABLED. Assert island k's digest is BYTE-IDENTICAL in all four. Then PERMUTE THE ISLAND ORDER in the config and assert it again (that second half catches order-dependent seeding, which the first half misses). This test would FAIL TODAY against the single shared `rng: SmallRng` — that is the point of writing it first.
- GOLDEN: hard-coded expected first-8-draws per (domain, island_id) for a fixed master seed, checked in as a fixture. This is the cross-platform stability guarantee.
- NEGATIVE, and do not skip it: two islands built from the SAME base config must NOT produce identical streams. This asserts the island_id actually entered the KDF. The bug it catches — "I forgot to mix in island_id, and everything looked fine because everything was perfectly deterministic" — produces 8 identical islands, a beautiful green determinism gate, and zero science. It is the most likely way this bead ships broken.
- NEGATIVE: an archipelago config with `rng_seed = None` -> typed error at construction (not a `rand::random()` fallback).
- STATISTICAL SMOKE (a supplement, never a substitute for the digest proof): pairwise correlation of 10^5 draws between island streams sits within the band expected of independent streams; likewise between different domains of the SAME island. This is what catches a KDF that diffuses badly — including, specifically, the `master + island_id` mistake called out above.
- Determinism under threads: identical per-island streams at 1 and 8 threads. bd-16g.5.4's gate subsumes this, but assert it here too — it is cheap and it localizes the failure to this module instead of to "the archipelago."

LOGGING.
- info at construction, ONE LINE PER (island, domain): {island_id, domain, stream_seed}. Print the DERIVED SEEDS. Every reproducibility investigation in this area begins by diffing derived seeds across two runs; if they are not in the log, that investigation begins with a rebuild and a print statement.
- info, ONCE, prominently: the master seed. It is not a secret. An archipelago run whose master seed does not appear in its own log is not reproducible by the person reading the log, which defeats the entire purpose of the run.
- debug: the first 4 draws per stream. This mirrors what the digest's RNG probe already does (lib.rs:9321, "four samples from a cloned RNG") and it is the cheapest possible instrument for "did the streams diverge, and if so, at which island and which domain."

title: Archipelago determinism + scaling gates (digest across thread counts; efficiency curve)
description:
SCOPE. The two CI gates that make bd-16g.5's claims falsifiable: (a) an archipelago determinism gate that EXTENDS the existing `--det-check`, and (b) a throughput-vs-island-count benchmark that emits a machine-readable efficiency curve. OUT OF SCOPE: the implementation being gated (.1, .2, .3, .5).

WHY. bd-16g.5 claims BOTH bit-exact reproducibility AND near-linear scaling. An unfalsifiable claim is exactly what the bd-2z0 recovery program exists to eliminate, and a parallel archipelago without a determinism gate WILL drift — silently, at 8 threads, on someone else's machine, four months from now. A perf claim with no recorded curve is marketing.

*** WHAT ACTUALLY EXISTS TODAY — read `run_det_check` at crates/scriptbots-app/src/main.rs:572 before designing anything. ***
The pattern is already right and should be REUSED, not reinvented: compose the parent's EFFECTIVE config; pin an explicit seed (`SCRIPTBOTS_DET_SEED`, else generate one and print it); serialize the WHOLE config to a TOML layer in a temp file — the comment at main.rs:575 explains why ("env-only forwarding loses `--config`/`--rng-seed` flags"); spawn two `--config-only` children with `--config <layer>`, `SCRIPTBOTS_DET_RUN=1`, `SCRIPTBOTS_DET_TICKS`, `SCRIPTBOTS_RNG_SEED`, and `RAYON_NUM_THREADS=1` vs default; parse each child's JSON stdout; compare.
*** BUT NOTE WHAT IT COMPARES (main.rs:644-690): `ticks`, `last_tick`, the full `Vec<TickSummary>` element-by-element, and the EVENT COUNT. It does NOT compare `characterization_digest_v0`. *** `TickSummary` is nine aggregate fields (tick, agent_count, births, deaths, total_energy, average_energy, average_health, max_age, spike_hits). It catches gross divergence and MISSES any permutation of agents that preserves the aggregates — which is precisely the class of bug a parallel migrator produces. Fixing that is part of THIS bead: emit `characterization_digest_v0` at checkpoint ticks and compare digests, and KEEP the summary comparison as the fast, human-readable first failure signal (it prints a lovely divergence report at main.rs:669-684; do not throw that away, it is how you find the tick to look at).

DESIGN.
- EXTEND, DO NOT FORK. Add the archipelago matrix into the existing det-check machinery (e.g. `--det-check-archipelago <TICKS>` sharing the same child-spawn/config-layer/seed-pinning code path). A second copy of `run_det_check` will drift from the first within two months and then one of them will be wrong and nobody will know which.
- THE MATRIX. All cells must produce IDENTICAL per-island digests AND an identical migration journal:
    * 8 islands, RAYON_NUM_THREADS=1
    * 8 islands, RAYON_NUM_THREADS=8
    * 8 islands, RAYON_NUM_THREADS=4   (islands > threads — catches work-stealing-order dependence; this is the cell people forget, and it is the one that fails)
    * 8 islands, RAYON_NUM_THREADS=3   (a non-divisor — catches chunking assumptions)
    * 8 islands with the ISLAND ORDER PERMUTED in the config (catches order-dependent seeding and order-dependent UID allocation, neither of which any thread-count variation will ever surface)
- COMPARE IN THIS ORDER, so the failure message is useful rather than merely correct: tick counts -> per-island `TickSummary` sequence (print the first divergence in the existing human-readable style) -> per-island `characterization_digest_v0` at checkpoint ticks -> the migration journal, event by event, in order. Report the FIRST diverging (island, tick), not "digests differ."
- DIGEST CAVEATS, HONORED RATHER THAN IGNORED. `characterization_digest_v0` (crates/scriptbots-core/src/lib.rs:9316-9331) requires a QUIESCENT tick boundary — it returns `CharacterizationError::NonQuiescent` when pending_deaths/pending_spawns/simulation_commands are non-empty — so take digests AT BARRIER BOUNDARIES, which are quiescent by construction. And its own doc says it is "a stable V0 regression oracle for ONE PINNED BUILD LANE, not a checkpoint or replay guarantee": this gate therefore compares runs of the SAME BINARY across thread counts and island orders. That is exactly the claim bd-16g.5 makes ("bit-identical digest at 1 thread vs 8 threads vs 8 islands-on-4-threads"). Do NOT stretch it into a cross-platform reproducibility promise that the digest cannot honestly support.
- SCALING GATE: run {1, 2, 4, 8, 16} islands at a FIXED per-island workload; record ticks/sec; emit a machine-readable artifact (JSON/CSV, under the `runs/` convention) with the efficiency column: throughput(N) / (N * throughput(1)). bd-16g.5 sets the bar at >= 0.7 efficiency at 8 islands. Enforce it as WARNING-plus-artifact on CI (a hard perf gate on a shared, noisy runner is a flake generator that will be disabled within a month) and as a HARD gate in a documented local/self-hosted benchmark lane. The artifact MUST record the machine, core count, thread count, build profile, and — critically — the nested-rayon dial from bd-16g.5.1 (was intra-island `par_iter` enabled?). A throughput number without its machine and its pool topology is not a measurement, it is a number.

HARD REQUIREMENTS.
- The DETERMINISM gate runs on EVERY PR. Keep it cheap: small worlds, ~2k ticks, 8 islands. The SCALING benchmark runs on a schedule or a label.
- A determinism failure MUST print: the first diverging (island, tick), both sides' `TickSummary`, both digests, and THE LAST THREE MIGRATION EVENTS BEFORE THE DIVERGENCE. A gate that says "mismatch" and stops costs a full day of bisecting; a gate that hands you the barrier that broke costs twenty minutes.
- ZERO TOLERANCE: digests compare for EXACT equality. No epsilon. If anyone proposes an epsilon, the determinism claim is already dead and the honest move is to say so out loud rather than to widen the tolerance.
- *** THE GATE MUST FAIL IF MIGRATION IS SILENTLY DISABLED. *** Assert `total_moves > 0` in the run being gated. Otherwise a bug that turns migration off makes the archipelago trivially deterministic — islands never interact — and the gate goes GREEN while the headline feature is completely broken. This is the most insidious way a determinism gate lies, and it is not hypothetical: "make the test pass" pressure finds this hole on its own.

TESTS. This bead IS the gate, so its test is a MUTATION TEST: deliberately introduce each known determinism killer in a scratch build and assert the gate goes RED for each.
  (a) select emigrants in slotmap-handle order instead of ascending agent_uid;
  (b) iterate topology edges out of a HashSet;
  (c) seed islands by `master_seed + island_id` (bd-16g.5.3 forbids this; the gate must catch it if it slips in);
  (d) allocate agent UIDs from one shared atomic counter across islands;
  (e) apply migration INSIDE the island-step parallel section rather than at the barrier;
  (f) compare digests with an epsilon.
RECORD THIS LIST IN THE TEST FILE. If a future change makes any of them pass, the gate has rotted, and the list is how the next person finds out.

LOGGING. Print in the project's house style (owo-colors; `run_det_check` already establishes the ✔/✖ vocabulary and AGENTS.md asks for informative, colorful console output): per matrix cell, {islands, threads, seed, ticks, per-island digest, migration_events, PASS/FAIL}. The scaling run prints the table with the efficiency column and the artifact path. THE ACCEPTANCE: CI output ALONE must tell you which cell failed and with exactly what seed and thread count to reproduce it locally. If a developer has to re-run the gate to find out what the gate found, the logging is wrong.

title: Archipelago views and per-island run-DB columns with migration-graph reconstruction
description:
SCOPE. Persistence and offline reconstruction for the archipelago: per-island columns in the run DB, a migration journal table, an islands table, a `--report-archipelago` reconstruction path, and the tiled view's DATA path. OUT OF SCOPE: the migrator (bd-16g.5.2), the RNG (bd-16g.5.3), the gates (bd-16g.5.4).

WHY. bd-16g.5's acceptance requires persisting per-island metrics and migration events to ONE run DB and reconstructing each island's history and the migration graph offline. None of that is possible against the current schema, so this bead is the difference between an archipelago you can watch and an archipelago you can STUDY. It serves the project beyond islands: adding island_id and lifting the primary keys generalizes the run DB from "one world's rows" to "one run's rows, partitioned," which is the same shape bd-2z0.5.5's experiment runner and bd-2z0.5.6's exports will want. And the migration journal is what keeps bd-2z0's replay promise true in the presence of a feature that moves agents between worlds.

*** THE SCHEMA PROBLEM, UP FRONT — THIS IS THE ACTUAL WORK. ***
The run DB today is single-world down to its primary keys. From the DDL in crates/scriptbots-storage/src/lib.rs (around lines 58-160):
    ticks(tick INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, epoch, closed, agent_count, births, deaths, total_energy, average_energy, average_health)
    metrics(tick, name, value, PRIMARY KEY (tick, name))
    events(tick, kind, count, PRIMARY KEY (tick, kind))
    replay_events(tick, seq, agent_id, scope, event_type, payload, PRIMARY KEY (tick, seq))
    agents(tick, agent_id, ...)   births(tick, agent_id, ...)   deaths(tick, agent_id, ...)
There is NO run_id and NO island_id anywhere. Eight islands writing at the same tick COLLIDE ON THE PRIMARY KEY OF `ticks` at the very first tick, not at the first barrier. This is not a nice-to-have column; it is a schema migration, and it is this bead's real content. Anyone who plans this bead as "add a column" has not read the DDL.

DESIGN.
- ADD `island_id INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0` to ticks/metrics/events/replay_events/agents/births/deaths, and LIFT EVERY PRIMARY KEY to include it: `ticks(island_id, tick)`, `metrics(island_id, tick, name)`, `events(island_id, tick, kind)`, `replay_events(island_id, tick, seq)`. A single-world run then IS an archipelago of one, at island_id = 0 — ONE schema, ONE code path, no "archipelago mode" fork of the storage layer. Do NOT ship a parallel set of `island_*` tables: that doubles every analytics query forever, and it is precisely the tech debt AGENTS.md's "no compatibility shims, do it the RIGHT way" rule exists to prevent.
- NEW TABLES:
    migrations(island_id_from, island_id_to, tick, seq, agent_uid, rule, key_value, rank, PRIMARY KEY (tick, seq))
      -- `seq` is the barrier's APPLICATION order (bd-16g.5.2 phase 4), so replaying the table in (tick, seq) order reproduces the barrier exactly. If seq is anything other than application order, the table is a log, not a journal, and replay is a guess.
    islands(island_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, label TEXT, config_hash BLOB, config_json TEXT)
      -- so an offline reader can reconstruct WHAT island 3 ACTUALLY WAS without needing the original config file, which will be gone.
  Match the existing DDL's discipline: it is rigorous about CHECK constraints (`CHECK (tick >= 0)`, `CHECK (closed IN (0,1))`, ...). Add `CHECK (island_id >= 0)` and a real bound; a NULL or out-of-range island_id must be impossible at the database level, not merely unlikely at the Rust level.
- ONE STORAGE WORKER, STILL. AGENTS.md's storage contract is not negotiable: `fsqlite::Connection` is `!Send + !Sync`, lives on the storage worker thread, is never placed in cross-thread `Arc<Mutex<_>>`; admission is bounded; each batch gets a stable BLAKE3 identity and moves through an outbox with admitted/applied/durable watermarks, and retry-safety depends on an IDENTICAL payload reproducing an IDENTICAL batch id. THEREFORE: the archipelago submits ONE batch per barrier containing all islands' rows, assembled in ascending (island_id, tick, seq/name/agent_id) order. NOT N concurrent submissions from N islands — that would make batch identity depend on thread scheduling, which breaks the retry-safety property the whole contract is built on. This is the single most likely place a well-meaning contributor will "helpfully" parallelize and quietly destroy the storage layer's determinism. Say it in the module doc.
- MIGRATION/RECOVERY PATH: the storage contract says startup REFUSES an existing database (except the explicit `--recover-storage FILE` path). So there is no fleet of legacy DBs to migrate — but the schema version must still be bumped and asserted, and the structural-verification path tracked by bd-2z0.8.9.4.2 must be updated IN THE SAME CHANGE, or `--recover-storage` will reject every database this feature produces. Coordinate; do not leave recovery broken and discover it during an incident.
- OFFLINE RECONSTRUCTION IS THE ACCEPTANCE. From the DB ALONE, with no live process: (a) each island's population/energy history; (b) the migration graph — a directed multigraph over islands, weighted by emigrant counts per epoch; (c) each emigrant's origin, destination, tick, and the selection key that chose it. Ship it as a query plus a `--report-archipelago <db>` mode in the EXISTING CLI (not a new binary — AGENTS.md's bar for new files is high and this is a report, not a program). Shipping it as a mode means CI EXERCISES it. An export path that nothing ever runs is an export path that does not work; that is not pessimism, it is the observed base rate.
- THE TILED VIEW (renderer/TUI, outside core) reads the lock-free `Arc<AnalyticsSnapshot>` the storage worker already publishes. AGENTS.md: "GUI, TUI, and API consumers load them without a mutex; rendering and paint paths never acquire a database lock or issue SQL." N island panels with sparklines and a migration arc animated on the barrier epoch is EXACTLY the feature that tempts someone to query the DB from the render loop. It must not.

HARD REQUIREMENTS.
- DETERMINISTIC ROW ORDER WITHIN A BATCH: ascending (island_id, tick, seq/name/agent_id). Two runs of the same archipelago produce byte-identical batch payloads and therefore identical BLAKE3 batch identities. That is not a nicety — it is what makes the storage layer's retry path safe.
- POPULATION CONSERVATION MUST BE VERIFIABLE OFFLINE. A query over `migrations` + `births` + `deaths` + `ticks` must reconcile each island's population at every barrier. If it does not reconcile, the persistence is LYING about the simulation, and every analysis built on it is worthless. Make that reconciliation a TEST, not an aspiration.
- NO PANIC and NO SILENT TRUNCATION: island_id fits u16 in memory but is INTEGER in SQLite; assert the round-trip.
- THE VIEW MUST DEGRADE: 64 islands must not render 64 live panels at 1 fps. Cap the panels, aggregate the remainder, and SAY SO ON SCREEN — a view that silently drops islands 32-63 is worse than a view that admits it is summarizing.

TESTS.
- Unit: DDL round-trip — insert rows for 8 islands AT THE SAME TICK; assert no PK collision. This is the test that fails today, on the current schema, and it is the reason this bead exists.
- Unit: batch assembly order is deterministic across two runs (hash the serialized payload and compare).
- E2E (REAL DB, NO MOCKS — the storage contract means a real file with a real advisory lease on a real worker thread): 8 islands x 2k ticks, ring migration; close the DB; reopen it offline; reconstruct per-island histories and the migration graph; assert the graph's edge weights equal the counts in the live run's `BarrierReport`s, and that per-island population RECONCILES from births/deaths/migrations at EVERY barrier.
- NEGATIVE, the important one: an emigrant that appears in `migrations` but whose agent_uid never subsequently appears in the DESTINATION island's `agents` rows -> the reconciliation test FAILS. This catches a migrator that journals a move it did not make, and a persistence layer that dropped one. NO IN-MEMORY ASSERTION CAN SEE EITHER BUG; only the offline reconstruction can.
- NEGATIVE: 0 islands (typed error); 1 island (the DB must be identical to a plain single-world run's, modulo the island_id=0 column — assert it, because that is what proves the "one schema, one code path" claim rather than merely asserting it in this description).
- DETERMINISM: two identical archipelago runs produce identical DB CONTENTS (compare a canonical, ordered dump). This is the persistence-layer counterpart of bd-16g.5.4's digest gate: a run can be deterministic in memory and nondeterministic on disk, and only this test knows the difference.

LOGGING.
- info per barrier persist: {tick, islands, rows_by_table, batch_id, admitted}.
- warn on queue pressure: the bounded persistence queue is real, and back-pressure is 8x more likely at 8 islands than at 1 — this feature will be the first thing to hit it, so the warning must name the tick and the depth.
- error on `NotAdmitted`: {tick, island_id, table, cause}. The storage contract LATCHES the fault and RETAINS the exact batch for retry, so the log must say precisely WHICH barrier is stuck — otherwise the operator cannot decide whether to retry or to abandon the run, which is the only decision they have.
- The offline report prints, in the project's colored console style: the islands table, the migration matrix, and the per-island reconciliation result (✔/✖ each). A ✖ there means the database contradicts itself, and it must be impossible to miss.

title: Open-ended evolution: MAP-Elites behavioral archive and novelty-search selection
description:
THE IDEA. Add optional open-ended-evolution machinery: a MAP-Elites archive that keeps the best agent found in each cell of a behavioral grid (e.g. speed x diet x aggression x sociality), plus a novelty-search selection mode that rewards being BEHAVIORALLY DIFFERENT from the archive rather than merely fit. Expose both as config: selection_mode = fitness | novelty | curiosity(hybrid), archive_dims = [...].

WHY IT MATTERS. Every naive alife sim converges: after a few thousand generations one strategy dominates and nothing interesting happens again — you are watching a fixed point. That is the single biggest reason people stop watching. MAP-Elites (Mouret & Clune) and novelty search (Lehman & Stanley) are the field's proven answers, and they are a natural fit here because ScriptBots ALREADY has a behavior space worth exploring (diet, speed, spike usage, giving, signaling) and bd-2z0.11.2 is already defining exactly those phenotype features. The archive also becomes a durable artifact: "here are the 400 distinct viable lifestyles this world produced," which is far more compelling than a single champion.
It also serves the LLM scientist (bd-16g.1): "explore this world" becomes a well-posed objective with a measurable coverage metric (archive fill %, QD-score).

DESIGN.
- The archive is an ANALYSIS/SELECTION layer, not new physics: cells keyed by discretized phenotype vector; each cell stores the elite genome + its provenance (run, tick, uid, lineage).
- Novelty score = mean distance to k nearest neighbors in behavior space (archive + current population). Selection modes must be explicit config, default OFF (pure legacy fitness) so parity runs are untouched.
- Determinism: the archive is updated at a fixed cadence in a fixed agent order; tie-breaking is by stable UID. Same seed -> same archive, byte-for-byte.
- Persist the archive to the run DB and export it (bd-2z0.5.6) so archives from different configs can be compared/merged offline (QD-score, coverage, and archive-diff are the headline metrics).
- Re-seeding: allow spawning agents FROM the archive ("resurrect the elites") — this makes the archive a reusable library of behaviors, and enables cross-run transfer experiments.

ACCEPTANCE. With selection_mode=novelty on a seed that provably converges under fitness (show the collapse in behavior-space coverage), archive coverage and QD-score are materially higher at equal tick budget, and the archive contains qualitatively distinct lifestyles (demonstrate with the phylogeny/behavior views). With selection_mode=fitness (default), digests are IDENTICAL to pre-feature runs — the feature must be provably inert when off.

TESTS + LOGGING (required).
- Unit: archive insertion/replacement rules (better elite replaces cell; ties broken by stable UID; cell discretization boundaries exact).
- Unit: novelty score against a hand-computed k-NN fixture.
- Unit (critical): with the feature disabled, the characterization digest is unchanged versus the pre-feature build — the "inert when off" proof.
- Determinism: same seed -> byte-identical archive contents and QD-score.
- E2E: two 20k-tick runs (fitness vs novelty) on the same seed, persist both archives, export, and assert coverage/QD-score deltas; log per-archive-update {tick, cell, uid, displaced_uid, novelty, fitness} at debug and a coverage/QD summary line at info every N ticks so the exploration curve is visible in the log.

title: Behavior-space definition, discretization, and archive storage/persistence
description:
SCOPE. The behavior descriptor, its discretization, the archive data structure, and its persistence. Nothing else: novelty scoring is bd-16g.6.2, QD metrics/export/resurrect is bd-16g.6.3. Proposed home: a new `qd` module inside scriptbots-core (AGENTS.md sets a very high bar for new files/crates — a module first, a crate only if a second consumer appears). Storage tables land in scriptbots-storage, through its existing writer.

WHY. Everything else in bd-16g.6 is a function of this: novelty is a distance in this space, QD-score is a sum over these cells, resurrection reads these genomes. It also feeds bd-16g.1 ("explore this world" becomes a measurable objective), bd-16g.3 (behavior clusters cross-check speciation), and bd-16g.12. If the descriptor is wrong, every downstream number is a confidently-reported artifact. Reuse the phenotype features bd-2z0.11.2 already defines — do NOT invent a second feature vector; the epic explicitly forbids three children each inventing their own.

DESIGN.
- `BehaviorSpaceV0 { version: u16, axes: Vec<Axis> }`, `Axis { name: &'static str, feature: PhenotypeFeature (bd-2z0.11.2), domain: (f32, f32), bins: u8 }`. Default axes: diet tendency, mean speed, spike-usage rate, give rate, sound usage, turn rate. The space is VERSIONED and stored with the archive — an archive whose axis definitions are not recoverable offline is scientific garbage.
- `BehaviorDescriptor([f32; D])` computed from an agent's ACCUMULATED lifetime statistics, never from one tick's state (an instantaneous descriptor is noise, and noise fills cells). Agents younger than `min_lifetime_ticks` (default 200) are NOT archive-eligible. Failure mode prevented: newborns with meaningless descriptors carpeting the grid and inflating coverage.
- Discretization: `fn cell_index(&BehaviorSpaceV0, &BehaviorDescriptor) -> Result<CellId, QdError>` — per-axis uniform HALF-OPEN bins [lo, hi), value clamped to the declared domain, boundary behavior exactly specified and tested. `CellId(u64)` packs bins (<= 256 bins/axis, D <= 8) so cells are `Ord`.
- `MapElitesArchive { space, cells: BTreeMap<CellId, ArchiveEntry> }`. BTreeMap, NOT HashMap — iteration order feeds coverage, export, and the digest; HashMap order is a determinism landmine that will not surface until CI runs on another machine.
- `ArchiveEntry { uid: AgentUid (bd-2z0.3.1), tick_inserted, descriptor, quality: f32, genome: GenomeBlob + genome_version (bd-2z0.3.2), provenance { run_id, parent_uid, generation } }`. Store the VERSIONED genome, never a live brain struct — a brain refactor must not orphan every archive we ever wrote.
- Insertion: replace the incumbent iff `quality > incumbent.quality`; on exact tie the LOWER uid wins (stable, and independent of iteration order). `quality` is an explicit, versioned config choice (lifetime intake | age at death | offspring count), default documented.
- Cadence and placement: archive maintenance runs every `archive_interval` ticks (default 100) at ONE fixed point in `WorldState::step` — after `stage_reproduction`, before `stage_record_history` — iterating agents in stable-uid order. Never inside `stage_brains` or any rayon reduction with unordered accumulation.

HARD REQUIREMENTS.
- ZERO RNG draws. `WorldState`'s RNG stream position is load-bearing (see the "preserve the historical RNG position of spawn_agent" comments in scriptbots-core). One stray `rng.random()` behind an `if archive_enabled` branch shifts every downstream draw and silently changes the world. The archive is an OBSERVER.
- Determinism: BTreeMap iteration, uid tie-breaks, index-order float summation. Same seed -> byte-identical serialized archive.
- No panics: empty archive, D=0, `domain.0 == domain.1`, NaN/inf descriptor -> typed `QdError`, never a panicking index or a silent bin 0.
- Bounds: reject a space with `prod(bins) > 1_000_000` in `ScriptBotsConfig::validate()`, not at tick 30k with an OOM. Genome blobs dominate memory — document bytes/cell and enforce a configured byte cap with an explicit error (no silent eviction: an archive that quietly forgets elites reports a coverage number that is a lie).

TESTS.
- Unit (binning table): value == domain.lo -> bin 0; value == domain.hi -> LAST bin, not out-of-range; below/above -> clamp; NaN -> typed error.
- Unit (insertion): strictly-better replaces; equal quality keeps the lower uid; worse never replaces; eligibility filter rejects agents younger than min_lifetime_ticks.
- Unit (NEGATIVE — the one that matters): a 5k-tick pinned-seed run with the archive ENABLED must produce a `characterization_digest_v0` byte-identical to the same run with it DISABLED, and identical to the checked-in pre-feature fixture digest. If enabling the archive changes the digest, the archive is touching world state or the RNG stream. This test exists to find exactly that bug.
- Determinism: two runs, same seed -> identical archive bytes; assert iteration yields CellIds in sorted order (the anti-HashMap regression).
- E2E: 20k-tick run with persistence -> reopen the DB -> reload the archive -> assert equality with the in-memory archive; assert the schema migration (V2 -> V3) leaves `ticks`/`metrics`/`events`/`replay_events` intact.
- NEGATIVE: a space configured past the cell cap fails at `validate()` with the cap named, before any allocation.

PERSISTENCE. New schema version const in scriptbots-storage (`SCRIPTBOTS_SCHEMA_V3`), written through the existing batch/outbox admission path — never a side-channel connection; the storage crate owns the writer lock. Tables: `archive_space(run_id, space_version, axes_json)` and `archive_cells(run_id, cell_id, uid, tick_inserted, quality, descriptor BLOB, genome BLOB, genome_version)`. Self-describing: an archive file plus its space row must be readable with no access to the build that wrote it.

LOGGING. Target `scriptbots::qd::archive`. debug per insertion {tick, cell_id, binned_axes, uid, quality, displaced_uid, displaced_quality}. info every 100 archive intervals {tick, filled_cells, total_cells, coverage_pct, mean_quality, max_quality}. warn ONCE when the eligibility filter rejects >90% of the population, and warn when an axis' observed values are entirely inside one bin — a mis-scaled axis domain is indistinguishable from "nothing is novel" unless the log says so. error on persistence rejection with run_id + batch id. A reviewer must be able to answer "why does uid 41 own cell (3,7,2)?" from the log alone.

title: Novelty score (k-NN in behavior space) and selection modes with inert-when-off proof
description:
SCOPE. The novelty score (k-NN in behavior space), the selection-mode plumbing that lets novelty actually influence who reproduces, and the "provably inert when off" proof. Consumes bd-16g.6.1's descriptors/archive. Does not own QD metrics or resurrection (bd-16g.6.3).

WHY. Without this, bd-16g.6.1 is a passive scrapbook. The parent bead's whole claim — "evolution that goes somewhere instead of converging" — lives or dies here. It is also the bead with the highest blast radius in the epic: it is the only one that reaches into `stage_reproduction`, i.e. into the RNG-ordered heart of the deterministic kernel. Every hard requirement below exists because that edit is the most dangerous one in bd-16g.6.

TWO CODE FACTS THAT CHANGE THE DESIGN (read before writing a line):
1. There is NO selection operator in ScriptBots. There is no generational GA, no tournament, no population-level fitness sort. Reproduction is a per-agent gate in `stage_reproduction`: energy above `reproduction_energy_threshold`, cooldown expired, attempt cadence fires, then a single RNG draw against `reproduction_attempt_chance` (clamped [0,1]). "selection_mode" therefore CANNOT be a selection operator — it must be a modulation of that gate. Writing it as a GA selection step would mean rewriting the kernel, which this bead must not do.
2. `SelectionMode` ALREADY EXISTS in scriptbots-core as the UI selection enum (Replace/Add/Clear, used by `SelectionUpdate`/`ControlCommand::UpdateSelection`).
