- Two runs, same seed and config: manifests are byte-identical outside the non-reproducible block. This is the test that makes "provenanced" mean something.
- A run that FAILS mid-way still leaves a manifest (see hard requirements).
- A dirty source tree produces `reproducible: false` and a warning naming the dirt — assert it, because a manifest that claims reproducibility it does not have is worse than no manifest.

LOGGING. info once at emit: {path, config_digest, root_seed, reproducible, warning_count}. warn if the manifest could not be written, naming why — and CONTINUE.
close_reason: main now writes run.manifest.json next to the run DB (after brains+seeding, before bootstrap ticks), carrying the resolved thread policy AND its deciding layer; failures warn and never kill the run; reproducible=false is logged loudly. E2E runs the real binary and asserts the manifest exists, records the actual seed, and that two identical runs agree on config digest.

title: Migrate the ~51 core RNG call sites onto domain streams (MOVES the characterization digest)
description:
SPLIT OUT OF bd-2z0.3.10 (2026-07-14). That bead had two halves: DECIDE the generator, and
IMPLEMENT versioned domain streams. The decision landed (fnp-random REJECTED — nightly-only, no
wasm32 support, and its only advantage is NumPy bit-parity that this project does not need; its
parity oracle is the legacy C++ ScriptBots). The SUBSTRATE landed in a7f25e4
(crates/scriptbots-core/src/rng_domains.rs: RngDomain, versioned FNV-1a derivation over a stable
domain tag, DomainStreams with per-domain checkpoint/restore, 7 tests incl. the headline
independence proof).

WHAT REMAINS: cutting the ~51 `self.rng` call sites in scriptbots-core over to their domains.

WHY IT IS A SEPARATE BEAD, and not laziness: the migration RE-BASELINES EVERY STOCHASTIC
DECISION and therefore MOVES THE CHARACTERIZATION DIGEST and WorldDigestV1. Burying a
science-wide re-baseline inside the commit that introduces the substrate would make it
unreviewable — nobody could tell which digest movement came from the new streams and which from
a mistake. Same reasoning that split bd-300o out of bd-16g.15.1.

THE WORK:
1. Assign each of the ~51 `self.rng` sites in crates/scriptbots-core/src/lib.rs to a domain.
   Grep `rg -n '&mut self\.rng|self\.rng\.' crates/scriptbots-core/src/lib.rs`. The obvious
   mapping, from the sites I read while building the substrate:
     - food scatter / regrowth                 -> RngDomain::Food
     - spawn placement, culling, population floor injection, random_spawn_position -> Population
     - partner/parent selection, random_key    -> Lineage
     - BrainRunner::mutate, AgentRuntime mutation rates -> Mutation
     - BrainRunner::crossover, the crossover_chance roll -> Crossover
     - interventions, terrain, weather         -> Environment
   DO NOT GUESS on the ambiguous ones. `AgentRuntime::new_random` (lib.rs ~11624, ~11775) is
   used both for seeding founders (Population) and for the discarded-runtime path — read each
   call site rather than pattern-matching on the function name.

2. Replace `WorldState::rng: SmallRngStream` with `DomainStreams`. Note `rng_before:
   self.rng.clone()` (~11706) captures the stream for replay/recovery — that becomes a
   DomainStreams clone, and the replay path must be updated in lockstep or recovery silently
   restores the wrong streams.

3. WorldDigestV1's `rng` lane currently encodes the single stream's checkpoint. It must encode
   ALL SIX domain checkpoints (DomainStreams::checkpoint() already returns them in a stable
   BTreeMap). If it does not, two worlds whose mutation streams are poised differently would
   digest identically — reintroducing, in a new place, exactly the blindness bd-2z0.3.9 removed.

4. RunManifestV1::random_stream is a single RandomStreamState. It must become the per-domain
   map, or a resumed run restores only one domain and silently re-rolls the other five.

5. THE ACCEPTANCE TEST, and it is the one that justifies the whole bead:
   Add a draw to ONE domain's code path (e.g. an extra food-scatter roll) and assert that the
   MUTATION lane of WorldDigestV1 is UNCHANGED across an otherwise identical run. That is the
   property the single-stream design cannot satisfy, and it is what makes controlled experiments
   possible. Without it, this migration is just moving code around.

6. RE-BASELINE DELIBERATELY: the digest WILL move. Record the before/after digests in the commit
   message so the move is a reviewed artifact rather than a mystery, and confirm no golden
   elsewhere in the repo is silently invalidated (as of today no pinned characterization-digest
   constants exist — verify that is still true before landing).

title: Wire the genome/provenance protocol into reproduction (it is built but UNUSED), then prove provenance end-to-end

comments.author: Jeff Emanuel
comments.text:
SCOPE WAS WRONG — CORRECTED BY INVESTIGATION (2026-07-13). I claimed this to write the provenance assertions and found there is NO PROVENANCE TO ASSERT. Not 'unasserted': UNPRODUCED.

WHAT I FOUND (verified by reading, not assumed):
1. `BrainProvenance` is NEVER CONSTRUCTED outside tests. `rg 'BrainProvenance::'` in core's non-test region returns nothing.
2. `register_family` is NEVER CALLED outside core. `rg 'register_family'` across the workspace, excluding core's own lib.rs, returns nothing. The family registry is never populated by any product code.
3. `stage_spawn_commit` — the path every offspring actually takes — uses `BrainRunner::clone_runner` / `crossover` / `mutate`. It never touches BrainGenomeEnvelope, never builds a BrainProvenance, never consults a family adapter.

SO THERE ARE TWO PARALLEL SYSTEMS:
  (a) BrainRunner (clone/mutate/crossover) — what reproduction ACTUALLY runs on. It works, and bd-2z0.3.6 now proves it (mutation off -> child genome bit-identical to parent; mutation on -> provably differs). It carries NO provenance.
  (b) BrainFamilyAdapter + BrainGenomeEnvelope + BrainProvenance + the family codecs (MlpBrainFamily, DwraonFamilyAdapter, AssemblyFamilyAdapter, all landed recently) — a complete, well-typed genome protocol that NOTHING WIRES UP.

CONSEQUENCE, and it is bigger than this bead: bd-16g.13.1 (genome browser / parent-child mutation diff) has NO GENOMES TO DIFF. bd-16g.3's phylogeny can draw edges but cannot say what happened along them. Any feature that consumes genome provenance is currently consuming a type that no run ever fills in.

REVISED SCOPE (the assertion is the LAST step, not the first):
  1. DECIDE, explicitly: does the BrainRunner path become the canonical one (and provenance rides on it), or does reproduction move onto the adapter/genome protocol? Both are defensible; picking neither leaves two systems and a permanent lie. Whoever owns bd-2z0.3.2's protocol should make this call — it is their design.
  2. WIRE the chosen path: register the families at startup (install_brains is the obvious place — it already installs the runner factories), and have the spawn path produce a genome envelope carrying BrainProvenance { parents: [Option<AgentUid>; 2], created_at }.
  3. ONLY THEN assert what this bead originally asked for: parent UIDs on crossover vs clone, genome hashes that actually change when the genome changes, OffspringStatePolicy honoured for BOTH Reset and Inherit, and a >=5-generation chain proving genomes keep evolving rather than converging on a placeholder.

I am RELEASING this bead rather than doing step 1 myself: the family adapters landed in the last few hours and whoever is building them is mid-flight in this area. Wiring it from the outside would collide with their design. Mailing them the finding.

title: Storage conformance test re-declares weakened schema copy; export SCRIPTBOTS_SCHEMA_V1 and consume it
description:
ROOT CAUSE (anchors at e2d9aaa, crates/scriptbots-storage/tests/frankensqlite_workload_conformance.rs:12-140): the workload-conformance suite re-declares a private, WEAKENED copy of the production schema — every NOT NULL and CHECK (x IN (0,1)) constraint stripped — plus its own copy of the 39-column agent INSERT. It therefore validates the fsqlite engine against a schema nobody ships, and silently drifts whenever SCRIPTBOTS_SCHEMA_V1 changes; the real constraints are only exercised by the in-crate unit test.

FIX:
1. Export the production DDL from the crate: pub const SCRIPTBOTS_SCHEMA_V1 (or a Storage::schema_sql() accessor) plus the canonical agent_insert_sql() column list, and make the conformance test consume those exports — delete-by-replacement of the local copies (in-place edit of the test file; no new files).
2. Add a constraint-enforcement probe to the conformance suite: after applying the real schema, attempt a direct INSERT violating a NOT NULL and one violating a CHECK; both must error (proving the engine enforces what production declares).
3. Keep the suite honest about what it gates: it opens the exact pinned fsqlite revision file-backed, closes, reopens, verifies committed data + integrity_check — those assertions stay untouched.

TESTS: the suite itself; plus one unit test in lib.rs asserting schema_sql() executes cleanly on :memory: and contains the expected table names, so the export cannot rot. LOGGING: conformance test logs each DDL batch it applies and row counts per table on the reopen pass, so CI failures localize without rerunning locally.
close_reason: Production schema and canonical agent INSERT are exported and consumed by FrankenSQLite conformance; constraints, reopen/integrity, row-count diagnostics, and migration-vs-export drift guard are covered. Same exact-source DSR runtime-storage-union6-f44c236 is fully green.

title: Design review: differential-drive turn rate ~10x below legacy (heading += (r-l)*speed/wheel_base vs C++ BOTSPEED*(w2-w1))
description:
DESIGN REVIEW — decide and implement one locomotion policy. Evidence (anchors at e2d9aaa vs original_scriptbots_code_for_reference/World.cpp:362-372):
- Legacy: BOTSPEED=0.3; each wheel's velocity rotates the bot about the OPPOSITE wheel contact point; net turn rate ~ BOTSPEED*(w2-w1) rad/tick (max ~0.3, ~17 deg/tick) and translation emerges from the two rotation applications.
- Rust stage_actuation: heading += (right-left)*bot_speed/wheel_base with wheel_base = 2*bot_radius = 20 -> max ~0.03 rad/tick (~1.7 deg/tick), 10x less agile, and translation is straight along the averaged heading (no rotate-about-wheel arc).
CONSEQUENCE: predators cannot execute legacy-style tight pursuit turns; evolved behavior differs qualitatively from the reference simulator; the README's faithful-port claim is materially weakened. This was flagged as "intentional-looking" by audit — the decision has never actually been made, which is exactly what this bead resolves.

OPTIONS: (A) restore legacy kinematics exactly, selectable via config (locomotion_model = "legacy" | "differential"), default legacy for parity — RECOMMENDED because parity is a core project promise and the differential model can stay for experiments; (B) keep differential drive but retune wheel_base so the angular-velocity envelope matches legacy (cheaper, still loses the rotate-about-wheel arc); (C) declare the divergence intentional and document it prominently in README + parity notes. Whichever option wins must be recorded in the bead comments with rationale.

IMPLEMENTATION NOTES (for option A): port World.cpp's exact two-rotation update into stage_actuation behind the config enum; keep torus wrapping; boost multiplies wheel speeds as today; the characterization trace constants in crates/scriptbots-app/src/lib.rs WILL change — re-pin them in the same commit with the rationale in the commit message (see e2d9aaa for the precedent and procedure).

TESTS (required): micro-oracle unit tests with 3-4 numeric cases hand-computed from World.cpp math (given w1,w2,angle,pos -> expected angle,pos within 1e-6); property tests: w1==w2 -> straight line, w1==-w2 -> pure rotation with position invariant to within float noise; e2e: seeded 500-tick run logging the |dheading|/tick distribution (mean, p95, max) via tracing, asserted against the legacy envelope (~0.3 rad max) when locomotion_model=legacy and against the differential envelope otherwise; determinism suite green after re-pinning.

title: Franken ecosystem deep-leverage program (asupersync spine, fsqlite depth, analytics quartet, FrankenTorch brains)
description:
CHARTER. Coordination epic for the 2026-07-12 franken-ecosystem leverage program: the outcome of a six-repo survey (rust_scriptbots architecture; asupersync; frankentorch+frankenjax; franken_numpy+frankenscipy; franken_networkx+frankenpandas; frankensqlite+frankensearch+frankentui). Goal: use the in-house franken libraries PROFOUNDLY where they fit and record principled skips where they do not. This epic owns no code; every leaf lives under the domain epic where it belongs (bd-16g.2 narrative, bd-2z0.8.9 fsqlite, bd-2z0.4 host runtime, bd-2z0.11 analytics, bd-2z0.3 brains, bd-2z0.8 dependency lane, bd-2z0.12 web, bd-2z0.13 docs) and is linked here as `related` for one-stop program discovery. Consult `br dep tree` on this bead to see the whole program.

CURRENT STATE (verified 2026-07-12). The ONLY direct franken dependency is fsqlite =0.1.16 (root Cargo.toml:48, default-features=false, features=["native"] — note `native` still transitively compiles the JSON/FTS5/R-tree extensions via fsqlite-core/native -> extensions). asupersync + franken-kernel/-evidence/-decision are in Cargo.lock only transitively via fsqlite. Everything else (fsci/fnx/fpandas/fnp/ftorch/ftui) has ZERO code presence; prior beads had already DECIDED direction in several areas but not implemented: bd-2z0.4.3 (CLOSED) selected asupersync =0.3.6 and the scriptbots-runtime crate layering; bd-2z0.6 owns the FrankenTUI Evolution Lab; bd-2z0.11.3 owns the fsci/fnx adapter decision; bd-2z0.3.10 owns the fnp-random RNG adapter decision; bd-2z0.5.6 owns Arrow/Parquet/CSV export contracts; bd-2z0.8.9 owns the fsqlite program; bd-2z0.8.7.1 adopts asupersync-native fastmcp_rust for MCP.

WHAT THIS PROGRAM ADDS (the genuine gaps; each is a new bead linked related):
1. fsqlite depth — FTS5+BM25 narrative search (already compiled into our binary, zero new deps); async-api (AsyncConnection + Cx) for control-plane reads; BEGIN CONCURRENT decision for archipelago-scale persistence; pin-record drift bug.
2. asupersync spine — channel spine (command bus, snapshot watch bus), region-owned background services + structured shutdown, LabRuntime deterministic chaos harness for the persistence protocol, Cx::scoped_cpu spike as a rayon alternative (upstream built it for exactly this consumer class), browser-runtime evaluation for scriptbots-web.
3. Analytics quartet — scriptbots-analytics crate + sb-analyze CLI; fsci-stats rigor layer (bootstrap CI, permutation tests) validating the narrative detectors; fnx lineage/interaction graph reports over the bd-16g.3.1 ancestry store; frankenpandas Parquet/Arrow/CSV export+summaries implementing bd-2z0.5.6 formats offline.
4. FrankenTorch brain family — batched cohort inference (BatchBrain), FtBrain with flat-genome weights (parameters_to_vector), optional hybrid lifetime gradient learning, benches + tournament entry (bd-16g.12).
5. Governance guards — license/rider audit (asupersync MIT + OpenAI/Anthropic no-rights rider is ALREADY transitively in our tree via fsqlite); wasm dependency-graph denylist guard; asupersync single-version-universe guard; perf budget regression gates.

KEY SURVEY FACTS FUTURE SELVES NEED:
- Toolchain: workspace already pins nightly-2026-07-09 (rust-toolchain.toml), so nightly-only franken deps are admissible.
- Publishing: crates.io — asupersync (0.3.5+), fnx-classes/fnx-algorithms 0.2.0, frankenpandas 0.1.2, ftui family 0.5.0. GIT-ONLY (pin exact revs): frankenscipy, franken_numpy, frankentorch, frankenjax, frankensearch. franken_networkx's GIT repo has a broken absolute-path dep (/dp/frankentui) in fnx-runtime — MUST consume from crates.io, never git.
- wasm32: NO franken numeric/graph/frame library supports wasm. Only asupersync (real BrowserRuntime incl. wasm-browser-deterministic profile) and fsqlite-wasm (experimental, in-memory) are wasm-capable. scriptbots-web builds core with default-features=false; every new native dep must follow the existing rayon/wide feature-gating pattern.
- Perf reality: franken value is in the SHELL (concurrency, storage, UI, analytics), NOT the tick hot loop. The hand-rolled wide::f32x4 stages + toroidal UniformGridIndex beat fsci KDTree (f64-only, Vec-per-point alloc, no torus) for per-tick queries. Keep detect.rs hand-rolled and bit-stable (f64::total_cmp) — fsci validates it OFFLINE, never replaces it.

PRINCIPLED SKIPS (recorded so we do not re-litigate):
- frankenjax: by its own README a verified reference implementation of jit/grad/vmap semantics, not an inner-loop engine; measured ~2.3-3.2us dispatch per jitted call; no optimizers; matmul only via primitive_with_params(Primitive::Dot). Wrong tool for thousands of 25x30 f32 forwards/tick. Revisit only if we ever need oracle-verified autodiff semantics.
- franken_numpy (general): UFuncArray stores flat Vec<f64> with dtype tag; perf campaign targets LARGE arrays + Python surface; fsci dominates for our slice-shaped stats. EXCEPTION: fnp-random (bit-exact NumPy PCG64DXSM parity) stays a live candidate under bd-2z0.3.10.
- frankensearch: hybrid Tantivy-BM25 + FSVI vector search with 2-tier embedders — but fsqlite FTS5 covers the lexical "what happened around tick N" need with ZERO new deps. Its high-level search API also lacks a filter parameter (only doc-id bitset filters truly prune), so tick-range filtering would need a wrapper anyway. Revisit for cross-run SEMANTIC search in the Lab UI if event volumes and querying needs grow.
- Hot-loop franken adoption of any kind: rejected (see perf reality above).

SEQUENCING. FTS5 (days, zero deps) and the pin-drift bug fix are immediate; asupersync spine beads follow the already-in-flight bd-2z0.4.x host work; analytics implementation waits on the bd-2z0.11.3 decision it feeds; FrankenTorch waits on the license gate + BatchBrain substrate; guards land alongside their first triggering integration. title: Build/test is broken on this checkout path: RCH refuses to offload, local link fails (no mold)
description:
SYMPTOM: every 'cargo test'/'cargo build' in this working copy fails with:
  clang: error: invalid linker name in argument '-fuse-ld=mold'

ROOT CAUSE (from 'rch diagnose'):
  Project path normalization failed for /Users/jemanuel/projects/rust_scriptbots:
  input resolves outside canonical root
  (resolved=/Users/jemanuel/projects/rust_scriptbots root=/Volumes/USBNVME16TB/data/projects)

RCH classifies the command correctly (CargoTest, confidence 0.95 >= 0.85, 'WOULD
INTERCEPT'), selects a worker, and then FAILS path normalization and falls back to a
LOCAL build. The local build cannot succeed: .cargo/config.toml sets
target = x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu with -fuse-ld=mold, and this is an aarch64 macOS
host with no mold installed. Even if it linked, the product would be a Linux ELF that
cannot execute here. So ALL testing in this repo depends on RCH offload working.

THE PATH TOPOLOGY IS INCONSISTENT:
  /data -> /Volumes/USBNVME16TB/data      (rch canonical_root = /data/projects)
  /dp   -> /Users/jemanuel/projects        (rch alias_root = /dp)
The repo exists ONLY under /dp (= /Users/jemanuel/projects/rust_scriptbots). There is
no /data/projects/rust_scriptbots. RCH canonicalizes the cwd, so invoking cargo from
the /dp spelling does not help — it realpaths straight back to /Users/... and is
rejected. 'rch exec -- cargo ...' fails the same way.

WHO IS AFFECTED: everyone working in this checkout. Other agents' cargo processes were
observed holding the build-directory lock and would hit the same wall.

WORKAROUND I USED (changes NO config, repo or global):
  CARGO_BUILD_TARGET=aarch64-apple-darwin CARGO_TARGET_DIR=<scratch> cargo test -p <crate>
This builds natively for the host and links with the system linker. scriptbots-core is
pure Rust and passes fully this way (191 tests, clippy -D warnings clean).
CAVEAT, and it matters: ~34 scriptbots-storage tests FAIL under this workaround —
process-exit/durability/file-lock tests that depend on platform semantics (e.g.
'child did not exit at the requested admitted boundary', 101 vs 86). I verified those
failures reproduce on a CLEAN TREE, so they are an artifact of the native target and
NOT a regression. Do not use this workaround to certify storage.

FIX OPTIONS (a human should choose; I did not want to rewrite the user's global tool
config or the shared .cargo/config.toml, both of which have blast radius beyond one task):
  (a) point RCH's path topology at the real checkout root, or
  (b) move/mirror the checkout under /data/projects so it sits inside canonical_root, or
  (c) install mold + a native linker profile so local builds work without RCH.

Until this is resolved, NOTHING in this repo can be certified on its canonical target.

comments.author: GoldenPanther
comments.text:
SHARPER DIAGNOSIS (GoldenPanther, 2026-07-13). I tested the fix I proposed and it is
WRONG. Correcting the record before anyone builds on it.

WHAT I DID: `.rch/config.toml` is project-scoped and OUTRANKS the user config, so I set
    [path_topology]
    canonical_root = "/Users/jemanuel/projects"
and re-ran. Path normalization then SUCCEEDED — `rch diagnose` stopped warning, RCH
selected a worker (vmi1152480) and started the transfer pipeline. So normalization was
indeed the first wall, and this does clear it.

BUT IT REVEALS THE REAL SEMANTICS AND BREAKS THE NEXT STAGE:

    rsync: [generator] failed to set times on
      "/Users/jemanuel/projects/rust_scriptbots/ci/fixtures": Operation not permitted (1)
    rsync error: some files/attrs were not transferred (code 23)
    Remote execution failed: Project sync failed: rsync failed, running locally

`canonical_root` is the REMOTE path root ON THE LINUX WORKERS, not a local directory.
Pointing it at the local checkout makes RCH try to rsync the project INTO
/Users/jemanuel/projects/... ON THE WORKER, which it cannot create/chtimes. So the
"fix" trades a fast failure for a slow one: every build would now burn ~40s on a doomed
rsync before falling back to the same unlinkable local build. That is strictly worse, so
I REMOVED the file. The tree is back exactly as it was (canonical_root = /data/projects).

WHY THE OTHER PROJECTS WORK: they live under /data/projects (-> /Volumes/USBNVME16TB/data
/projects). Their realpath lands inside the resolved canonical root, so normalization
passes AND the remote destination is the path the workers actually expect. Our repo is
the outlier: it sits at /Users/jemanuel/projects/rust_scriptbots.

THE SYMLINKS ARE INCONSISTENT WITH RCH'S MODEL, AND THAT IS THE BUG:
    /data -> /Volumes/USBNVME16TB/data       (canonical_root = /data/projects)
    /dp   -> /Users/jemanuel/projects        (alias_root = /dp)
For RCH's alias mechanism to mean anything, /dp should resolve INTO /data/projects. It
does not — it points at the home directory instead. RCH canonicalizes the cwd via
realpath, so invoking cargo from the /dp spelling cannot help: it resolves straight back
to /Users/... and is rejected. Both symlinks are dated 2026-07-11, so this likely broke
when projects were moved off the USB volume.

SO THE VIABLE FIXES ARE (a human should choose):
  1. Move/mirror this checkout under /data/projects (i.e. onto the USB volume) so it sits
     inside the canonical root, like every project that currently offloads successfully.
     This is the option most consistent with how RCH is already configured and working.
  2. Repoint /dp -> /data/projects and relocate the checkout accordingly.
  3. Teach RCH a local->remote path MAPPING (distinct from a shared root) so a checkout
     outside canonical_root can still be synced to the correct remote destination. This is
     an RCH feature question, not a config one.
  4. Install mold + a native linker profile so local builds work without RCH at all.

DO NOT do what I tried (overriding canonical_root to the local path). It clears

title: wasm-vs-native parity test runs both sides in wasm runtime with mismatched config; compare against committed native fixture
description:
ROOT CAUSE (anchors at e2d9aaa, crates/scriptbots-web/src/lib.rs ~620-724): the "wasm-vs-native parity" test is only half-meaningful. (a) Config mismatch: the reference world is built from a raw config with default population_spawn_interval=100 while the harness SimSpec::config() zeroes it; every case runs <=64 ticks so stage_population never fires and the mismatch stays invisible — extend past 100 ticks and one side spawns agents the other does not. (b) Both the "native" and "wasm" sides execute inside the same wasm test runtime (wasm_bindgen_test_configure!(run_in_browser)), so the test proves same-runtime determinism of the wrapper, NOT cross-architecture parity; native<->wasm float divergence (libm sin/cos/atan2/powf differ across platforms) is structurally undetectable.

FIX:
1. Use SimSpec::config() for BOTH sides so the scenario is identical, and extend at least one case to >=150 ticks so population spawning is exercised.
2. Add a committed native-generated fixture: a native-only (#[cfg(not(target_arch = "wasm32"))]) test/generator in scriptbots-web that runs pinned seeds and serializes postcard snapshots at ticks {1, 8, 64, 150} to tests/fixtures/native_parity_v1.postcard. The wasm CI test deserializes the committed fixture and compares against wasm-computed snapshots.
3. Comparison policy: per-agent position/velocity/heading/energy with explicit tolerance (start 1e-5); on mismatch, log the FIRST diverging tick, agent index, field name, both values, absolute delta, and the config hash — enough to diagnose from CI output alone. If genuine libm divergence appears, the deliverable becomes a documented per-field tolerance policy (recorded in the fixture header), not a silent loosening.
4. Document fixture regeneration in the test file header (exact cargo command + when regeneration is legitimate: only after intentional semantic changes, in the same commit, with the digest-change rationale).

TESTS: this bead IS a test bead; acceptance = wasm CI job red when a wasm-side semantic divergence is injected (verify once by temporarily perturbing a constant locally), green on the committed fixture, and the failure output contains the full divergence report described above.
DEPENDS/RELATED: coordinate with bd-2z0.12.1 (renderer-neutral WASM snapshot projection) — if the snapshot schema moves, regenerate fixture v2 rather than mutating v1.

title: Define auto-tune, low-power, and user-config precedence
description: Make startup configuration precedence explicit and reproducible across defaults, scenario files, environment, CLI, low-power mode, auto-tune probe children, and final runs. Explicit user values must not be silently overwritten, and the resolved policy must be present in run provenance.
acceptance_criteria: A table-driven matrix covers defaults, scenario, environment, CLI, low-power, auto-tune probe children, and final-run layering; explicit user values win according to the documented order and are never silently reset; probe overrides cannot leak into the final run; the resolved values and source layer are recorded in RunManifestV0; deterministic tests cover conflicting and absent values.
close_reason: Landed 281ee9b (precedence) + 88a7d04 (manifest records it). The fourth criterion — config-layering (defaults -> scenario file -> env -> CLI) — is a distinct surface and is split to bd-1n2p rather than being closed on the strength of the other three. WHAT LANDED: a real bug is fixed (an exported SCRIPTBOTS_MAX_THREADS=16 was silently overwritten by --low-power's 2, with no warning and no record); precedence is now one pure function with an explicit order and an 8-case matrix; the auto-tune probe RECOMMENDS rather than decides, so a probe child's tuning cannot leak into a run whose operator already chose; declined layers are reported rather than dropped; and the manifest now records the RESOLVED policy — the count, the LAYER that decided (cli-flag/environment/auto-tune/low-power-default/builtin-default), and the layer that was DECLINED. That last part closes the criterion I previously could not: when I first worked this bead the binary emitted no manifest at all, so a thread_policy field would have recorded nothing; bd-28yt then wired emission into startup, which unblocked it. Proven e2e through the real binary, not a unit test of the resolver. TWO DEFECTS FOUND WHILE TESTING, both filed: (1) bd-15c8 — FrankenSQLite refuses to open a database on exFAT, which is what external drives are formatted as; proven by flipping TMPDIR from exFAT to APFS and watching the same tests go 0/4 -> 4/4 with no code change. This also CORRECTS THE RECORD: several of us have been writing these storage failures off as an 'aarch64 target artifact', and that diagnosis was wrong — the filesystem is the variable, and real regressions could be hiding behind that excuse. (2) bd-3p7i — the manifest's environment capture is clobbered by our own unsafe set_var, so it reports the resolved value rather than what the user exported and cannot evidence an override at all; that is exactly why thread_policy had to exist. clippy -D warnings clean; 4/4 e2e green.

comments.author: Jeff Emanuel
comments.text: Partial landing at commit e2d9aaa (2026-07-12, GoldenPanther): the silent override where --low-power clobbered auto-tune's SCRIPTBOTS_MAX_THREADS selection is fixed (threads_set_by_auto_tune latch; explicit --threads still wins over both). The broader precedence contract (defaults < scenario files < env < CLI, documented auto-tune/low-power interaction, reproducible probe children) remains this bead's deliverable.

comments.author: Jeff Emanuel
comments.text:
PART 1 LANDED (281ee9b). Bead stays OPEN — two of the four acceptance criteria are done, two are not, and closing on the other two would be exactly the ceremonial dishonesty bd-2z0.1.4 just removed.

DONE:
- A REAL BUG IS FIXED. A user who exported SCRIPTBOTS_MAX_THREADS=16 and passed --low-power had their explicit value silently overwritten with 2. No warning, no record. Cause: the thread count was decided by a chain of if/else-if branches scattered through startup, each writing into a process-global env var, so the winner was whichever branch ran LAST rather than the layer the user most explicitly stated.
- PRECEDENCE IS NOW EXPLICIT, in one pure function (crates/scriptbots-app/src/precedence.rs): --threads > SCRIPTBOTS_MAX_THREADS > auto-tune > --low-power > builtin. The organising rule: a layer naming a SPECIFIC VALUE beats a layer expressing a PREFERENCE about defaults. --low-power is a MODE that fills in a knob the user did not set; it does not overrule one they did.
- PROBE CONTAINMENT: the auto-tune probe now RECOMMENDS rather than decides (main.rs no longer set_vars from the probe). Evidence must not overrule an instruction, and that is precisely what stops a probe child's tuning leaking into a final run whose operator already decided. Tested.
- DECLINED LAYERS ARE REPORTED, not silently dropped (ThreadPolicy::overridden + a log line).
- TABLE-DRIVEN MATRIX: 8 cases over CLI/env/auto-tune/low-power/default incl. every conflict and the absent-value case, plus tests for probe containment, declined-layer reporting, and purity.

REMAINING SCOPE (why this bead is not closed):
1. SCENARIO-FILE AND CLI CONFIG LAYERING IS NOT COVERED. The matrix covers the THREAD knob's layers. The brief also asks for defaults -> scenario file -> environment -> CLI layering over the config itself (load_config_layer / merge path). That is a distinct surface and deserves its own matrix.
2. THE MANIFEST DOES NOT RECORD THE RESOLVED POLICY, because main.rs NEVER EMITS A RUN MANIFEST AT ALL. RunManifestV0::from_world is currently only constructed from tests and tooling — I verified this rather than assuming it. Adding a thread_policy field would therefore record nothing for real runs; the actual gap is that the manifest emission path is not wired into startup, which is a bigger and separate problem than precedence. Recommend splitting it out rather than pretending a field satisfies the criterion.

FINDING FOR WHOEVER PICKS THIS UP: the startup path mutates process-global env vars with unsafe set_var to communicate decisions to the Rayon pool builder in core. That is a workable channel but a poor one (it is unsafe in Rust 2024 precisely because it races with other threads). If HostCore (bd-2z0.4.5) lands a sole-owner config path, the thread policy should travel through it as a value rather than through the environment.

comments.author: Jeff Emanuel
comments.text:
CLOSED. All four elements of the brief are satisfied; two were already true and two were ceremonial.

1. INSPECT RENDERED TERMINAL BUFFERS - DONE. run_headless_frames always drew into a real ratatui TestBackend and then THREW THE BUFFER AWAY. Nothing read it, so the draw could have been a no-op while the test passed on the strength of the simulation having ticked. The buffer is now inspectable and a new test asserts the HUD panel and status line were painted, that >200 cells are non-blank, and that the tick shown is THIS world's tick (a HUD rendering a plausible screen for the WRONG world is worse than one rendering nothing).

2. DISTINGUISH CPU SURROGATE FROM LIVE FRAMEBUFFER - DONE. wgpu_capture_smoke/agents asserted only that a PNG existed and that its FILE LENGTH was > 0. A PNG of a solid black frame passes both. Worse, both are named wgpu_* and both run green on a headless box with NO GPU - i.e. llvmpipe, a CPU rasterizer, was doing the drawing (new_for_capture_test quietly sets allow_software_adapter). The compositor always knew which adapter it picked and never told anyone; it now reports it, and every failure message names the surface that actually rasterized.

3. FAIL REPLAY VERIFICATION ON EMPTY EVIDENCE - ALREADY TRUE. require_non_vacuous_replay (main.rs:1755) is wired into the real path at main.rs:1680 and refuses a vacuous nonzero run. Verified rather than assumed; no change needed.

4. RENAME TESTS THAT OVERCLAIM - DONE. wgpu_capture_smoke -> a_captured_terrain_frame_is_actually_rasterized_and_not_merely_written; wgpu_capture_agents -> both_agents_are_rasterized_into_the_frame_at_the_positions_they_were_given.

A FINDING WORTH RECORDING: my first version of the agents test demanded the agent's literal input colour at its centre pixel, and it FAILED - but the renderer was right and my test was wrong. The agents carry glow and selection, so the red agent lands on screen as a washed pink [255,188,175], not [255,64,51]. Rather than reverse-engineer the blend (which would have been a test of the shader's arithmetic, not of whether the agent was drawn), the test now renders the SAME scene with the agents removed and requires the frames to differ near each agent AND to be identical in a far corner. If the agent-drawing path were deleted the frames would be identical - the one thing the old test could never notice.

BOTH NEW ALARMS ARE PROVEN TO FIRE: two tests construct exactly the artifacts the old assertions would have accepted (a uniform black image; an untouched terminal buffer) and prove the new detectors reject them. An evidence check nobody has watched fail is a check nobody knows works.

comments.author: Jeff Emanuel
comments.text: CONFIRMED IN PRACTICE (2026-07-12, GoldenPanther) with a concrete failure: bv reads .beads/beads.jsonl while br exports to .beads/issues.jsonl. At the time of writing, beads.jsonl was 146 BYTES and contained ZERO of the 153 issues in the br database — so 'bv --robot-triage' cheerfully reported open_count=100 and 'bv --robot-insights' reported Cycles: none, both computed from an essentially EMPTY graph. This is worse than a stale number: bv's cycle check silently passes because there is nothing to check, so an agent that validates a new dependency graph with bv gets a false green. I worked around it by copying issues.jsonl -> <tmp>/.beads/beads.jsonl and running 'bv --db <tmp>/.beads' (which then saw all 153 beads, 133 open, 45 actionable, no cycles — the real answer). FIX SHAPE: make br export write the file bv reads (or make bv read issues.jsonl / accept the br DB directly), and add a guard so bv REFUSES to emit metrics when its snapshot's bead count is implausibly smaller than the DB's (a silent empty-graph green is the dangerous case, not the stale-by-one case). Suggested test: create N beads via br, run bv --robot-insights, assert bead_count matches; and assert bv errors (not passes) when handed an empty/missing snapshot.

description:
WHY. bd-2z0.11.1/.11.2/.11.3 and bd-16g.1.4 all need a HOME: an offline analytics layer that reads finished run DBs and produces reports. Today the only offline consumer is control_cli's Export subcommand (crates/scriptbots-app/src/bin/control_cli.rs:85-134), which reads the run DB DIRECTLY via --db — exactly the direct-database-access-from-app-binaries pattern bd-2z0.8.9.5 exists to remove. A dedicated analytics crate fixes both problems at once: it becomes the ONE blessed offline DB reader (read-only, identity-verified), and the franken analytics adapters (fsci-stats, fnx, frankenpandas) get a home outside the default product build (plan build budgets: default TUI/server product must not compile heavy deps) and outside the wasm graph entirely.

SCOPE (scaffold only — NO franken deps in this bead; that keeps it unblocked by license/decision gates).
- New workspace member crates/scriptbots-analytics: library + bin sb-analyze. Depends on scriptbots-storage (StorageReader / read-only open) + existing workspace deps only.
- Report framework: a Report trait (name, description, run(&ReaderCtx, &Params) -> ReportOutput), registry, and output sinks (human markdown, machine JSON with stable schema + schema_version field from day one). Per-stage tracing timings baked into the framework so every future report gets logging for free.
- CLI: sb-analyze <run.db> list | run <report> [--params k=v] [--json out.json] [--md out.md]. Read-only DB open with identity verification (reuse open_existing_with_expected_identity semantics, storage lib.rs:2496).
- First two zero-new-dep reports to prove the frame: run-summary (ticks, population trajectory stats via existing Welford-style math) and narrative-timeline dump (EventRecords ordered, honoring the FTS bead when present, plain scan otherwise).
- Cargo discipline: crate is a workspace member but NOT a dependency of scriptbots-app; cargo builds it only when asked (per-binary dep graphs) so default product build budgets are untouched. Assert via the wasm/build-budget guard bead.
- Migration path for control_cli Export: once sb-analyze covers its dataset kinds, control_cli's direct-DB Export should delegate or deprecate in favor of sb-analyze (coordinate with bd-2z0.8.9.5 — do not delete anything here; just record the successor path).
TESTS. Unit: report registry, param parsing, JSON schema snapshots, read-only enforcement (attempt a write -> typed error). Integration: run against a fixture DB checked in under testdata (small, generated by a seeded headless run, regeneration script included). Logging: per-report begin/end spans with row counts and durations; --verbose flows to tracing filter.
ACCEPTANCE. sb-analyze list/run works on a fixture DB; CI compiles + tests the crate; default-product build time measurably unchanged (record before/after).
DEPS. None hard (deliberately); related bd-2z0.11.3, bd-2z0.5.6, bd-16g.1.4, bd-2z0.8.9.5.

title: fsci-stats rigor layer: bootstrap CIs, permutation tests, distribution fits for detector validation
description:
WHY. The narrative detector kernel (crates/scriptbots-core/src/detect.rs: two-sided CUSUM :181, threshold :288, regime slope/autocorr :447, bimodality :603) is deliberately hand-rolled, bit-stable (f64::total_cmp), and ONLINE. What it lacks is statistical CERTIFICATION: is that detected regime change real or noise? What is the effect size CI? bd-16g.2.3 sets a false-positive budget and bd-16g.1.4 wants effect sizes with CIs over matched-seed runs — both need real statistics machinery. frankenscipy's fsci-stats is the strongest analytics fit in the whole franken family for us: Rust-native free functions over &[f64] (describe/percentile/histogram/zscore/iqr...), 95+ continuous distributions with pdf/cdf/ppf/fit, hypothesis tests (t/KS/Mann-Whitney/Wilcoxon/ANOVA), bootstrap, gaussian_kde, QMC; std::thread::scope parallelism explicitly work-gated so small-n inputs stay serial (their trait docs record parallel being 7-9x SLOWER at n~4096 — they gate correctly); #![forbid(unsafe_code)]; no tokio/rayon anywhere.

HARD BOUNDARY (do not cross): detect.rs stays hand-rolled, online, bit-stable in core. fsci NEVER enters scriptbots-core or any tick path. This bead is OFFLINE validation in scriptbots-analytics that ANNOTATES events after the fact.

INTEGRATION FACTS. Git-only dependency (NOT on crates.io) — pin exact rev per the bd-2z0.8 protocol; nightly-only (std::simd) — fine, workspace pins nightly-2026-07-09; all APIs are f64 (our f32 metric series widen at the boundary — cheap, offline).

SCOPE (reports in scriptbots-analytics, feature "fsci" if isolation proves useful).
1. narrative-validate report: for each persisted EventRecord, block-bootstrap CI (autocorrelation-aware) on the before/after delta of its metric window; permutation test against a stationary null; emit annotated JSON (event + p-value + CI + effect size) and a markdown table. This directly serves bd-16g.2.3's false-positive budget with a principled method instead of eyeballed thresholds.
2. distribution-report: population/energy/trait histograms with fitted candidate distributions (normal/lognormal/gamma where sensible), KS goodness-of-fit, bimodality cross-check against detect.rs's score (agreement rate logged — divergence is interesting, not an error).
3. matched-seed effect sizes for bd-16g.1.4: given two run DBs (control/treatment), paired effect sizes with bootstrap CIs per metric — the exact statistical core bd-16g.1.4 needs, exposed as a report it can call.
TESTS. Golden tests on synthetic series with KNOWN ground truth (injected step change of known size: CI must cover truth >=94% over 200 seeded replications — log the coverage number); permutation p-value calibration under pure-null series (uniformity check); f32->f64 widening roundtrip sanity; fixture-DB integration run. Every report logs sample sizes, method params (block length, n_resamples), and wall time.
ACCEPTANCE. narrative-validate + distribution-report + effect-size report run on fixture DBs in CI; coverage/calibration tests green; zero fsci symbols in any default-product or wasm build graph (guard bead enforces).
DEPS. Blocked by: analytics scaffold, bd-2z0.11.3 (the formal adapter decision this evidence feeds — implement behind it), license audit bead. Related: bd-16g.2.3, bd-16g.1.4.

title: fnx lineage and interaction graph reports (components, communities, centrality)
description:
WHY. Evolution runs are GRAPHS: the ancestry DAG (who descends from whom) and interaction networks (who fights/feeds whom). bd-16g.3.1 builds the ancestry substrate (stable-UID edge list, append-only persistence, offline rebuild); bd-2z0.11.1 wants lineage fitness and founder contribution. franken_networkx gives us NetworkX-parity algorithms in Rust: connected/weakly-connected components, Louvain + label-propagation + greedy-modularity communities, full centrality suite (degree/closeness/betweenness/eigenvector/Katz/PageRank/HITS), Dijkstra/Bellman-Ford/A*, all with NetworkX-identical semantics (their conformance gate diffs against real NetworkX).

INTEGRATION FACTS (survey 2026-07-12, do not re-derive):
- CONSUME FROM CRATES.IO ONLY: fnx-classes = "0.2.0", fnx-algorithms = "0.2.0" (published 2026-06-21). The GIT repo is UNUSABLE as a dependency: fnx-runtime declares an optional dep with an absolute local path (/dp/frankentui) that breaks resolution on any machine without that path. crates.io releases strip path deps.
- Node keys are String (attrs BTreeMap) — integer agent UIDs must be formatted; budget one O(V) format pass per rebuild, fine offline.
- Bulk-build with extend_edges_unrecorded (reserves capacity, skips per-edge policy recording) — NEVER add_edge in a loop for full-graph builds.
- fnx-algorithms hard-depends on rayon: acceptable (analytics crate is native-only, never wasm).
- Their own cost model: break-even ~100 nodes; algorithms convert String labels to dense indices per call (one O(V) pass). Our graphs (1k-100k nodes, built once per report) are squarely in the win zone.

SCOPE (reports in scriptbots-analytics).
1. lineage-structure: from the bd-16g.3.1 ancestry store (or directly from births/deaths tables until it lands — births carry parent_a/parent_b, core lib.rs:1553): weakly-connected components = founder families; per-founder descendant counts, extinction depth, surviving-lineage table. Feeds bd-2z0.11.1's fitness math with the structural layer.
2. dynasty-communities: Louvain over the mating/ancestry graph (seeded, resolution param exposed) — candidate "species/dynasty" clusters to cross-check bd-16g.3.2's online speciation clustering (agreement rate logged, divergence is signal).
3. interaction-centrality: build per-epoch interaction graphs from combat/food-share events IF per-pair interaction data is persisted; TODAY the events table stores per-kind counts only (storage lib.rs V1 schema), so this report starts with what replay_events JSON provides and this bead documents exactly what extra persistence (pairwise interaction rows) would unlock — file a follow-up storage bead rather than silently widening scope here.
4. Graph exports: GraphML/edge-list dumps for external tooling.
TESTS. Golden: hand-built mini genealogy (3 founders, known components/communities) asserts exact fnx outputs; determinism: seeded Louvain stable across runs; scale smoke: 100k-edge synthetic DAG under time budget (log build/convert/algorithm timings separately — the String-key tax must be visible in logs). Fixture-DB integration in CI.

title: frankenpandas export and summary layer: Parquet/Arrow/CSV + groupby-rolling run summaries
description:
WHY. bd-2z0.5.6 defines provenance-rich Arrow/Parquet/CSV export CONTRACTS for run/agent/lineage/event/metric data. Something must implement the offline half for analysts, and hand-rolling Parquet writers + groupby/rolling summary math is exactly the wheel frankenpandas already built: DataFrame/Series with pandas-parity semantics, groupby (3 execution paths, measured 2.2-4.3x faster than pandas 2.2.3 at 100k-1M rows on accepted workloads), rolling/expanding/ewm/resample, joins incl. merge_asof, and fp-io with full CSV option matrix + Parquet/Arrow IPC/JSONL.

HONESTY CLAUSE (from their own artifacts, record and respect): their perf scorecard marks overall release readiness "PARTIAL / NOT FULLY VALIDATED" (high-CV rows rejected). We are consuming SEMANTICS (index alignment, NaN rules, format IO), not chasing their benchmarks. If a workload is slow, fsqlite SQL remains our query engine — the boundary is: FrankenSQLite = query engine, frankenpandas = interchange + summary-shaping layer. Never re-implement SQL-shaped queries as DataFrame pipelines.

INTEGRATION FACTS. crates.io: frankenpandas = "0.1.2" (umbrella with prelude) — or the leaner fp-frame + fp-groupby + fp-io if the umbrella's default features drag rusqlite (bundled C) — MEASURE and pick the minimal set; disable default sql-sqlite feature regardless (we have fsqlite; a second embedded SQLite in the tree is absurd). No tokio (explicit upstream policy). Native-only (analytics crate; never wasm).

SCOPE (in scriptbots-analytics).
1. sb-analyze export: read run DB -> write Parquet/Arrow/CSV per the bd-2z0.5.6 contract (schema_version + provenance columns: run identity digest, seed, config hash, exporter version). Column layouts defined WITH .5.6, not invented here — if .5.6's contract work has not started, this bead contributes the draft schema and .5.6 reviews/owns it.
2. sb-analyze summarize: per-epoch groupby aggregates (population by diet/brain-kind, trait means/stds), rolling-window smoothed metric series, per-lineage aggregates joined from births/deaths — emitted as small tidy DataFrames -> Parquet/CSV + markdown tables.
3. Round-trip verification mode: export then re-read, assert frame equality (this is our conformance net against fp-io bugs).
TESTS. Golden CSVs for tiny fixture DBs; Parquet round-trip equality incl. nulls/NaN policy (document the NaN convention explicitly — pandas semantics differ from naive expectations); dtype stability snapshots; large-ish smoke (1M metric rows) with stage timings logged; cross-check one summary against a plain SQL computation of the same aggregate (agreement = conformance evidence).
ACCEPTANCE. Export + summarize + round-trip green on fixture DB in CI; minimal feature set recorded in the bead on close (with cargo tree evidence); provenance columns match .5.6 contract; NaN/null policy documented in docs/analytics.
DEPS. Blocked by: analytics scaffold, bd-2z0.5.6 (contract), license audit. Related: bd-2z0.11.3, control_cli CSV export (supersedes it for offline use; control_cli keeps its REST-based export for live instances).

title: Analytics E2E: seeded run -> full report suite -> ground-truth invariant assertions
description:
WHY. Each analytics report has unit/golden tests, but the product promise is the PIPELINE: simulate -> persist -> analyze -> report, with numbers a scientist can trust. This bead is the end-to-end proof with ground truth planted where we control it.

SCOPE. scripts/e2e_analytics.sh (+ a small Rust driver where shell is too weak), VERBOSE logging at every stage, CI (extended/nightly lane — it is heavier than PR CI):
1. Run a seeded headless sim to T ticks with a scenario CHOSEN TO GUARANTEE structure: an injected mid-run food-scarcity step (via config schedule or intervention command once bd-16g.10.1 lands; until then pick a seed empirically exhibiting a population crash and pin it) => known regime-change ground truth window.
2. sb-analyze run-summary + narrative-timeline: assert the crash event exists in the window, human_text matches expectation.
3. narrative-validate (fsci): assert the planted change is flagged significant (p < 0.01) AND at least one pure-noise stretch is NOT flagged (false-positive control demonstrated in-pipeline).
4. lineage-structure (fnx): assert founder-component count == initial spawn cohorts; descendant counts sum to total births from the DB (exact accounting identity).
5. export (frankenpandas): Parquet round-trip equality; row counts match SQL counts exactly.
6. FTS surface: control_cli narrative search for the planted event returns it (ties the narrative-search e2e into the same artifact).
7. Emit a single MANIFEST.json artifact: every stage, duration, pass/fail, log paths — the CI artifact a human opens first.
FAILURE POLICY. Any stage failure fails the job loudly with the stage log inlined in CI output; flaky-seed drift (the pinned seed stops crashing after a legit sim-physics change) is handled by a documented re-pinning procedure IN the script header, not by silent tolerance widening.
ACCEPTANCE. Green in the extended CI lane 10 consecutive runs; MANIFEST.json artifact present; re-pinning procedure documented.
DEPS. Blocked by: fsci rigor bead, fnx graphs bead, frankenpandas export bead (and transitively the scaffold + FTS beads).

title: Evaluate asupersync BrowserRuntime (deterministic profile) for scriptbots-web
description:
CONTEXT. scriptbots-web is a minimal wasm build (core+brain only, default-features=false so no rayon/wide; JS drives stepping over Rc<RefCell<WorldState>>; snapshots via serde-wasm-bindgen JSON or postcard — crates/scriptbots-web/src/lib.rs:132-560). asupersync is the ONLY franken library with real wasm32 support: target_arch=wasm32 requires exactly one browser profile feature (wasm-browser-minimal|dev|prod|deterministic); native Runtime::build errors on wasm and routes to BrowserRuntime with a BrowserReactor; sibling crates asupersync-browser-core (canonical wasm-bindgen boundary) and a live wasm demo exist. The wasm-browser-deterministic profile keeps replay-safe semantics IN THE BROWSER.

WHY IT COULD MATTER. (a) Deterministic browser scheduling aligns with fork-this-world/replay ambitions (bd-16g.8.2 needs honest determinism claims in the browser); (b) a structured runtime replaces ad-hoc JS-driven stepping with budgeted ticks + cancellable background work if the web build grows (workers, streaming snapshots); (c) it would UNIFY the concurrency model native/web instead of maintaining two idioms.

SCOPE (evaluation, not adoption).
- Spike: drive the existing WasmSim stepping through BrowserRuntime with the deterministic profile in a branch; measure bundle-size delta, startup cost, tick-pacing fidelity vs the current rAF/JS loop; confirm the profile's determinism claims hold for our stepping pattern (seeded run digest equality across two browser sessions).
- Map which spine conventions (watch snapshot bus, shutdown watch) could share code between native and web via feature gates.
- DECISION RULE: adopt only if bundle-size cost <= ~15% and determinism digests hold; otherwise document and close rejected. Either way, record findings for the PLAN_TO_CREATE_SIBLING_APP_CRATE_TARGETING_WASM.md successor work.
TESTS if adopted: browser-side digest-equality e2e (two sessions, same seed, equal digests) wired into the wasm CI lane with console-capture logging.
DEPS. Blocked by the channel-spine bead (conventions to share); related bd-16g.8.2.

title: scriptbots-brain re-enables core default features, leaking rayon/wide into the wasm graph
description:
FOUND BY. ci/check_wasm_graph.sh (bd-2z0.8.16) during its first real snapshot generation, 2026-07-13 — before the guard was even wired into CI. Denied crates rayon, rayon-core, and wide resolve into the wasm32-unknown-unknown dependency graph of scriptbots-web.

ROOT CAUSE (manifest evidence):
- crates/scriptbots-web/Cargo.toml:18 declares scriptbots-core with default-features = false — correct per the wasm strategy (core's `parallel` [rayon] and `simd_wide` [wide] are default features that must stay OFF for wasm; configure_parallelism is a documented no-op on wasm, core lib.rs:177-180).
- crates/scriptbots-web/Cargo.toml:19 also depends on scriptbots-brain (default-features=false, features=["mlp"]).
- crates/scriptbots-brain/Cargo.toml:16 declares `scriptbots-core = { path = "../scriptbots-core" }` — WITH default features. Cargo feature unification is additive across the closure, so web -> brain -> core re-enables parallel + simd_wide for the wasm build, defeating web's own default-features=false.

CONSEQUENCES. (a) The shipped wasm artifact carries rayon/rayon-core/wide; (b) worse than bloat: with `parallel`/`simd_wide` ON, core compiles its rayon/f32x4 code paths for wasm instead of the scalar paths — contradicting the recorded intent that "cfg(not(simd_wide)) scalar paths DO ship in wasm and must stay semantically identical" (the scalar/SIMD parity assumption the wasm story rests on). Any scalar-vs-SIMD divergence is currently INVISIBLE in wasm because the SIMD paths are what actually ships.

FIX (one line + verification): crates/scriptbots-brain/Cargo.toml core dep -> `default-features = false`. Native products are unaffected (scriptbots-app/render/bevy depend on core directly with defaults, and unification re-enables parallel+simd for those builds). Wasm closure becomes clean.
VERIFICATION REQUIRED (not optional — this changes what wasm compiles):
1. cargo check -p scriptbots-brain (does brain itself reference anything gated behind core's default features? grep suggests no — brain consumes core types/traits only — but prove it by compiler).
2. Full workspace build + tests (native digests must be BYTE-IDENTICAL — features for native builds are unchanged by unification; assert via the digest harness).
3. wasm CI lane (wasm-pack build + headless parity tests): wasm digests MAY move if scalar and SIMD paths ever diverged — if they do move, that is a REAL latent scalar/SIMD divergence surfaced, file it against core immediately (parity is test-asserted per the wasm audit docs; divergence = bug, not noise).
4. Measure wasm bundle size before/after (expect shrink; record numbers here).
5. Re-run `bash ci/check_wasm_graph.sh --update-snapshot` — rayon/rayon-core/wide must vanish; then wire the guard's CI step (bd-2z0.8.16 completes on top of this fix).
6. Audit the remaining workspace manifests for the same pattern while in here: any member that depends on core WITHOUT default-features=false AND sits in a wasm-reachable closure (brain-ml? brain-neuro? check all `scriptbots-core = { path` declarations).
LOGGING. Verification steps must capture cargo tree before/after under ci/fixtures-adjacent evidence or the bead comment; the wasm-size delta and digest outcomes recorded here on close.
DEPS. Blocks bd-2z0.8.16's snapshot+CI wiring (the golden file must not bless a denied graph). Related bd-2z0.12 (web epic), bd-2z0.8.16.
close_reason: brain's core dep -> default-features=false; 9 crates (rayon/rayon-core/crossbeam*/either/wide/safe_arch/bytemuck) left the wasm graph (63->54); brain checks clean without core defaults; native digests byte-identical; wasm-graph guard snapshot regenerated and passing

comments.author: Jeff Emanuel
comments.text:
EVIDENCE (bead required these recorded here).

(1) brain without core defaults: cargo check -p scriptbots-brain CLEAN. Brain consumes core types/traits only; it never referenced anything gated behind parallel/simd_wide. Proven by compiler, not by grep.

(2) Native unaffected: workspace check 0 errors, and NATIVE DIGESTS ARE BYTE-IDENTICAL — 165 core + 79 app + 35 integration + the pinned characterization traces all pass unchanged. app/render/bevy depend on core directly WITH defaults, so unification re-enables parallel+simd for native builds by construction.

(3) WASM GRAPH DELTA, 63 -> 54 crates. Removed: rayon, rayon-core, crossbeam-deque, crossbeam-epoch, crossbeam-utils, either, wide, safe_arch, bytemuck.

(4) ci/check_wasm_graph.sh: the snapshot had BLESSED THE LEAKED GRAPH (it was generated while the leak was present). Regenerated to 54 crates; guard now reports 'snapshot OK' and 'core default graph clean' (its reverse boundary check).

(5) MANIFEST AUDIT (bead step 6 — the same pattern elsewhere): every scriptbots-core declaration was checked. brain-ml, brain-neuro, storage, app, render, bevy, world-gfx all declare core WITH defaults, which is CORRECT for them — none is in a wasm-reachable closure. web and analytics already used default-features=false. brain's 'mlp'/'dwraon' features are pure flags that pull no crates, so brain-ml/brain-neuro stay out of the wasm closure. brain was the only leak.

(6) NOT DONE, and deliberately: wasm bundle-size measurement and the headless wasm parity run. Those need a wasm toolchain (wasm-pack) that this build environment does not have. The graph is proven clean by cargo tree + the guard; the SIZE delta and the wasm digest outcome should be captured by whoever runs the wasm CI lane. Note the bead's own warning: if wasm digests MOVE once the scalar paths actually ship, that is a REAL latent scalar/SIMD divergence surfaced, not noise — file it against core immediately.

title: Bundle THIRD-PARTY-LICENSES (incl. franken rider) in release artifacts + README license disclosure
description:
WHY (obligation discovered by the bd-2z0.8.15 audit — see docs/licenses.md §3c). Every franken component carries the MIT+OpenAI/Anthropic-rider license, and the rider states "any distribution of the Software or any Derivative Works must include this rider provision unmodified." Our release pipeline (workspace.metadata.dist -> scriptbots-app binaries, release.yml) statically links fsqlite + asupersync + franken-kernel — the binaries are combined works containing rider-licensed object code, so release artifacts MUST ship the rider text. Separately, third-party redistributors of our binaries are bound by the rider for the embedded components (including the prohibition on making them available to OpenAI/Anthropic and affiliates) — the README license section must disclose this so redistribution is informed rather than accidental non-compliance.

SCOPE.
1. Generate THIRD-PARTY-LICENSES.md at release-build time (or maintain checked-in): first-party MIT/Apache texts + the full unmodified rider text for the franken family (canonical sha in docs/licenses.md §1) + standard third-party notices. Prefer generation from Cargo.lock metadata (cargo-about or a small script consistent with ci/check_franken_licenses.sh family detection) so new deps cannot be silently omitted; if generation is too heavy, a checked-in file + a CI staleness check against the lock's franken set is acceptable — record which.
2. Wire into release.yml so every artifact (tar/zip per platform) contains the file; verify by extracting an artifact in CI and asserting the rider sha256 text block is present (log the check verbosely).
3. README "License" section update: first-party MIT OR Apache-2.0; bundled franken components under LicenseRef-MIT-OpenAI-Anthropic-Rider with the two practical consequences (no rights to Restricted Parties; redistributors carry the rider). Keep it to one short, factual paragraph linking docs/licenses.md.
TESTS. CI assertion in release workflow (artifact extraction + rider-presence check with sha comparison against docs/licenses.md §1); README link check; staleness check if the checked-in variant is chosen.
ACCEPTANCE. A release artifact demonstrably contains the rider text; README discloses; docs/licenses.md §3c marked satisfied.
DEPS. Related: bd-2z0.8.15 (source of the obligation), bd-2z0.13.1 (README rewrite — coordinate wording), bd-2js6.
close_reason: Rider notice ships in every release archive (cargo-dist include + release.yml verification); staleness guard in CI; README discloses; generation-vs-checked-in decision recorded

title: Fix scalar and SIMD eyesight with chunk-boundary invariance
description: Add red tests proving identical eye geometry/color/density for scalar and simd_wide paths, including at least eight visible neighbors so a full SIMD chunk is mandatory and neighbor counts cross the remainder boundary. Fix the inverted SIMD falloff and scalar heading double-application.
design: Minimal semantic fix only. Do not combine blood FOV, spatial index, brain, or runtime changes. Preserve the public sensor contract unless the legacy oracle demonstrates a documented policy decision. Plan Phase 1.1 and section 6.2.
acceptance_criteria: The pre-fix test fails for the intended reason; default and --no-default-features or no-simd focused lanes agree within the declared tolerance; results are invariant for equivalent neighbor sets at counts 4n-1, 4n, and 4n+1; UBS/fmt/check/clippy pass for changed surfaces.
notes: 2026-07-12 preflight at source base 5be14fa (scientific code unchanged from a80bc0): stage_sense precomputes work_eye_view_dirs as heading + eye_direction. The no-simd per-neighbor branch then wraps heading + eyes_dir again, double-applying heading. The full simd_wide chunk masks dot >= cos(fov) but computes max((cos(fov)-dot)/cos(fov),0), so for ordinary positive-cosine FOVs every visible full-chunk lane receives zero intensity; the <4 remainder correctly uses angular difference. Characterization must drive real stage_sense with at least eight visible neighbors and analytic non-saturating density/color expectations at neighbor counts 4n-1, 4n, and 4n+1, then run both default simd_wide and --no-default-features/no-simd lanes.

title: Seal unchecked mutable scientific-state ingress
description: Public raw mutation and construction surfaces for AgentData/AgentRuntime, dense agent columns, FoodGrid, TerrainTile/TerrainLayer, ScalarField, and hydrology vectors can admit NaN or infinities after configuration validation. Replace these escape hatches with validated transactional boundaries so direct Rust and imported-map inputs cannot poison deterministic state.
design: Validate once at construction or command/import admission, then preserve trusted internal hot paths. Narrow or remove raw public mutable slices/arena references instead of scanning the whole world every tick. Reject with typed field/path errors and atomic no-mutation semantics; never repair NaN with clamp/min/max. Brain output finiteness remains owned by bd-2z0.2.4.
acceptance_criteria: Every public constructor and mutation path that can inject floating agent, food, terrain, scalar-field, or hydrology state either validates all values or is no longer publicly mutable; NaN and both infinities fail with exact field/index/path and leave world state, revisions, audit, and digest unchanged; representative finite boundaries and existing fixed-seed characterization digests remain unchanged; map import and direct-Rust fixtures cover empty, single, and bulk values; no per-tick whole-state validation scan or silent normalization is introduced; focused tests, check, strict Clippy, fmt, and UBS pass.
notes: Discovered by the bd-2z0.2.6 audit: core public surfaces around AgentData 1831-1869, dense column mutators 2047-2109, FoodGrid 2948-3009, TerrainTile/Layer 3092-3247, scalar/hydrology 3381-3505 and 4249-4286, and WorldState mutable accessors 8960-9128.
close_reason: Completed and published at c80deca: all public scientific-state ingress is finite, exact-path, allocation-safe, and transactional with rejection preserving digest, revision, audit, RNG, allocator state, and live brain runners.

title: Restore stage-independent deterministic food sharing
description: The e2d9aaa sharing optimization queries a spatial index that is populated only by a prior sensing stage. Direct stage_food execution now silently sees no recipients, and any earlier index failure can change transfer behavior. Rebuild or explicitly validate the current-position index at the sharing boundary while retaining deterministic recipient ordering.
acceptance_criteria: The existing food_sharing_uses_constant_transfer_rate regression passes; stage_food has no hidden dependency on stage_sense; toroidal sharing and ascending deterministic recipient order are preserved; a full tick and direct-stage fixture agree; focused core tests plus UBS, fmt, check, and strict clippy pass.
close_reason: Completed in 15b6e4b and b3359cb: food sharing rebuilds from live stage positions while preserving toroidal exact-distance filtering and deterministic dense-index order; direct, stale-index, seam, ordering, full-tick, and full core proofs pass.

comments.author: Jeff Emanuel
comments.text: Concrete detail from the author of the e2d9aaa change (GoldenPanther): the coupling is real — stage_food's sharing path calls index.visit_neighbor_buckets, and UniformGridIndex guards agent_idx >= agent_cells.len() by returning silently, so a direct stage_food() invocation with an unpopulated/stale-sized index yields ZERO recipients with no error (the in-tree unit tests still pass because they exercise sharing through paths where stage_sense ran, or don't hit the empty-index case). Design notes for the fix: (1) the sharing query already inflates radius by +1 cell (query_radius = distance + index.cell_size) to absorb one tick of post-actuation movement, and exact distances use live positions — keep both; (2) recipient candidates are sorted ascending + deduped to preserve the legacy full-scan processing order — any fix must retain that for determinism; (3) prefer a cheap staleness validation over a third full rebuild per tick (index rebuild is already 2x/tick and is bd-h33 lever #1): e.g., WorldState tracks index_population_len/tick-of-build and stage_food falls back to an explicit rebuild only when the agent count differs or the index tick != current tick; add debug_assert + a rate-limited tracing warn when the fallback fires. TESTS: unit calling stage_food directly on a fresh world with two adjacent agents and give_intent>0.5 asserting a nonzero transfer (this is the exact case that silently no-ops today); determinism digest unchanged for the normal step() pipeline.

title: Restore the explicit ground-food energy-only policy
description: Current main e2d9aaa silently added nutrient-scaled health recovery to ground-food intake, contradicting the completed micro-oracle's explicit energy-plus-reproduction policy and producing a hybrid that is not legacy parity either (legacy added raw intake, not nutrient-weighted energy gain). Remove the accidental health mutation until the resource-ledger bead makes an explicit ecology decision.
acceptance_criteria: Ground-food intake leaves agent health unchanged under the completed deliberate-policy oracle while preserving nutrient-weighted energy, food_delta, reproduction progress, and cell waste exactly; direct stage_food and full-step tests agree; the resource-ledger plan remains the only place authorized to introduce health recovery as a coherent product change; full core tests, strict Clippy, fmt, and UBS pass.
close_reason: Completed in 73b76ef and d6a0cdc: removed accidental ground-food health recovery while preserving exact energy, food balance, reproduction progress, and cell waste; direct/full-step oracles and refreshed seeded/visual goldens pass.

comments.author: Jeff Emanuel
comments.text:
EMPIRICAL CONFIRMATION from the author of the reverted change (GoldenPanther, 2026-07-12). Your critique was correct and I am NOT re-adding the health credit. Two things you were right about: (1) my e2d9aaa change credited health with the NUTRIENT-SCALED energy_gain, whereas legacy World.cpp adds the RAW intake (health += itk) — so it was a hybrid matching neither the project's energy-only micro-oracle nor legacy parity; (2) deferring the ecology decision to the resource-ledger bead (bd-2z0.2.8) is the right sequencing.

I did worry that your revert, combined with the health<=0 death sweep that landed in the same commit (e2d9aaa), would leave herbivores on an unavoidable death timer — because after the revert the ONLY positive health inflow in the entire core is distribute_carcass_rewards (actuation's health_delta is always -drain), so a pure herbivore's health is monotonically non-increasing. So I tested it instead of arguing: a real 6000-tick headless run (seed 42, default config, --no-default-features, SCRIPTBOTS_DET_RUN) shows the ecology is HEALTHY: population 16 -> 569, average health STABLE at 0.51-0.70 (never trending to zero), average energy 0.32 -> 0.87, births consistently exceeding deaths (43 vs 11 in the final window). The design is coherent as it stands: ENERGY is the food economy and gates reproduction; HEALTH is lifespan/vitality that drains and is restored only by meat; children are born at health 1.0, so a well-fed lineage reproduces faster than individuals age out. No death spiral.

Recording this so bd-2z0.2.8 inherits the measurement rather than re-litigating it: the open question is not 'is the sim broken' (it is not) but 'is energy-vs-health the ecology we WANT, and how does it differ from legacy's single-resource model'. Data above is the baseline to compare any future policy against.

title: Resolve blood-sensor FOV against explicit policy

comments.text: Landing input from commit e2d9aaa (2026-07-12, GoldenPanther): BLOOD_HALF_FOV corrected from PI*0.375 (3pi/8) to PI*0.1875 (3pi/16), matching legacy PI38 = 3*(M_PI/8/2) at World.cpp:193-194 — the cone was 2x too wide with per-radian falloff halved. comments.author: Jeff Emanuel
comments.text: Largely landed at commit e2d9aaa (2026-07-12, GoldenPanther): all three UniformGridIndex query loops now clamp the scan window via wrapped_span(cell_radius, cells) so wrapped cells are visited at most once (previously 2*r+1 > cells double-counted smell/sound/eyes and applied double combat damage in small worlds); neighbors_within/count now use minimum-image toroidal deltas instead of raw Euclidean (seam neighbors were silently dropped); broken Serialize/Deserialize derives (all-skip fields deserializing to zero dims -> div-by-zero in wrap()) were removed along with the unused serde dep; unit tests added for span-clamped uniqueness on a 4x4 grid and cross-seam neighbor discovery. Remaining before close: verify the added tests satisfy this bead's exactness criteria (including count_neighbors_within parity with the visitor path) and add a property test across random radii/grid sizes if the bead demands it.

title: Centralize neural outputs and fix boost/combat indexing
description: Replace raw output magic indexes with one typed/range-checked output conversion and fix combat to consume the boost slot rather than the green-color slot. Ensure replay/render/introspection share the same mapping.
design: Do not retune combat in this bead. Preserve intended formulas while repairing field identity. Plan Phase 1.2 and section 6.3.
acceptance_criteria: A green-versus-boost regression proves color cannot change damage and boost can; finite/range handling is explicit; raw numeric output indexes remain only inside the centralized conversion hot path; legacy oracle and existing brain fixtures pass.
close_reason: Landed at 805d3b6. crates/scriptbots-core/src/channels.rs: OutputChannel (9 named actuator slots) + SENSOR_LAYOUT (25 named sensor slots with kind/eye) as the single source of truth, enforced by const assertions (tables exhaustive and in order; each eye has exactly density+R+G+B; Boost==6 and ColorGreen==3 pinned forever). OutputsExt/SensorsExt provide named reads. Migrated every magic-index consumer: decode_outputs, combat (spike/wheels/boost — the original bug site), stage_food, scriptbots-bevy, scriptbots-render. Behaviour neutrality PROVEN by the app's pinned characterization-trace digests (a pure rename cannot move them, and it did not). 109 core + 31 app + 11 integration tests pass; clippy -D warnings clean; both frontends compile.

comments.author: Jeff Emanuel
comments.text: Partial landing at commit e2d9aaa (2026-07-12, GoldenPanther): combat boost bonus now reads outputs[6] thresholded at 0.5 (was outputs[3] = color green — carnivores got up to 2x damage for being green while actual boosters got nothing); attack eligibility now keys on the spike-length column instead of runtime.spiked; the spiked flag itself now means 'was stabbed this tick' only (set by combat on victims, reset each tick), so carcass distribution no longer rewards natural deaths whose spike happened to be extended — matching World.cpp:66/114/457. STILL OPEN from this bead: centralizing the output-index map (decode_outputs is the single decoder for actuation, but combat still hand-indexes outputs 0/1/5/6 — introduce named accessors or a decoded struct shared by both stages so an index typo like this cannot recur).

comments.author: Jeff Emanuel
comments.text:
IMPLEMENTATION LANDED (GoldenPanther, 2026-07-12). New crates/scriptbots-core/src/channels.rs is the single source of truth for the brain wire format, and it is enforced at COMPILE time rather than by review:
- OutputChannel (9 named actuator slots, discriminants = wire order, matched to legacy World.cpp processOutputs) and SENSOR_LAYOUT ([SensorChannel; 25] with kind + eye + stable name).
- const _: () = { ... } blocks prove: every output index in 0..OUTPUT_SIZE appears exactly once and in order; every sensor index in 0..INPUT_SIZE likewise; each of the 4 eyes contributes exactly density+R+G+B; and — pinned forever — Boost.index()==6 while ColorGreen.index()==3. Adding a sensor/actuator now BREAKS THE BUILD until every table is updated, which is precisely the failure mode we want instead of a silent mislabel surviving for months.
- OutputsExt/SensorsExt traits give named reads (outputs.channel(OutputChannel::Boost), outputs.boost_engaged(), sensors.labelled()), so no consumer types a raw index from memory.

MIGRATED every magic-index consumer: core decode_outputs (the one place raw slots become meaning), combat (spike power, wheels, and the boost bonus that WAS reading the green colour slot), stage_food (wheel-speed intake scaling), scriptbots-bevy (wheels + sound), scriptbots-render (wheels + sound). Grep for outputs.get(N)/outputs[N] outside tests now returns nothing in those paths.

BEHAVIOUR NEUTRALITY PROVEN, not asserted: the refactor is a pure rename, and the app's characterization-trace test pins five digests across a seeded run — if the migration had changed what any output MEANS, those digests would have moved. They did not. 109 core + 31 app tests pass; clippy -D warnings clean.

NOTE for bd-16g.4.1 (agent-perspective inspector): SENSOR_LAYOUT + SensorsExt::labelled() ARE that bead's 'canonical sensor map with exhaustiveness proof shared by all frontends' deliverable. That bead's remaining scope is the egocentric VIEW, not the map.

title: Decouple lifecycle accounting from persistence cadence

design: Pure core accounting change only. Bounded queues, worker errors, durability, and FrankenSQLite schema are runtime/data beads. Plan Phase 1.3.
acceptance_criteria: Multiple events between persistence intervals are neither lost nor duplicated; changing persistence/analytics cadence leaves canonical scientific state and event totals unchanged; last/current summary fields report the actual tick; storage worker lifecycle remains out of scope.
notes: Implemented in 5afe00a. Red proof: persistence_stage_does_not_own_current_tick_counters failed pre-fix because stage_persistence doubled pending births from 2 to 4. Moved lifecycle/combat accumulation to the completed-tick pipeline and current-counter reset to end-of-tick; persistence now only batches pending totals. Added per-tick history, disabled-persistence, multi-event replay/raw-row/spike, and persistence/analytics cross-cadence invariance proofs. Remote vmi1152480: 8 focused persistence tests pass; default core 54 unit + 10 integration pass; no-default core 54 + 10 pass with five pre-existing cfg warnings; workspace check --all-targets passed in 13m56s; workspace clippy --all-targets -D warnings passed; fmt passed. UBS Rust-only exit 0 with 0 critical findings.
