title: Drive HostCore with fixed-deadline native lifecycle
description: Drive the exact .4.5 HostCore with a native fixed-deadline lifecycle. The driver owns scheduling, wakeups, cancellation, and bounded catch-up only; it cannot mutate WorldState except by invoking HostCore. Use the minimal Asupersync pieces selected by .4.3, or the documented alternative, while keeping manual/browser drivers independent.
design: Inject a monotonic clock and use deadline progression rather than repaint/frame deltas. Commands wake the driver, but only HostCore boundary processing changes control or science. Bound missed-deadline catch-up and record skipped wall-clock opportunity without inventing extra science order. Graceful Shutdown is an idempotent ordered envelope: define when new admissions close, finish or terminally reject earlier/pending envelopes in order, retain unadmitted journal work, request storage flush through the port, publish final status, and join every owned task before returning. Cancellation and panic paths satisfy explicit obligations and never bypass status bookkeeping silently.
acceptance_criteria: Manual and native drivers produce identical command, StepOutcome, ControlRevision, EventSequence, and WorldDigest traces for the same injected deadline/command schedule. Tests cover early/late/backward clock observations, wake storms, bounded catch-up, long pause with low CPU, cancellation before/during/after a step, queue-full science stop, shutdown with empty/nonempty queues, flush timeout/failure, and repeated idempotent shutdown. Repaint count and number of synthetic clients cannot affect ticks. The new production host lifecycle exposes no world lock and leaves no detached simulation/scheduler task. This bead does not claim the legacy Bevy driver or GPUI/TUI world access is gone before their adapter migrations.
notes: Native lifecycle only; browser/WASM may call the same HostCore from its own adapter but requestAnimationFrame must not become scientific time. Storage implementation and frontend teardown remain separate beads.

title: Publish immutable multi-subscriber snapshots
description: Publish immutable, renderer-neutral RenderSnapshot values from the sole-owner host: current tick/summary, run and control health, typed revisions, compact dynamic agents, and Arc-shared terrain/food/hydrology layers keyed by content revision. Provide bounded latest-value multi-subscriber semantics with an independent cursor for every consumer.
design: Snapshot publication is a lossy latest-value read model, not the scientific event journal and not a database query. Build snapshots only from HostCore-owned state/StepOutcome at the declared cadence; static layers reuse Arc values until their own revision changes, dynamic data uses a measured compact representation, and selected-agent detail is requested separately. Each subscriber may skip stale frames and load the newest Arc without retaining an unbounded queue. SnapshotRevision is publication order and never substitutes for ControlRevision, ScientificRevision, ConfigRevision, or EventSequence.
acceptance_criteria: Two fast subscribers plus stalled, dropped, and reconnecting subscribers remain independently bounded; the newest snapshot is coherent and monotonic; static layer pointer/content changes occur only with the matching revision; current summary advances independently of persistence cadence; and snapshot cadence/subscriber load cannot change WorldDigest or tick count. Measure allocation, bytes, build p50/p95, and 1k/10k agent costs. The new host/client API exposes no Arc<Mutex<WorldState>>, mutable core references, or FrankenSQLite handle. This does not falsely assert legacy frontends are migrated; .6.1 and .7.2 remove their old world-lock paths.
notes: Scientific events and gap recovery are implemented by .4.8. Frontend-specific camera, selection, top-K, glyph, and chart work must not become global mutable snapshot state.

comments.text:
[GoldenOtter 2026-07-12] Implementation-relevant asupersync facts for the snapshot bus (program: bd-2js6; channel spine bead: bd-2z0.4.12):
- asupersync watch::channel(init) has a FULLY SYNCHRONOUS send(value) (no Cx) — a plain sim/snapshot thread can publish without touching an executor; async consumers use changed(&cx). Unbounded mpsc send is also sync. Bounded mpsc try_send/try_recv are sync non-blocking.
- watch = latest-value single-slot; your per-consumer independent cursor requirement is NOT satisfied by one watch alone (slow consumer skips intermediates by design — fine for renderers, wrong for consumers needing every revision). Candidate shapes: watch per consumer-class, or broadcast::channel(cap) (has lagged-receiver semantics), or keep the bespoke ring and use asupersync only for wakeup. bd-2z0.4.12 implements the Bevy-path stepping stone and defers the multi-subscriber product design to this bead — please coordinate so we do not ship two competing buses.

title: Add per-client projections and sequenced event journal
description: Add deterministic renderer-neutral projections keyed by client/request and a bounded sequenced scientific-event journal. Viewport, camera, selection, requested detail, and chart windows are per-client inputs; no client can mutate global projection or scientific state. Event subscribers use EventSequence cursors, detect gaps, and either catch up from the journal or report an explicit truncated display window.
design: Projection functions are pure functions of immutable snapshot plus request and may use a keyed cache whose identity includes all request and source revisions. The hot event ring carries ordered notifications/cursors, while the journal is the lossless source. A cursor yields contiguous batches or an explicit Gap containing expected and available sequence ranges plus a catch-up locator. Events with JournalState Pending are never evicted or overwritten; reaching high water stops later science through HostCore until the exact batch is acknowledged. File-mode Durable records support crash-safe catch-up. CommittedVolatile memory-mode records may leave the hot ring only while the live in-memory journal remains queryable and must never be advertised as crash-durable.
acceptance_criteria: Two clients with different cameras, selections, detail requests, and chart windows produce isolated deterministic projections and cannot affect each other, world digests, or scientific revisions. Tests cover contiguous cursor reads, duplicate polling, slow consumers, ring wrap, explicit Gap metadata, durable file-journal catch-up, live memory-journal catch-up, unavailable catch-up, disconnect/reconnect, and shutdown. No Pending event is evicted; high-water pressure retains exact events and pauses before loss. Projection/event memory, latency, and top-K/canvas scaling are measured, and slow UI consumers never create an unbounded queue.
notes: This bead defines event sequencing and catch-up behavior; .4.10 implements production journal admission, acknowledgements, watermarks, and crash-durability proof. Presentation screens and renderer-specific picking remain in frontend beads.

title: Migrate CLI, REST, and MCP control to HostClient
description: Migrate the control CLI, REST, MCP, SSE, and NDJSON surfaces to the same HostClient/service contract. Remove their direct SharedWorld locks and projected-before-applied responses. Expose Pause, Resume, Step, Speed, status lookup, config/selection commands, and ordered graceful Shutdown with CommandId, expected ControlRevision, and the two-axis application/journal receipt. Add an explicit server-only application mode that runs the authoritative host with no visual frontend.
design: One transport-neutral control service performs validation, submits HostClient envelopes, reads immutable snapshots/status, and maps typed failures consistently; CLI, REST, and MCP are adapters only. Centralize the REST default at http://127.0.0.1:8088 so scriptbots-control, server configuration, help, README, and tests agree. SSE and NDJSON records carry monotonic sequence/revision fields, stable event IDs, heartbeat/schema metadata, bounded payloads, and explicit gap/reconnect behavior rather than polling a world lock. A state-changing request either waits to its documented application/journal level or returns Accepted with a status URL/ID; it never returns a fabricated future config as current.
acceptance_criteria: In explicit server mode with no renderer, CLI, REST, and MCP all perform Pause, Resume, Step, Speed, valid/invalid config, status lookup, and idempotent Shutdown with equivalent CommandId, ControlRevision, ApplicationState, JournalState, error, and retry semantics. scriptbots-control defaults to port 8088. A transport-conformance suite runs the same vectors for duplicate ID, stale revision, validation rejection, queue full, disconnected host, storage pending/failure, and shutdown pending across CLI/REST/MCP. SSE and NDJSON tests prove monotonic nonduplicated sequences, resume/gap behavior, response bounds, and cancellation cleanup. Reads use immutable snapshots; ASCII capture has real content/provenance, while unavailable live PNG capture returns a typed honest error rather than empty success.
notes: This bead migrates control transports, not TUI/GUI rendering internals. It must not claim crash durability beyond .4.10 acknowledgements, and it must not substitute a semantic CPU PNG for a live frontend framebuffer. Keep loopback defaults and schema/version discovery agent-friendly.

title: Replay, persistence, and experiment data
description: Implement run-scoped provenance, commands/events/checkpoints/digests, deterministic bundles, multi-run FrankenSQLite persistence, export, and verification.

title: Design multi-run FrankenSQLite schema and provenance migrations
description: Replace single-run primary-key assumptions with run-scoped FrankenSQLite tables for manifests, configs, seeds, features/build/source provenance, agents/lineages, metrics, commands, events, checkpoints, and digests. Use versioned transactional MigrationRunner/user_version migrations and validation.
design: Build on the proven fsqlite storage boundary and coordinate with bounded runtime storage while keeping schema logic independently testable. No destructive migration without explicit user permission; create/migrate test databases only. Plan sections 7.1 and 7.6.
acceptance_criteria: Two runs with overlapping ticks/agent ordinals coexist; run_id participates in all required keys; manifest provenance is queryable; migration is transactionally tested; schema version and failure recovery are explicit; analytics queries remain bounded.

title: Persist sequenced command status and domain event journals
description: Persist commands, tick-boundary status transitions, nonempty lifecycle/combat/domain events, event sequence, and digest references using the runtime durability protocol.
design: Uses corrected core accounting and runtime storage worker. Do not reconstruct events from aggregate metrics. Plan sections 7.2-7.4.
acceptance_criteria: Admitted/applied/durable/rejected/failed transitions are queryable; event sequences detect gaps/duplicates; births/deaths/combat between persistence intervals survive; an empty domain-event stream cannot satisfy a scenario expected to emit events.

title: Implement full checkpoints and first-divergence replay
description: Persist and restore world, brain genome/evaluator state, RNG streams, commands, config, environment, counters, and manifest; replay from tick zero or checkpoint and report the first stage/tick divergence.
design: Builds on digest/checkpoint envelope, runtime protocol, and journals. Do not call two empty vectors a successful replay. Plan Phase 4.1.
acceptance_criteria: Encode/decode is idempotent; next-tick output after restore matches; tick-zero and checkpoint replay match WorldDigestV1 in the bit-exact lane; empty evidence fails; divergence output identifies tick, stage, expected/actual digest, and relevant artifact.

title: Assemble and verify portable deterministic run bundles
description: Package manifest/source provenance, commands/status, events, checkpoints, digests, the FrankenSQLite run database, exports, and artifact index with integrity hashes and an import/verify command.
design: No silent best-effort verification. Packaging is separate from release distribution. Plan Phase 4.2.
acceptance_criteria: A second clean checkout using the pinned toolchain verifies a bundle; missing/tampered files fail with a precise reason; artifact paths are relative and portable; bundle schema is versioned; verification does not require GUI.

title: Build deterministic matched-seed experiment runner
description: Run scenario variants over matched seed cohorts with bounded concurrency, checkpoint/resume/branch, progress/status, and reproducible summaries using the canonical HostCore and bundle formats.
design: Scientific execution layer, not a UI. Depends on honest brain families, runtime, and bundle verification. Plan Phase 4.3.
acceptance_criteria: An MLP-versus-DWRAON sample produces comparable run bundles with identical environment seed schedule; interrupted batches resume without duplicate runs; concurrency does not change individual digests; resource bounds and failure policy are documented.

title: Provide provenance-rich Arrow, Parquet, and CSV exports
description: Define stable run/agent/lineage/event/metric exports for offline tools, including schema/version/provenance metadata and bounded streaming behavior.
design: Keep offline analytics optional and presentation-independent. Plan sections 7.7-7.8.
acceptance_criteria: Exports round-trip representative data; run identity and units survive; large tables stream without materializing the entire run; schema evolution is explicit; FrankenPandas/SciPy/NetworkX adapters consume exports rather than entering the tick loop.

title: Bound and instrument timed-out storage supervisor reaping
description: Replace one-independent-thread-per-timeout handoff with a bounded supervisor registry keyed by writer lease and storage path. Coalesce repeated handoffs without moving the FrankenSQLite Connection, and expose active, queued, and hung worker counts.
acceptance_criteria: Saturation and repeated timeouts never drop a JoinHandle or receipt, never block unrelated storage paths, preserve synchronous fallback when thread spawn or registry admission fails, allow eventual stopped publication and safe reopen, never hard-cancel a worker or move a Connection across threads, and include deterministic tests for duplicate handoff, saturation, hung worker, and recovery.
close_reason: Bounded, path-keyed supervisor registry replaces one-thread-per-timeout; coalesces repeated handoffs; never drops a JoinHandle (queued requests drained before a reaper retires; spawn-failure keeps the request in a shared slot); synchronous fallback preserved on saturation and spawn failure; active/queued/started/coalesced/synchronous counts exposed; deterministic tests for duplicate handoff, saturation, cross-path independence, and reopen-after-reap

title: Bound persistence admission by payload bytes and preparation time
description: The persistence queue is bounded only by command count; arbitrarily large batch vectors are prepared before any deadline and can exhaust memory or violate caller latency. Add deterministic per-batch byte/event ceilings and total in-flight byte permits without moving the FrankenSQLite connection or weakening exact retry semantics.
acceptance_criteria: Oversized batches are rejected synchronously before unbounded allocation or worker admission with a typed NotAdmitted result retaining exact retry data; total admitted payload bytes remain within a configured hard cap; preparation observes a deterministic deadline; byte permits are released exactly once on commit, refusal, timeout handoff, crash, and shutdown; boundary, saturation, retry, and recovery tests plus strict Clippy, fmt, and UBS pass.
close_reason: Byte/record ceilings enforced BEFORE from_batch allocates; typed PayloadTooLarge/InFlightBytesExhausted refusals retain exact retry data; total in-flight bytes bounded; permit is RAII so it cannot leak on any exit path; boundary/saturation/retry/leak tests + clippy clean

title: Persist pairwise interaction events (combat/food-share edges) for graph analytics
description:
WHY. The fnx interaction-centrality report (bd-2z0.11.7, report 3) and the ecosystem-accounting ideas (bd-16g.11) both want WHO-did-WHAT-to-WHOM edges: combat (attacker, victim, damage, tick) and food-share/altruism (giver, receiver, amount, tick). TODAY the schema only stores per-kind COUNTS in `events` plus JSON blobs in `replay_events` (storage lib.rs V1 schema :57-166) — aggregate counts cannot reconstruct an interaction GRAPH, and parsing replay JSON for every analytics run is slow and schema-fragile. This bead was explicitly promised by bd-2z0.11.7 ("file a follow-up storage bead rather than silently widening scope") — this is that bead.

DESIGN.
- New `interactions` table (schema migration in the storage lane, coordinating with the V3 FTS migration bd-16g.2.6 for version numbering): (tick, kind: combat|share|spike_hit|..., actor_uid, target_uid, magnitude REAL) with stable agent UIDs (the same stable-UID discipline as bd-16g.3.1's ancestry store — NOT slot indices, which recycle).
- Volume control (the reason this is not free): combat/share events at 5k agents can be orders of magnitude denser than births/deaths. Ship with (a) a sampling/stride knob (persist every interaction | every Nth tick window | aggregates-only fallback = current behavior) recorded in run config + provenance, and (b) an explicit budget test proving the write path stays within the bounded-admission envelope (bd-2z0.4.10 semantics) at 5k agents with persistence enabled — if the budget cannot hold at full fidelity, the default ships as windowed sampling and says so loudly in docs.
- Emission point: eating/food-sharing stage (core lib.rs:7313+) and combat stage (:7752+) already compute these pairs; extend the PersistenceBatch plumbing (lib.rs:1654) rather than adding a side channel.
- Consumers: bd-2z0.11.7 upgrades its interaction-centrality report from replay-JSON parsing to SQL over `interactions`; bd-16g.11's energy-flow accounting gains its edge list.
TESTS. Unit: emission correctness (synthetic staged fight/share scenarios produce exactly the expected rows, UIDs stable across slot recycling); sampling-stride semantics; migration fresh+upgrade. Integration: seeded run at 2k agents, assert row counts match in-sim event counters exactly (accounting identity); bounded-admission budget test at 5k agents with tracing of batch sizes/flush durations. Logging: per-flush interaction-row counts at debug; run-summary totals at info.
ACCEPTANCE. Interaction graph queryable via SQL on a seeded run DB; accounting identity test green; write-path budget evidence recorded in the bead; sampling default documented.
DEPS. Blocked by bd-2z0.5.2 (sequenced domain event journals — this table must ride that design, not compete with it). Related bd-2z0.11.7, bd-16g.11, bd-16g.3.1.

description: Compare published crate, exact Git revision, and local source availability for FrankenTUI; review licensing/distribution, API stability, toolchain/default features, and rollback boundary; select one immutable integration.
design: Current sibling HEAD observed at fccff2a7e51d39a927bced882877a45aef5c8d39 but must be reverified at execution. Do not modify or clean the sibling checkout. Plan Phase 3.2.
acceptance_criteria: Decision names exact source/revision/version and license evidence; mutable path/branch is rejected; minimal build spike passes pinned toolchain; default feature impact is measured; implementation beads depend on this decision.
notes: Decision complete: use FrankenTUI Git revision fccff2a7e51d39a927bced882877a45aef5c8d39 (local HEAD == origin/main, v0.5.0-83) with =0.5.0 constraints. Product: ftui default-features=false+crossterm; ftui-extras default-features=false+charts,theme; direct ftui-a11y. Dev: ftui-harness default-features=false and ftui-pty, all same rev. Preserve LicenseRef-MIT-OpenAI-Anthropic-Rider and exact provenance in every distribution/SBOM; never describe combined binaries as only MIT OR Apache-2.0. Isolated repo /Users/jemanuel/projects/rust_scriptbots__frankentui_spike commit 98c2e0e passed remote cargo check --all-targets and cargo test 1/1 on nightly-2026-07-09. Graph evidence: 70 unique normal tree lines, 124 normal+dev, 159 lock packages, zero forbidden WGPU/Asupersync/native/render-thread normal hits. Product manifest/lock pin remains serialized under bd-2z0.8.8. Upstream lifecycle/simulator gaps are tracked by bd-2z0.6.3.1 and block bd-2z0.6.3.

title: Build FrankenTUI Model shell, receipts, and simulator harness
description: Implement the approved FrankenTUI Model/update/view/subscription shell, terminal RAII, HostClient receipt flow, routing, help/status overlays, and ProgramSimulator-based deterministic harness.
design: Shell only; detailed screens/canvas follow. Reuse approved source APIs rather than recreating a pseudo-framework. Plan Phase 3.3.
acceptance_criteria: State transitions and command receipts are deterministic; terminal restoration passes panic/quit paths; minimal goldens cover capabilities and errors; ProgramSimulator can inject time/input/snapshots without a live world.

title: Close FrankenTUI lifecycle and simulator contract gaps
description: At exact FrankenTUI revision fccff2a7e51d39a927bced882877a45aef5c8d39, make Model::on_error execute, guarantee on_shutdown on runtime-error exits, expose deterministic ProgramSimulator time/subscription/shutdown support, and prove bounded integration behavior. ScriptBots may implement upstream fixes in ~/projects/frankentui and advance the immutable revision only through the serialized dependency protocol.
notes: Completed upstream at FrankenTUI 15cc6543f76b814394c590f9e7719dedd6684e4c, confirmed exact on both upstream branches. Runtime now invokes Model::on_error for fatal runtime, command, and subscription failures; drains observed subscription failures; preserves the original fatal error; and runs one-shot on_shutdown/teardown on quit, signal, or error. ProgramSimulator now exposes deterministic time, subscription delivery, error injection, cancel, and idempotent shutdown APIs. Proof: lifecycle 13/13, serialized doctor_frankentui 2418/2418, workspace all-target check, runtime strict Clippy, format/diff checks. Two unrelated load-sensitive timing tests were identified honestly: subscription_manager_stops_removed passed targeted, perf_ordering_overhead measured 100.18ms against a 100ms threshold under load. ScriptBots dependency adoption remains serialized in bd-2z0.8.8.
close_reason: Lifecycle and deterministic simulator contract fixed and pushed upstream at immutable revision 15cc6543f76b814394c590f9e7719dedd6684e4c.

title: Build responsive layered world canvas and inspector
description: Render revisioned terrain/food/agents/sensors/selection in a zoomable responsive FrankenTUI canvas with compact/standard/wide breakpoints and a selected-agent inspector.
design: Consumes projections only; no world stepping or global camera state. Plan sections 8.2-8.4.
acceptance_criteria: Goldens pass at required terminal sizes and color capabilities; Unicode/emoji widths do not corrupt layout; mouse/keyboard selection, pan, zoom, resize, and density modes work; 1k/10k snapshot render budgets are measured.

title: Implement command palette and acknowledged controls
description: Add searchable command palette and discoverable key bindings for pause/resume/step/speed, scenario/config interventions, checkpoint/export, screen navigation, and diagnostics with admission/application/durability feedback.
design: No direct state mutation. Reuse HostClient command schemas and status lookup. Plan section 8.5.
acceptance_criteria: Every mutating action shows pending/applied/rejected/failed/durable status; palette filtering and keyboard/mouse paths are tested; conflicting/stale config revisions explain recovery; help is generated from the same command registry.

title: Build lineage, brain, experiment, replay, and diagnostics screens
description: Implement Lineages, Brain Arena, Experiments, Replay, Environment, and Diagnostics screens from canonical snapshots/data queries, including checkpoint/export/branch workflows.

acceptance_criteria: A user can run, inspect, intervene, checkpoint, branch, compare, and export without leaving TUI; slow queries are bounded/cancellable; each screen has empty/loading/error/data goldens; enabling introspection cannot change simulation digest.

title: Prove TUI goldens, input storms, and PTY lifecycle
description: Run deterministic buffer goldens, resize/mouse/key storms, slow snapshot readers, command conflict flows, real PTY startup/teardown, crash/panic restoration, and terminal capability matrix.
design: Tests the shipped FrankenTUI path, not a CPU surrogate. Plan sections 8.6 and 13.5-13.6.
acceptance_criteria: No terminal corruption, leaked alternate screen, stuck input, duplicate tick, or unbounded queue occurs; goldens include metadata and are never auto-blessed in CI; PTY logs identify exact failure; resource budgets pass.

title: Capture actual current-version Bevy and GPUI live frames
description: Build minimal real current-version Bevy render-app and GPUI window/paint probes, capture actual framebuffer/window evidence with backend/platform metadata, and distinguish API/code red from unavailable hardware.
design: Characterization only; preserve the current rendering implementation. Plan Phase 3.6 and section 9.4.
acceptance_criteria: Each backend has a bounded launch result, real capture or explicit hardware blocker, exact API/compiler fingerprint, and metadata-bearing artifact; CPU surrogate images are not labeled live; no dependency migration starts without this baseline.

title: Make scriptbots-render no-default feature lane compile
description: The canonical pinned render coverage lane passes with default world_wgpu, but cargo test -p scriptbots-render --lib --tests --locked --no-default-features fails E0433 because build_gpu_agent_instance unconditionally returns and constructs scriptbots_world_gfx::AgentInstance while that optional dependency is disabled. Gate the GPU-only helper and every remaining type reference with the exact world_wgpu cfg, without changing default-render behavior.
acceptance_criteria: cargo test -p scriptbots-render --lib --tests --locked --no-default-features compiles and preserves the default lane 5 unit + 1 snapshot pass count; cargo check/test with default world_wgpu also remains green; cargo tree with no defaults contains no scriptbots-world-gfx/wgpu edge; cfg placement covers return types, constructors, call sites, tests, and imports; fmt, clippy -D warnings, UBS, and the renderer feature matrix pass.
notes: 2026-07-12 canonical proof at a80bc0 on pinned worker vmi1152480: default cargo-llvm-cov lane passed 6/6; no-default failed E0433 at canonical lib.rs:12758 and :12807 (live dirty tree currently shifted to approximately 12781/12830). Raw log is in the separate de-monolith workspace under phase2_raw/coverage_crates-scriptbots-render-src-lib-rs/nodefault.log. Do not edit the live file until GoldenPanther releases its renderer WIP.
close_reason: Published at f131dbf (source commit 45ec391): GPU helper and references are cfg-gated and unreachable no-feature stubs removed. Default renderer 13 plus 1 snapshot; no-default renderer 11 plus 1 snapshot; NO_GPU_EDGE and strict Clippy green.

title: Make GPU rendering fallible, deterministic, and backend-correct
description: Repair confirmed cross-backend rendering correctness defects before final visual polish: native platform backend selection, typed adapter/device/readback/capture failures, deterministic animation and capture inputs, shader/CPU tonemap parity, explicit linear/sRGB handling, atlas edge safety, and truthful post-processing controls.
design: Characterize current live paths first. Ordinary presentation must never read back. Keep semantic CPU projection artifacts distinct from real framebuffer captures. Fix behavior before extracting the renderer monolith.
acceptance_criteria: On macOS the native product reports Metal, on Windows DX12, and on Linux Vulkan; MoltenVK and other portability backends are explicit diagnostic products. Render and capture APIs reject zero dimensions and return typed errors for adapter, device, resize, device-loss, map, timeout, empty, blank, or metadata-mismatch failures; no empty Vec or missing image is reported as success. GPU readback is one-shot capture-only and never occurs in normal presentation. WGSL and CPU tonemap coefficients agree, the selected tonemap control is actually consumed, unsupported FXAA is not claimed, linear-to-sRGB ownership is explicit and golden-tested, reversed-edge smoothstep and atlas-bleed hazards are removed, and animation/capture inputs derive from tick or recorded sequence rather than wall time. Actual framebuffer evidence includes backend, adapter, driver, scale, viewport, world digest, snapshot revision, color space, tonemap, source revision, and toolchain.
notes: 2026-07-12 committed-code audit: GPUI wgpu presentation blocks on wait_indefinitely readback and rebuilds CPU row quads; render_wgpu_png_offscreen can return empty success; map/poll failures are ignored; shader ACES uses 1.51 where CPU uses 2.43; tonemap uniform is unused; FXAA is a stub; color-space ownership is inconsistent; standalone macOS feature policy enables Vulkan while smoke code asks for Metal.

comments.author: Jeff Emanuel
comments.text: Landing input from commit e2d9aaa (2026-07-12, GoldenPanther), relevant to backend-correctness scope: (1) GPUI now schedules window.request_animation_frame() at the end of render — previously the sim only advanced on input events because pump_simulation runs inside render and nothing else invalidated the window; (2) bloom blur uses separate H/V uniform buffers+bind groups (a single shared buffer made both passes sample the last-written direction -> vertical streaks); (3) offscreen PNG repack derives geometry from the ReadbackView (SB_WGPU_RES_SCALE used to cause slice panics/skewed PNGs); (4) readback source tracks whether the post pass ran this frame (stale post target froze the image when env flags disabled post at runtime); (5) tonemap honors params.tonemap with aligned env parsing; (6) wgpu canvas renders at physical resolution via window.scale_factor() (HiDPI was quarter-res); (7) bevy: health_factor /2.0 (was /100 -> always dim) and Esc only exits when nothing is selected. Remaining architectural items for this bead/epic: single stepping owner (bd-22j) and command-bus routing of GUI mutations (bd-37m) are filed separately with acceptance criteria.

acceptance_criteria: One host drives zero/one/multiple presentation windows with identical WorldDigest; snapshots are bounded; selection/actions return receipts; renderer shutdown/reconnect does not own or duplicate simulation time.

description: Build batched/revision-aware presentation for terrain, water/hydrology, hazards, food density, and scenario annotations using immutable static/dynamic snapshot layers.

title: Run exact-revision GPUI direct-texture feasibility decision

title: Prove shipped GUI visuals, lifecycle, and device failures

title: wasm dependency-graph denylist guard (franken/native deps must never leak into scriptbots-web)
description:
WHY. scriptbots-web builds scriptbots-core with default-features=false (no rayon, no wide) and only brain(mlp) — the whole wasm story depends on that graph staying clean. The franken program adds a family of NATIVE-ONLY deps (survey fact: NO franken numeric/graph/frame library supports wasm32 — fnx-algorithms hard-requires rayon; frankenpandas default features pull bundled-C rusqlite; fsci/ftorch are thread/simd-native; only asupersync and experimental fsqlite-wasm are wasm-capable). One careless feature edge and the wasm build breaks at best silently bloats at worst — and today NOTHING guards this beyond luck and review attention.

SCOPE.
1. ci/check_wasm_graph.sh: cargo tree --target wasm32-unknown-unknown -p scriptbots-web --edges normal,build --prefix none | sort -u, diffed against an explicit DENYLIST (rayon, wide, fsci-*, fnx-*, frankenpandas/fp-*, ft-*, fnp-* [unless the bd-2z0.3.10 adapter is deliberately admitted with a wasm-capable config], rusqlite, tokio) plus an ALLOWLIST-pinned full-graph snapshot so ANY new crate appearing in the wasm graph requires a conscious snapshot update in the same PR (golden-file pattern: drift is visible in review, not silent).
2. Failure output: which denied/new crate, which dependency edge chain introduced it (cargo tree -i for the culprit), file:line hint for the likely feature edge. Verbose by design — this guard's error message is its UX.
3. Wire into PR CI (fast: no compilation, just resolution) + document in AGENTS.md's wasm section.
4. Include the reverse guard while we are here: assert scriptbots-core's default-feature graph does NOT contain any fsci-*/fnx-*/fp-*/ft-* (the analytics/brain crates must be the only doors, per build-budget policy).
TESTS. Self-test with a doctored manifest in a temp workspace copy (inject a denied dep, assert the guard fails with the right chain); snapshot-update procedure documented in the script header.
ACCEPTANCE. Guard green in PR CI; denylist + snapshot committed; a deliberate injection in a scratch branch demonstrably fails with a readable message (paste output in the bead on close).
DEPS. None hard; the analytics scaffold and frankentorch admission beads reference it as their enforcement mechanism. Related bd-2z0.8.13.

title: asupersync single-version-universe CI guard (one 0.3.x across fsqlite/fastmcp/scriptbots)
description:
WHY. Three independent consumers of asupersync are converging in this workspace: (1) fsqlite (pinned, currently resolves asupersync from crates.io), (2) fastmcp_rust (bd-2z0.8.7.1 — its manifest wants 0.3.4 + test-internals feature), (3) our own direct dependency (channel-spine bead; bd-2z0.4.3 pinned =0.3.6 at decision time). bd-2z0.8.7.1's crux paragraph already documents the hazard: caret-compatible 0.3.x versions unify into ONE build — which is exactly what we need, because Cx/channel types crossing crate boundaries (our Cx into fsqlite's AsyncConnection; fastmcp's Cx into our handlers) must be the SAME TYPES from the SAME compiled crate. Two universes = compile errors at best, subtle trait-object incompatibilities at worst. A =0.3.6 EXACT pin on our side would FORCE a split the moment fsqlite floats to 0.3.7 — the guard must catch both failure directions (split universe AND stale exact-pin fights).

SCOPE.
1. ci/check_asupersync_universe.sh: parse Cargo.lock; assert EXACTLY ONE `name = "asupersync"` entry; print all consumers with their declared requirements (cargo tree -i asupersync) on both pass (info) and fail (error).
2. Assert the resolved version satisfies every consumer's declared range; on failure, emit the exact conflicting requirement pairs and the standard fix playbook (documented in the script header: prefer widening our pin to a caret range matching the decision floor, e.g. ">=0.3.6, <0.4", over exact pins; escalate to the bd-2z0.8 lane owner if fsqlite/fastmcp disagree).
3. Extend the same check generically for the ftui crate family once bd-2z0.8.8 lands (all ftui-* crates must resolve to one version set) — parameterize the script, do not fork it.
4. Revisit-note for the channel-spine bead: whether =0.3.6 exact (the .4.3 decision) should become a caret floor is decided THERE with this guard as the safety net; record the outcome in both beads.
TESTS. Self-test against doctored lock fixtures (duplicate-entry fixture must fail; single-entry passes); runs in PR CI (pure lock parsing, milliseconds).
ACCEPTANCE. Guard live in PR CI; fixtures committed; playbook documented; output pasted in bead on close.
DEPS. Related bd-2z0.8.7.1, the channel-spine bead, the async-api bead. No blockers (the guard is useful the moment it exists — the transitive asupersync is already in the lock today).

title: Perf-budget regression harness: TPS and snapshot-latency gates as CI artifacts
description:
WHY. The plan sets explicit budgets (>=60 TPS at 1k agents; snapshot p95 < 4ms at 1k) and bd-h33 tracks a 1372-TPS optimization baseline with named next levers — but nothing GATES regressions today; criterion runs are local and advisory. The franken program is about to touch the exact machinery those budgets protect (channel spine under the tick loop, scoped_cpu spike, BatchBrain in stage_brains, learning steps in cohort context). Every one of those beads cites "the perf-budget harness" as its gate; this bead builds it.

SCOPE.
1. Extend benches/world_bench.rs (SB_BENCH_AGENTS pattern) into a scripted harness: scripts/perf_gate.sh runs a pinned scenario matrix (1k/5k agents x default brain families x N ticks), emits perf_baseline.json (TPS, per-stage timings from existing tracing spans, snapshot p95) with machine fingerprint + commit.
2. Baselines are PER-MACHINE-CLASS artifacts (the bd-h33 numbers come from a specific EPYC worker; CI runners differ): the repo pins a CI-runner baseline; local runs compare informationally against the nearest class. Never compare across classes — the harness must refuse, loudly, rather than mislead.
3. Gate policy: PR lane runs a SHORT deterministic configuration (fixed tick count, seeded) and fails on >10% TPS regression or snapshot p95 budget breach vs the pinned CI baseline; the extended lane runs the full matrix nightly and auto-files a comparison comment. Re-baselining is a reviewed, deliberate commit of the JSON (golden-file pattern), with the justification required in the commit message.
4. Noise discipline: 3 warmup + 5 measured repetitions, median-of-medians, log all raw numbers; if run-to-run CV exceeds 5% on the CI runner the gate goes advisory (warn, not fail) for that run and SAYS SO — a flaky perf gate is worse than none.
5. Documented interplay: bd-h33 owns making numbers BETTER; this harness owns not letting them silently get WORSE. Levers land there; gates live here.
ACCEPTANCE. perf_gate.sh + pinned baseline in CI; one deliberate synthetic regression (sleep injection in a scratch branch) demonstrably caught; CV/advisory behavior demonstrated in logs; docs section in AGENTS.md perf notes.
DEPS. Related bd-h33 (baseline owner), scoped_cpu spike, BatchBrain, hybrid-learning beads (its consumers). No blockers.

comments.author: GoldenPanther
comments.text:
FINDING (GoldenPanther, while executing this bead): the rand *version* work was
already done — the workspace is on rand 0.9, and `rand08` (0.8.5) is a JUSTIFIED,
ISOLATED pin: the `wfc` wave-function-collapse map generator takes rand 0.8's
traits in its public API, and it is the module's ONLY consumer
(crates/scriptbots-core/src/lib.rs, mod map_sandbox). RandomStream already isolates
the science lane, and RunManifestV1 already records `random_stream.algorithm`, so
"manifest identity" was satisfied too.

What was NOT satisfied is the reason this bead exists: *nothing stopped a dependency
or toolchain bump from silently moving the science*. Two real defects, both feeding
the characterization digest (the oracle that decides whether two runs are the same
run):

1. `compute_tileset_hash` hashed `serde_json::to_vec(spec)` with
   `std::hash::DefaultHasher`, and its output is fed into the terrain lane of
   `characterization_digest_v0` (lib.rs, `terrain_encoder.u64(metadata.tileset_hash)`).
   std explicitly does NOT promise DefaultHasher's algorithm across Rust releases
   ("hashes should not be relied upon over releases"). It IS stable within a
   toolchain — which is exactly why this went unnoticed — so the failure mode was a
   *compiler upgrade* silently changing the digest of every run that used a generated
   map. No error, no schema bump: an oracle that quietly stops agreeing with its own
   recorded history. Fixed: replaced with a canonical, length-prefixed, total byte
   walk hashed with the project's own specified `characterization_fnv1a64`. serde_json
   is now out of the hash path entirely, so a *serialization* crate bump cannot move
   the digest either.

2. The same function's `Err(_)` arm fell back to hashing `spec.tiles.len()` — so any
   two tilesets that failed to serialize and had the same tile count shared an
   identity. Two different worlds, one digest. The new walk is total; there is no
   failure path left to degrade into a collision.

Also verified NOT a bug: `generated_at_epoch_ms` (wall clock) is on MapArtifactMetadata
but is NOT encoded into the digest — checked the encoder field by field. It is
provenance metadata only. Left as-is.

Tests added:
- crates/scriptbots-core/src/lib.rs (mod map_sandbox::tests): 5 tests — a PINNED
  golden for the canonical tileset identity (the toolchain guard: any future move
  fails loudly and names itself), same-tile-count non-collision (the precise old
  fallback bug), None vs Some(0.0) non-collision, prefix-freedom across adjacent
  strings ("ab"+"c" vs "a"+"bc"), determinism.
- crates/scriptbots-core/tests/rng_sequence_compat.rs (NEW): 5 tests — a PINNED
  sequence golden for SmallRngStream so that a future `rand` bump that changes the
  generator fails HERE, in a test whose subject is the dependency, with instructions
  to bump the algorithm id and re-baseline, rather than silently moving every digest
  in the project and presenting as "the physics changed". Plus algorithm-identity
  stability, checkpoint/restore sequence identity, seed purity, and an anti-vacuity
  guard that different seeds actually diverge.

This is what makes a future rand bump SAFE TO ATTEMPT: it can now be tried and read
off as sequence-compatible or not, instead of guessed at.

title: Replace mcp-protocol-sdk with pinned fastmcp_rust (asupersync-native MCP layer)
description:
DECISION (owner directive, 2026-07-12): adopt github.com/Dicklesworthstone/fastmcp_rust as the MCP layer, replacing mcp-protocol-sdk 0.5.1.

WHY. (a) fastmcp_rust is asupersync-native, and bd-2z0.4.3's executable spike ALREADY selected asupersync (pinned "=0.3.6") as the runtime for the native driver — adopting fastmcp aligns the control plane with the runtime the project has already chosen instead of maintaining a second, unrelated async MCP stack. (b) It brings cancel-correctness (ctx.checkpoint()), budgets-not-timeouts, 4-valued Outcome, and capability security — all of which map directly onto the command-receipt/back-pressure semantics bd-2z0.4.x is building; mcp-protocol-sdk gives us none of that. (c) Tool definitions collapse to #[tool] async fns, removing the hand-rolled JSON-schema plumbing in servers.rs.

*** THE COMPATIBILITY CRUX — READ BEFORE STARTING ***
fastmcp_rust's manifest declares asupersync = "0.3.4" WITH the "test-internals" feature, and its Cargo.lock pins 0.3.4. ScriptBots' lock resolves asupersync 0.3.6 (pulled by the pinned FrankenSQLite). 0.3.4 and 0.3.6 are caret-compatible, so Cargo WILL unify both on 0.3.6 — which is exactly the single-Cx-universe outcome bd-2z0.4.3 demanded ("avoiding two incompatible runtime/Cx type universes"). BUT:
  1. fastmcp_rust has never been BUILT against 0.3.6 (its lock says 0.3.4). Step one of this bead is a bounded spike: build fastmcp_rust against asupersync 0.3.6 and run its test suite. If it fails, this bead's scope becomes "upstream fastmcp_rust to 0.3.6 first" — do not paper over it in ScriptBots.
  2. fastmcp_rust enables asupersync's "test-internals" feature, which its own manifest comments call a STOPGAP (0.3.4 moved Cx::for_request / Cx::for_testing / set_current behind it). Feature unification means ScriptBots' production graph would silently enable test-internals. That is unacceptable for a project whose whole thesis is honest reproducibility. Qualify it: either upstream fastmcp_rust to stop needing test-internals in non-test builds, or prove the feature is inert in our closure and RECORD that proof. Do not ship a production binary carrying a feature named test-internals without a written justification.
  3. Publication/pinning: fastmcp_rust's workspace is version 0.3.2 while its README advertises crates.io "fastmcp-rust = 0.1" — the naming/version story is unsettled. Follow the FrankenSQLite precedent in AGENTS.md: pin an EXACT git revision (rev = "<sha>") rather than a floating version, and record the rev in the dependency contract.
  4. Transport: ScriptBots' MCP is HTTP-only (mcp-protocol-sdk with default-features=false, features=["http"]; README states stdio/SSE are not used). fastmcp_rust's headline API is run_stdio, but crates/fastmcp-transport/src/http.rs (62KB) and sse.rs exist, and fastmcp-server exposes run_transport/run_transport_returning. VERIFY that the HTTP transport is a first-class, tested path before migrating — and note that run_* methods return `!` (they take over the process), so ScriptBots must use the *_returning variants (run_transport_returning_with_cx) to keep its own lifecycle/shutdown ownership. A `!`-returning server in our control thread would break the level-triggered shutdown we just fixed.

SCOPE.
- Port the four existing tools (list_knobs, get_config, apply_updates, apply_patch) to #[tool] handlers with identical JSON contracts (schemas, error shapes, tool names) — this migration must be OBSERVABLY IDENTICAL to clients on day one; new capabilities come later via bd-2z0.12.2.
- Keep REST/axum on Tokio for now (bd-2z0.4.3 explicitly retains Tokio/Axum as the server adapter). This bead does NOT migrate REST. Two runtimes coexisting in one process is the accepted interim state; document the thread/runtime topology so nobody "helpfully" merges them.
- Map fastmcp's Outcome (4-valued) onto the existing ControlError taxonomy without flattening it — the distinction between "rejected" and "failed" is exactly the back-pressure signal the command bus already models; do not collapse it to Result.
- Wire ctx.checkpoint() into any handler that can block on the world lock, so a cancelled MCP request stops waiting instead of parking a worker (this is the same class of bug as bd-134).

ACCEPTANCE. An MCP client sees byte-identical tool schemas and responses before/after migration (capture golden JSON for all four tools from the current server FIRST, then assert against it); the server shuts down cleanly via the existing ControlRuntime watch-channel path with no `!`-returning call; the dependency graph resolves ONE asupersync (0.3.6) with a recorded justification for any test-internals exposure; the pinned rev is recorded in AGENTS.md/README dependency contracts.

TESTS + LOGGING (required).
- Golden contract test: capture the current server's initialize/tools-list/tools-call responses for all four tools into fixtures BEFORE touching anything; the post-migration server must reproduce them (this is the only way to prove "no client breakage" honestly).
- Unit: Outcome -> ControlError mapping is total and lossless (table-driven over every variant).
- Unit: a cancelled request mid-lock-wait unwinds via checkpoint() and releases its worker (assert no thread leak, no poisoned state).
- E2E: real MCP HTTP client against the real server against the real world (no mocks), exercising all four tools, plus a shutdown-during-in-flight-request case; log every tool invocation with {tool, args_digest, outcome, latency_us} at info so a contract regression is visible in CI output.
- Dependency test: `cargo tree -d` shows no duplicate asupersync; a CI check asserts it stays that way.

comments.author: Jeff Emanuel
comments.text:
NOT STARTED — the prerequisite spike cannot be run in this environment.

The bead's own step one is a BOUNDED SPIKE: build fastmcp_rust against asupersync 0.3.6 and run its test suite, because fastmcp_rust has never been built against 0.3.6 (its lock pins 0.3.4, ours resolves 0.3.6 via the pinned FrankenSQLite). The bead is explicit that if that build fails, the scope becomes 'upstream fastmcp_rust to 0.3.6 first — do not paper over it in ScriptBots.'

I cannot run that spike: the source is NOT present at /dp/fast_mcp_rust in this working environment, and the bead's compatibility crux depends on compiling it. Starting the migration without the spike would mean adopting an MCP layer on the assumption that a never-tested version combination works — precisely the assumption the bead forbids.

WHOEVER PICKS THIS UP, the three traps are already documented in the brief and all three are real:
  1. asupersync 0.3.4 vs 0.3.6 — caret-compatible, so Cargo WILL unify on 0.3.6 (which is the single-Cx-universe outcome bd-2z0.4.3 wanted), but fastmcp_rust has never been built against it. Spike first.
  2. fastmcp_rust enables asupersync's 'test-internals' feature, which its own manifest calls a stopgap. Feature unification would silently enable it in ScriptBots' PRODUCTION graph. A project whose thesis is honest reproducibility must not ship a binary carrying a feature named test-internals without a written justification — either upstream the fix or prove the feature is inert in our closure and record the proof.
  3. run_* methods return  (they take over the process). ScriptBots must use the *_returning variants or the level-triggered shutdown will break.

Also note the transport check: ScriptBots' MCP is HTTP-only, and fastmcp_rust's headline API is run_stdio. Verify the HTTP transport is first-class and tested BEFORE migrating.

title: Adopt fsqlite async-api (AsyncConnection + Cx) for control-plane reads
description:
WHY. fsqlite ships an opt-in `async-api` feature (upstream crates/fsqlite/src/async_api.rs at our pinned line): AsyncConnection, a facade where a dedicated worker task owns the !Send Connection and every method (open/query/query_row/execute/execute_batch/begin/commit/rollback/close) takes asupersync &Cx. That buys: cancellation at VDBE opcode boundaries (surfaces as SQLITE_INTERRUPT), deadline propagation, and capability-narrowed read-only connections. Our control plane (REST/MCP read handlers) currently either reads the ArcSwap snapshot (fine) or risks blocking tokio workers on storage — bd-134 documents that failure class. This bead gives control-plane reads deadlines and cancellation without touching the write path.

SCOPE.
- Enable `async-api` on the fsqlite dependency ONLY for native builds of scriptbots-storage (never wasm; wasm never builds storage anyway).
- Add a READ-ONLY AsyncConnection lane in scriptbots-storage for control-plane queries: top_predators (lib.rs:1764), recent_metrics (:1793), run_ledger_summary (:1877), narrative search (sibling FTS5 bead). Each request gets a Cx with an explicit deadline budget.
- The write path is UNTOUCHED: StoragePipeline's "scriptbots-storage-worker" thread (lib.rs:4424) remains the sole writer and sole owner of the primary Connection; the async lane opens its own read-only connection (MVCC snapshot reads are the whole point of fsqlite).
- THE VERSION-UNIVERSE CRUX (same crux bd-2z0.8.7.1 documents for fastmcp_rust): the Cx type crossing the fsqlite boundary must come from the SAME asupersync build cargo resolves for us (0.3.x caret range unifies — verify in lock; the single-universe CI guard bead enforces it forever).

TESTS (detailed tracing on every path: budget, outcome, cancel/deadline cause).
- Cancellation: start a deliberately slow query (large synthetic table scan), cancel the Cx, assert typed interrupt error, assert the lane accepts subsequent queries (no poisoned state).
- Deadline: sub-ms deadline on a slow query -> deadline outcome, not a hang.
- Concurrency: N concurrent async readers while the writer thread applies heavy outbox batches — all reads succeed on MVCC snapshots, zero writer stalls beyond baseline (measure + log).
- Regression: full existing durability/crash suite (bd-2z0.8.9.7 family) stays green with the feature enabled.
ACCEPTANCE. Control-plane reads carry deadlines + cancellation; write path byte-identical behavior; exactly one asupersync version in Cargo.lock; feature never appears in any wasm target graph.
DEPS. Blocked by the asupersync channel-spine bead (direct asupersync dep + Cx conventions arrive there) and related to bd-2z0.8.9.11 (qualify that the pinned rev's async-api surface is the one described here).

title: Decision: BEGIN CONCURRENT / MVCC multi-writer for archipelago-scale persistence
description:
CONTEXT. FrankenSQLite's headline capability is page-level MVCC: BEGIN CONCURRENT with full SERIALIZABLE via SSI (downgradable via PRAGMA fsqlite.serializable=OFF). Upstream reports concurrent-writer throughput scaling ~41x at 8 threads vs C SQLite's serialized writers — WITH methodology caveats they themselves document (read upstream docs/bench-methodology-concurrent-writers.md before quoting any number; earlier figures were disowned as apples-to-oranges). Single-row writes are ~0.42x C SQLite (our batching already amortizes this).

TODAY single-writer is CORRECT: one HostCore, one storage worker, bounded outbox, three watermarks. Do not disturb it. But bd-16g.5.1 (archipelago: N HostCores) and bd-16g.5.5 (per-island run-DB columns) multiply writers, and this decision should be made from evidence BEFORE archipelago persistence is designed around an assumption.

SCOPE (decision memo, not implementation).
- Benchmark on the REAL ScriptBots batch workload (StoragePipeline flush transactions, INSERT OR REPLACE shape, lib.rs:3434): (a) N separate per-island DB files each with one writer thread, vs (b) one shared DB with N writers using BEGIN CONCURRENT. Measure throughput, SSI conflict/retry rate under realistic batch overlap, recovery-time and file-count operational costs.
- Analyze interaction with the durable-outbox watermarks: does a conflict-retry loop threaten the admitted>=applied>=durable invariants? Document precisely.
- DEFAULT ON NO CLEAR WIN: per-island DBs, one writer each (simplest recovery story, no conflict handling). The burden of proof is on shared-DB MVCC.
- Record accept/reject + rationale in THIS bead and in the AGENTS.md storage contract section; if accepted, spawn implementation beads (schema namespacing, conflict-retry policy, LabRuntime chaos coverage via the persistence-chaos bead).
TESTS. The benchmark harness itself ships with logging (per-run config, throughput, conflict counts) under crates/scriptbots-storage/benches or a bin; results table pasted into this bead on close.
DEPS. Blocked by bd-2z0.8.9.7 (durability suite is the safety net); related bd-16g.5.1, bd-16g.5.5.

title: fsqlite pin recorded inconsistently: Cargo.toml rev != epic/docs rev
description:
FACTS (verified 2026-07-12, incl. git archaeology). Three sources of truth disagree on the "immutable exact revision" of fsqlite 0.1.16:
- root Cargo.toml:48 pins rev 1eec0d2669d0a7938e155b62ce8ebcd72e5bed78;
- the bd-2z0.8.9 epic text, README, and UPGRADE_LOG cite cd9990bb16291d8c7c247b75b47faae8d7701adb as the pinned revision;
- the working-tree Cargo.lock still resolves cd9990bb… (manifest and lock disagree).
GIT HISTORY (the key evidence): commit 0be3dee introduced cd9990bb (bd-2z0.8.9.2 workload gate); commit e04543d ("fix(storage): bind recovery to exact database identity", bd-2z0.8.9.4.2) later DELIBERATELY replaced cd9990bb with 1eec0d2 in the manifest — so the MANIFEST is the newer recorded intent and the epic text/README/UPGRADE_LOG/lock lag behind it. bd-2z0.8.9.11 separately targets ADVANCING the pin to a293a252e75ee720e1981e8898f75cbc39ab03fa.

WHY IT MATTERS. The whole bd-2z0.8 program rests on "exact-revision" reproducibility with a single serialized Cargo.lock mutation lane. A silent manifest/doc/lock three-way drift breaks every parity or durability claim keyed to "the pinned revision", and bd-2z0.8.9.11 cannot qualify an upgrade FROM an ambiguous baseline. Worse: a manifest/lock rev mismatch on a git dependency means builds may fail or silently re-resolve the moment anyone runs cargo update.

SCOPE.
1. Confirm intent with the bd-2z0.8.9.4.2 lineage (why did e04543d move the pin to 1eec0d2? was it required for the identity-binding fix, or incidental churn?). DEFAULT: the newest deliberate change wins — align epic text, README, UPGRADE_LOG, AGENTS.md, and Cargo.lock to 1eec0d2. If investigation shows e04543d's rev bump was accidental, revert the manifest to cd9990bb instead. Either way: ONE rev string everywhere at close.
2. Do NOT advance the pin toward a293a252 here — advancement is bd-2z0.8.9.11's job with its own qualification gates; this bead only makes the record consistent and verified-building (cargo tree -p fsqlite must show the canonical rev after a lock refresh through the bd-2z0.8 lane).
3. Add CI guard ci/check_fsqlite_pin.sh: extract the rev from Cargo.toml, assert the IDENTICAL string appears in Cargo.lock and AGENTS.md; on failure print every discovered rev with file:line.
TESTS. The guard is the test; include a negative self-test (feed it a doctored temp file, assert it fails with the right message). Guard output must list all found revs verbosely for future drift forensics.
ACCEPTANCE. One rev string everywhere; guard green in CI; bd-2z0.8.9.11 can cite this bead as its clean baseline.
DEPS. This bead BLOCKS bd-2z0.8.9.11 (advance only from a consistent record). Coordinate with whoever owns the dirty working-tree Cargo.lock before touching it (single-lane rule).
close_reason: Pin records reconciled to 1eec0d2 everywhere (manifest/lock were already aligned by e04543d; docs+epic lagged); CI guard live; bd-2z0.8.9.11 unblocked

title: LabRuntime deterministic chaos harness for the persistence protocol
description:
WHY. The durable-outbox protocol (admitted >= applied >= durable watermarks, batch ledger, crash-recovery replay — crates/scriptbots-storage/src/lib.rs:2787-3484 + recover_outbox :2952) is exactly the kind of concurrent protocol whose bugs live in schedule interleavings that real-thread tests hit once a year. asupersync ships a purpose-built answer we get for free once the spine lands: LabRuntime — deterministic executor with virtual time, seeded scheduling, DPOR schedule exploration, fault/cancellation injection, and trace record/replay. bd-2z0.8.9.7 proves durability on real threads; this bead EXPLORES THE SCHEDULE SPACE deterministically. They complement, not duplicate.

SCOPE.
- New test crate/module tests/lab_persistence.rs in scriptbots-storage (dev-dependency on asupersync lab features; never a runtime dep of the product).
- Model the admission/apply/durable/recover state machine against LabRuntime: virtual-time timers for flush cadences, injected cancellations at every checkpoint, injected worker faults (simulated write failure, queue-full rejection per bd-2z0.4.10 semantics).
- Assertions: watermark monotonicity (admitted >= applied >= durable ALWAYS), no batch lost or double-applied across simulated crash+recover, fail-closed on queue-full (host retains batch, fault latched), clean-shutdown drains to durable == admitted.
- Seed corpus: fixed seeds checked in; failures print the seed + full trace; a failing seed is reproducible byte-for-byte (that is the whole point — capture it as a regression seed).
- Logging: per-schedule-run structured log (seed, explored interleavings count, injected faults, invariant check results); CI job runs a bounded exploration budget (e.g. N seeds x M schedules) so wall-time stays sane, with the budget documented in the test header.
ACCEPTANCE. Harness in CI; at least the four invariant families above covered; documented procedure in the test header for replaying a captured failure trace; zero flakes across 50 consecutive CI runs (determinism is the feature).
DEPS. Blocked by bd-2z0.4.10 (the adapter semantics under test) and the region-ownership bead (lifecycle boundaries the harness drives); related bd-2z0.8.9.7.

title: Cut the CPU sense lane over to sense_fixed (moves the characterization digest)
description:
SPLIT OUT OF bd-16g.15.1 (2026-07-13), which landed the kernel and left this deliberately open.

STATE TODAY. `scriptbots-core::sense_fixed` exists and is proven: SENSE_FRAC_BITS=20, a documented range derivation (~2^29 headroom), saturating-and-counted accumulation (a wrapping i64 would turn a sensor NEGATIVE — a silently insane input to a brain), and `poly_acos` with max error proven <= 1e-6 over a dense sweep INCLUDING the endpoints where naive polynomials blow up. The acceptance property is proven by a MATCHED PAIR: 64 neighbours x 1000 seeded shuffles gives a bit-identical i64 accumulator, AND the same neighbours summed in f32 provably diverge. The second half is what makes the first half mean anything.

BUT THE CPU LANE STILL ACCUMULATES IN f32. `stage_sense` has not been cut over. So today the kernel is a proven, unused leaf, and the simulator's actual sensing remains order-dependent — which is fine on one CPU lane and fatal the moment bd-16g.15.2 adds a second.

WHY IT WAS SPLIT rather than done in one commit: the cutover MOVES THE CHARACTERIZATION DIGEST. bd-16g.15.1's own brief demands that re-baseline be deliberate and reviewed, with a golden table of the new exact fixed-point values. Burying a digest move inside the commit that introduces a kernel would make the re-baseline unreviewable. There is ONE reference kernel and both lanes must run it — nobody gets to keep the old f32 path as "the reference", because that recreates the very problem (two lanes, different accumulation semantics, one of them order-dependent).

SCOPE.
1. Build each agent's eye unit vectors ONCE per agent (4 transcendentals per agent instead of 4 per agent-neighbour PAIR — also a speedup), then compute per-neighbour terms with `dot` + `poly_acos` instead of `atan2`.
2. Accumulate through `SenseAccum` (integer, order-free) instead of f32.
3. PRESERVE THE `dsq <= f32::EPSILON` EXCLUSION EXACTLY. The current code excludes coincident neighbours with that test; if the new lane excludes differently, the two lanes will disagree about WHO IS EVEN VISIBLE, and every downstream comparison becomes meaningless.
4. Emit the startup line the kernel bead specified: sense_kernel=fixed_point frac_bits=20 max_neighbors_assumed=<N> headroom_bits=<H> geometry=poly_acos poly_max_err=<e> — a reader must be able to reconstruct the run's numeric contract from one line. And `saturations_total` at run end: a run with a non-zero count is SUSPECT, because a sensor that hit the ceiling is a sensor that lied to a brain, and the run's conclusions inherit that.
5. Re-baseline the characterization digest WITH a golden table of the new exact values, so the move is a reviewed artifact rather than a mystery.

TESTS.
- Toroidal seam: a neighbour across the wrap produces the same contribution as the equivalent non-wrapped geometry (the world is a torus, and a sensing lane that forgot that would give agents a free blind spot to exploit).
- Parity against the old f32 path within a documented tolerance on hand-built worlds: single neighbour; neighbour at exactly `radius`; neighbour at dist ~ 0 (the exclusion case above).
- The golden table itself: exact fixed-point values for a fixed fixture, so any future drift is caught as a diff rather than a vibe.
- NEGATIVE: swap the accumulator back to f32 in a fault-injected build -> the order-independence test MUST fail. Prove the alarm fires.

RESIDUAL RISK, stated rather than hidden: `sqrt` is not guaranteed correctly-rounded in WGSL (the spec allows a few ULP), so `poly_acos` is transcendental-FREE but not yet PROVEN bit-exact against a shader. bd-16g.15.2 must verify that with the same inputs on both lanes rather than assuming it.

comments.text:

title: Route GPUI render-layer world mutations through ControlCommand (spawn/set_closed/selection bypass command bus)
description: Route every GPUI scientific mutation through acknowledged HostClient intents: spawn, crossover, closed-world changes, config/mutation edits, and scientific selection. Presentation state stays local.
design: Concrete GPUI command-boundary slice; no direct WorldState locks or mutation remain in the renderer.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Zero direct scientific mutations from render code: no calls to spawn_agent/runtime_mut/set_closed/selection writes remain in crates/scriptbots-render (enforced by a unit test that greps the crate source for the forbidden symbols, with an allowlist for presentation-only state). 2) Every GUI action (spawn herbivore/carnivore, crossover, closed-world toggle, mutation-rate adjust, selection) round-trips as a ControlCommand/HostClient intent and is observable in the command audit trail; deterministic replay of a GUI session applies identical commands. 3) Selection via GUI produces the same SelectionUpdate results as the REST /api/selection path (shared code path test). 4) The double-lock race in toggle_closed_environment (read lock, drop, write lock) is gone — single acquisition or command-applied. TESTS: unit per command mapping (key/button -> expected ControlCommand payload); e2e: scripted GUI session (headless) emitting commands, then a headless replay of the captured command log reproduces the same characterization digest — log every enqueued command with tick, source=gui, payload at debug level so divergences are diagnosable from logs alone.

title: Storage Drop::flush during unwinding can double-panic (abort); guard with thread::panicking()
description:
ROOT CAUSE (anchor at e2d9aaa): impl Drop for Storage (crates/scriptbots-storage/src/lib.rs, ~1680) runs a full transactional flush(). If the storage worker thread is already unwinding from a panic that originated inside fsqlite mid-flush, Drop re-enters the same possibly-inconsistent connection; if that second flush PANICS (not merely errors — the Err path is already handled with eprintln), it is a panic-in-drop-during-unwind, which aborts the whole process and takes the renderer/app down with it. Low probability, catastrophic blast radius.

FIX: at the top of Drop, check std::thread::panicking(); when true, skip the transactional flush entirely and fall back to the existing close_best_effort_in_place() path, emitting one structured eprintln/tracing line: db path, last committed tick if cheaply available, and panicking=true so post-mortems can see the degraded close. Normal (non-panicking) drop behavior must remain byte-for-byte unchanged.

TESTS (required):
- unit: wrap in std::panic::catch_unwind a scope that creates a Storage(:memory:), performs one committed batch, then panics; assert the test completes (no abort) and, after the catch, that a fresh Storage can reopen/read the same file path in the file-backed variant (proving best-effort close did not corrupt).
- unit (regression): the normal drop path still checkpoints — reuse the existing close/reopen conformance assertions.
- Logging: the degraded-close line must include the panicking=true marker; assert its presence by capturing stderr in the test (or route through tracing and use a test subscriber).

title: BrainBinding cloned/deserialized runners are never rehydrated from registry_key (describe() claims a kind with no live runner)
description:
ROOT CAUSE (anchors at e2d9aaa): BrainBinding stores its runner as #[serde(skip)] Option<Box<dyn BrainRunner>> and its Clone impl deliberately sets runner: None while keeping registry_key and kind (crates/scriptbots-core/src/lib.rs, BrainBinding Clone impl). Nothing generic ever rehydrates a cloned/deserialized binding: from_registry is only called by bind_agent_brain and the e2d9aaa inheritance paths. A runtime that round-trips through clone or serde therefore reports kind()/describe() as a real family while tick() returns None, silently degrading the agent to Self::default_outputs sensor-passthrough — analytics count it as (e.g.) mlp.baseline while no network runs. Reproduction was fixed in e2d9aaa; remaining exposure: (a) the AgentRuntimeSnapshot save/restore helper (core ~4444-4464) used by map-artifact application preserves the flag fields but cannot restore runners; (b) any future serde persistence of AgentRuntime (checkpointing is planned work under bd-2z0.3); (c) external embedders cloning runtimes via runtime_mut().

FIX: add WorldState::rehydrate_brains(&mut self) -> usize that sweeps all runtimes and, for every binding with runner.is_none() && registry_key.is_some(), rebuilds via BrainBinding::from_registry (fresh random weights are acceptable for now — the honest alternative to a silent zombie — and the checkpoint-weights story belongs to bd-2z0.3 genome serialization). Call it at the end of apply_map_artifact and expose it pub for embedders/checkpoint restore. Return the number rehydrated.

HONESTY GUARD: in stage_brains, when a job has runner None but the binding claims a kind, emit a rate-limited tracing warn (once per tick with a count, not per agent) so passthrough agents can never again hide silently. Consider exposing a fallback_brains counter on TickSummary so the TUI/REST surface it.

TESTS (required):
- unit: bind an agent from the registry, clone its runtime, insert as a new agent, assert !is_bound; run rehydrate_brains, assert is_bound and kind matches the registry entry, and tick() returns Some.
- unit: binding with kind but no registry_key stays unbound after rehydrate (documented non-goal), and describe() reports it honestly.
- e2e: build a mixed-family world (mlp + dwraon), apply_map_artifact roundtrip, step 10 ticks, assert zero default_outputs fallbacks (via the new counter) and that per-kind population analytics equal the pre-roundtrip counts. Log per-tick fallback counts and per-kind bound/unbound tallies with tracing so failures are diagnosable from output alone.

title: Birth-record stream is incomplete: founders and population-floor injections emit no BirthRecord
description: Agents enter the world through two doors: BORN (stage_spawn_commit, emits a BirthRecord) and INJECTED (bootstrap founders + stage_population floor/scheduled injection via spawn_random_agent). The injected path emits NO BirthRecord, so the birth-record stream is incomplete and any consumer building a phylogeny from records alone never sees those agents — their descendants name a parent that was never born. Found by the offline-ancestry E2E (commit 69ab3fd).
close_reason: Completed in aa83efb with full DSR-only verification, UBS delta acceptance, exact-class performance pass, and synthetic negative canary

comments.author: Jeff Emanuel
comments.text:
MEASURED: on a 600-tick seeded run the database rebuild found 31 agents; the record stream carried only 25. The 16 founders plus 6 floor-injected agents were absent from the birth log. The first version of the E2E failed with UnknownParent { child: AgentUid(20), parent: AgentUid(12) } — a first-generation child of a founder. In production that is not a test failure, it is a phylogeny that silently loses its roots.

WHY OFFLINE REBUILD WORKS ANYWAY (today): the agents table records every agent that ever existed, so an injected agent is exactly an agent with no birth row. StorageReader::load_ancestry_founders() recovers them with that query. But that is an INFERENCE, not a record — it should not have to be.

THE FIX: emit a BirthRecord for every agent that enters the world (parent_a/parent_b = None, generation 0). Then the birth log is complete by construction, a live consumer can build a correct phylogeny from records alone, load_ancestry_founders() becomes unnecessary and can be deleted, and descendants of injected agents stop becoming orphan roots.

CARE REQUIRED: this changes what every run persists (more birth rows), so it will move persistence-derived counts and may move pinned goldens. It deserves its own reviewed re-baseline, which is why it was not rushed into the bead that found it.

SIGNAL WHEN FIXED: crates/scriptbots-storage/tests/ancestry_offline_rebuild.rs currently asserts THE GAP STILL EXISTS, and says so in the failure message. That assertion will fail once this is fixed — delete it and assert digest equality between the live and rebuilt graphs instead.

comments.author: Jeff Emanuel
comments.text:
ATTEMPTED AND STASHED — with the design now known. The naive fix is WRONG, and finding out why is the useful part.

WHAT I TRIED. `insert_agent` is the single door every agent walks through, and it already knows whether the arrival is a birth. Emitting a BirthRecord there when `is_birth == false` (parents None, generation 0) makes the log complete by construction, at exactly one place. It worked: core went green (165 tests), the founders query returned EMPTY (i.e. every agent now has a birth row), and the offline-rebuild E2E's digest-equality assertion — the bead's real acceptance criterion — PASSED for the first time.

WHY IT IS STILL WRONG. It broke `terminal_end_to_end`: 'birth records should match reported total', left 44, right 20. That test guards a real contract I had not noticed, and it is right to.

THE CONFLATION: the `births` table has always meant TWO things at once, and my change forced them apart:
  - an agent's ORIGIN RECORD (what a phylogeny needs: every agent, however it arrived), and
  - a REPRODUCTION EVENT (what the demographic count means: summary.births / last_births).
An injected agent's arrival is NOT a birth. Recording it as one makes the row count (44) diverge from the reported birth total (20), and any downstream demographic statistic built on row counts silently starts counting the population floor's top-ups as reproduction. That would be a new lie in place of the old one.

THE CORRECT DESIGN (do this, do not re-attempt the naive version):
  1. Add an explicit `origin` to BirthRecord: Born | Seeded | Injected. The information is currently only IMPLIED (parents == None and birth_ordinal == 0), and implying it is how the two meanings got conflated in the first place.
  2. Add an `origin` column to the `births` table (schema V5).
  3. summary.births / last_births keep counting ONLY origin == Born, so every demographic statistic is unchanged and the terminal_end_to_end invariant holds — restated as 'birth ROWS WITH origin=Born match the reported total'.
  4. The ancestry graph ingests ALL origins, so the record stream is complete and a live phylogeny works from records alone.
  5. Then delete StorageReader::load_ancestry_founders() (it becomes vacuous), and switch the E2E from asserting the gap to asserting canonical_digest equality — which I have already verified PASSES once the records are complete.

THE WORK IS STASHED, not lost: `git stash list` -> the entry mentioning bd-3m5l. It contains the insert_agent change and the finished E2E rewrite (digest equality + the completeness assertion). Pop it, add the origin field, and the rest follows.

I did not push a schema migration written in a hurry at the end of a long session; that is precisely how the class of defect this bead exists to fix gets introduced.

comments.author: TopazCastle
