title: Checkpoint envelope skeleton (WorldDigestV1 has landed; the envelope has not)
description:
SPLIT OUT OF bd-2z0.3.9 (2026-07-14). That bead asked for two things: WorldDigestV1 AND a
checkpoint envelope skeleton. The digest LANDED (1a4f3e4). The envelope did not, and closing
bd-2z0.3.9 as though it had would be exactly the ceremonial dishonesty this lane exists to remove.

WHAT ALREADY EXISTS, so nobody rebuilds it:
- WorldDigestV1 (scriptbots-core, WorldState::world_digest_v1) — per-lane hashes for agents
  (ordered by the stable AgentUid), brains (genome AND evaluator state, via the new
  BrainRunner::state_digest), food, terrain, hydrology, rng (the RESTORABLE checkpoint with the
  algorithm id), counters (next_agent_uid / next_spawn_ordinal / next_birth_ordinal), and
  brain_registry — plus evaluator_state_covered and uncovered_families, which participate in the
  overall hash so a digest computed while blind to some brains can never collide with one
  computed while seeing them all.
- RandomStreamState: already a restorable checkpoint (algorithm id + codec version + state
  bytes), and from_state REFUSES a state whose algorithm id does not match.
- RunManifestV1: already records root_seed, random_stream, the three allocation counters,
  scenario identity, normalized config + digest, build provenance, brain roster, and
  CharacterizationLimitationsV0.

WHAT THE ENVELOPE STILL OWES:

1. A versioned CHECKPOINT envelope that can actually RESTORE a world: agents (by AgentUid, with
   spawn/birth ordinals and lineage), their brains' genome + evaluator state, food, terrain,
   hydrology, the RNG checkpoint, the counters, and the config. WorldDigestV1 tells you whether
   two worlds ARE the same; the envelope is what lets you RECREATE one.

2. THE HARD PART, and why this is not a serialization chore: restoring a brain means turning a
   persisted genome back into a LIVE RUNNER. BrainRunner::state_digest() is ONE-WAY — it can
   prove a restored brain is identical, but it cannot rebuild one. Rebuilding needs the genome
   protocol (BrainGenomeEnvelope / BrainFamilyAdapter), which bd-2cya found is BUILT BUT
   COMPLETELY UNWIRED: BrainProvenance is never constructed and register_family is never called
   by any product code. This bead is therefore genuinely blocked on that decision, not merely
   adjacent to it.

3. The acceptance test writes itself, and it is the only one that matters:
       RESTORE(SAVE(world)).world_digest_v1() == world.world_digest_v1()
   compared LANE BY LANE, on a world that has actually RUN — agents born, agents dead, brains
   mutated, slots reused — and NOT on a freshly seeded one, where slot reuse and lineage are
   untested and the comparison is vacuous. Assert per-lane equality rather than only `overall`:
   an envelope that restored the bodies but not the brains would otherwise fail with a single
   unhelpful "digests differ".

4. CharacterizationLimitationsV0::checkpoint_replay_guarantee is currently FALSE. When this bead
   lands it flips to true — and it must flip IN THE SAME COMMIT, or the manifest starts lying in
   the optimistic direction.

THE ORDERING TRAP: v0 ordered agents by the RECYCLED slotmap key. v1 orders by AgentUid precisely
so that a restore which re-allocates agents into different slots still digests identically. Any
envelope that persists slot keys, or that relies on insertion order, throws that guarantee away.

title: The manifest's environment capture is clobbered by our own set_var (reports the resolved value, not the user's)
description:
`BuildProvenanceV0::scriptbots_max_threads` claims to record what the ENVIRONMENT said. It does
not. It records what WE overwrote it with.

Startup calls `unsafe { std::env::set_var("SCRIPTBOTS_MAX_THREADS", resolved) }` (main.rs, ~line
198) to communicate the resolved thread count to Rayon's pool builder. `BuildProvenanceV0::current()`
later reads that same variable. So a user who exports SCRIPTBOTS_MAX_THREADS=16 and passes
`--threads 4` gets a manifest whose environment capture says "4" — the value we clobbered in, not
the 16 they actually set.

CONSEQUENCE: that field cannot evidence an override, which is exactly what it would be most
useful for. It is not merely uninformative — it is WRONG about the one fact it purports to
record. This is proven by an e2e test that drives the real binary
(crates/scriptbots-app/tests/run_manifest_emitted.rs, the_manifest_records_the_thread_policy_...),
which currently ASSERTS the clobbered value and tells the reader why.

MITIGATED, NOT FIXED: bd-2z0.1.10 added `RunManifestV1::thread_policy` (88a7d04), which records
the resolved count, the deciding layer, and the declined layer. That is now the authoritative
record and it is correct. But the environment capture sitting beside it still misreports, and a
reader comparing the two would reasonably trust the wrong one.

THE FIX, in ascending order of goodness:
  a) Capture the original environment BEFORE startup mutates it, and hand that snapshot to
     BuildProvenanceV0 instead of letting it read a variable we have already written.
  b) STOP USING THE ENVIRONMENT AS AN IPC CHANNEL. The thread count is passed to Rayon by mutating
     a process-global env var with `unsafe set_var` — which is unsafe in Rust 2024 precisely
     because it races with other threads reading the environment. Pass the value to the Rayon pool
     builder directly. If bd-2z0.4.5 (HostCore) lands a sole-owner config path, the thread policy
     should travel through it as a VALUE. The clobber is a symptom; the env-as-channel is the
     disease.

When fixed, the e2e assertion expecting "4" flips to "16" and the comment above it is deleted.

comments.author: GoldenPanther
comments.text: Released unstarted: both files this touches (crates/scriptbots-app/src/main.rs and src/lib.rs) are EXCLUSIVELY reserved by TopazCastle until ~2026-07-15T01:40. They hold both, so they are very likely already working precedence/manifest/startup — this fix belongs to whoever owns that surface right now, not to a second agent reaching into it. Mailing TopazCastle the finding so they can fold it in. The fix itself is small (see bead body): capture the environment BEFORE startup's set_var mutates it and hand that snapshot to BuildProvenanceV0::current, OR better, stop passing the thread count through the environment at all and hand it to the Rayon pool builder as a value.

title: bv reads a stale merge artifact — its work recommendations point at CLOSED beads
description:
`bv` IS READING A STALE MERGE ARTIFACT, SO EVERY AGENT'S WORK SELECTION IS WRONG.

AGENTS.md tells us to use `bv` with the robot flags to pick the next bead. That advice is
currently ACTIVELY HARMFUL: bv's recommendations point at work that is already finished.

PROOF (not inference):
- `bv --robot-triage` reports total=103, closed=3, open=100.
- `br` reports 251 records (185 open/in-progress + 66 closed). `br doctor` confirms the DB
  and .beads/issues.jsonl agree at 251 and the SQLite integrity check passes.
- `.beads/beads.jsonl` contains EXACTLY 103 records with EXACTLY 3 closed — bv's numbers to
  the record. It was last written 2026-07-12 08:53 and has not moved since.
- Spot check: bd-2z0.1.4 is `open` in beads.jsonl and `closed` in issues.jsonl (and closed
  in the DB). bv lists it as a QUICK WIN.

So bv reads `.beads/beads.jsonl` while `br` maintains `.beads/issues.jsonl`. Nearly a full
day of work is invisible to bv: 66 closed beads still look open to it, and ~148 newer beads
do not exist for it at all.

CONSEQUENCE, and this is the part that matters: bv's top picks right now are bd-2z0.1.6
("Define RunManifestV0 and characterization digest"), bd-2z0.1.4, bd-2z0.3.2, bd-2z0.1.7,
bd-2z0.3.6 — and several of those are CLOSED. An agent that obeys `bv --robot-next` is sent
to redo finished work. RunManifest in particular is not merely defined but EMITTED by the
binary (bd-28yt), with an e2e test that runs the real process and reads the file off disk.
This also explains the earlier oddity that bv's `quick_wins` "did not filter blockers": it
was not just mis-filtering, it was reasoning over a stale dependency graph.

`br doctor` already detects the cause and says so:
    WARN jsonl.merge_artifacts: Merge artifacts detected in .beads/
`.beads/beads.jsonl` (146 KB, stale) and `.beads/beads.base.jsonl` (927 KB) are leftovers
from a JSONL merge. `beads.jsonl` is TRACKED IN GIT, so I did NOT delete it — AGENTS.md
Rule 1 forbids deleting files without explicit written permission, and I am not going to
quietly remove a tracked file that three other agents' tooling reads.

`bv --db .beads/beads.db` does NOT help: it still reports 103/3, i.e. bv appears to prefer
the JSONL in the directory over the database it was pointed at.

WHAT TO DO UNTIL SOMEONE WITH PERMISSION CLEANS THIS UP:
DO NOT trust `bv --robot-next` / `--robot-triage` for work selection. Compute the frontier
from `br`, which is the source of truth, and check blockers explicitly — bv's own
quick_wins do not filter them even on fresh data:

  for i in $(br list --status open --json | jq -r '.[]|select((.issue_type//.type)!="epic")
             |select((.assignee//"")=="")|.id'); do
    B=$(br show $i --json | jq -r '[.[0].dependencies[]?
        |select(.dependency_type=="blocks" and .status!="closed")|.id]|join(",")')
    [ -z "$B" ] && br show $i --json | jq -r '.[0]|"P\(.priority) \(.id) \(.title)"'
  done | sort

THE FIX (needs a human, because it deletes/rewrites tracked files): remove the merge
artifacts `.beads/beads.jsonl` and `.beads/beads.base.jsonl` (or regenerate beads.jsonl
from the live DB) so that bv and br see the same graph. Then re-run `br doctor` until it is
clean, and confirm `bv --robot-triage` reports 251 records.
close_reason: Superseded by closed bd-2z0.1.9 (7fb9be1d, 508aa0f4): authoritative wrapper isolates issues.jsonl, cross-checks BR/BV counts, edges, exact ready IDs and hash, and fails closed. Live audit: 261 issues, 82 closed/24 in progress/155 open, 339 edges, 62 ready, BV hash 81af80126408f96b. Stale merge artifacts remain quarantined and need not be deleted.

title: Perf: continue optimization rounds from 1372 tps baseline (worker EPYC, seed 42, --profile-steps 1000, commit e2d9aaa) — next levers: CSR index rebuild, persistence row materialization off sim thread, GPUI RenderFrame Arc sharing, carcass via index
description:
BASELINE (do not lose): 1372 ticks/sec = 1000 headless ticks in 0.729s via `SCRIPTBOTS_RNG_SEED=42 SCRIPTBOTS_MAX_THREADS=8 cargo run --release -p scriptbots-app --bin scriptbots-app --no-default-features -- --profile-steps 1000` at commit e2d9aaa on an 8-core AMD EPYC Linux worker (kernel 6.17), linker override CARGO_TARGET_X86_64_UNKNOWN_LINUX_GNU_LINKER=cc, RUSTFLAGS empty. CAVEAT: --no-default-features disables ml/neuro brains AND the mimalloc fast-alloc feature; re-measure with default features before comparing against README numbers.

CONTEXT: commit e2d9aaa already landed round 1 (digest-verified behavior-neutral): activation snapshots gated to inspected agents, parallel stage_brains via extracted runners, combat 3-field CombatAgentView instead of AgentRuntime clones, reproduction partner-only cloning, food sharing via spatial index (+1-cell staleness margin), single profile fetch per regrowth SIMD lane. The remaining ranked levers below come from three independent audit passes; evidence anchors are at e2d9aaa.

RANKED LEVERS (one lever per commit, A/B each):
1. CSR spatial index rebuild — scriptbots-index/src/lib.rs rebuild() allocates a fresh Vec<usize> counts plus a brand-new Vec<Vec<usize>> (7200 inner vecs at default 120x60 grid) or HashMap on EVERY rebuild, and rebuild runs 2x/tick (stage_sense + stage_combat). Replace with persistent offsets/entries CSR arrays filled in two passes; bucket slices become contiguous (better query locality). Expected: eliminates ~14k allocs/tick.
2. Persistence batch materialization off the sim thread — StorageSink::submit runs full row building inside world.step(): String per agent from brain_binding.describe().into_owned(), serde_json::to_string per replay event (up to 1024), per-metric Strings. Keep only non-finite validation at admission; move row/JSON building into the worker thread.
3. Skip per-statement savepoints — flush_attempt wraps each of the 7 tables' inserts in Connection::execute_with_params which re-parses SQL and opens an internal statement savepoint per row. fsqlite ships execute_with_params_skip_statement_savepoint for prevalidated batches whose enclosing transaction is the rollback boundary — exactly this case. Biggest write-path win.
4. GPUI RenderFrame Arc sharing — scriptbots-render clones the full RenderFrame (all agents + 7200 TerrainTileVisual + full food grid) ~4x per frame per window incl. a 240-slot playback ring. Wrap in Arc, record playback at reduced cadence.
5. Carcass distribution + select_partner_index via the spatial index (both O(N) scans per corpse/parent today; radii are smaller than sense radius, index already built that tick).
6. PendingAnalytics::from_batch builds BTreeMap + Vec<MetricReading> per batch but the worker overwrites pending_analytics on each buffered persist — ~31/32 constructed and discarded. Build readings lazily at publish time.

METHOD (required): (a) measure baseline and post-lever with >=5 runs of --profile-steps 1000 seed 42 on the same host, report mean+min+max; (b) prove behavior-neutrality per lever with the characterization trace (scriptbots-app characterization_tests digests must be bit-identical) plus cargo test --workspace for headless crates; (c) one lever per commit so regressions bisect.

LOGGING (required): add an opt-in per-stage timing instrument behind SCRIPTBOTS_PROFILE_STAGES=1 (tracing spans or a simple [stage -> cumulative_us, count, p50, p95] table printed at exit) so future profiling doesn't need external tooling. Keep it measurement-only and off by default.

TESTS (required): existing determinism suites stay green; add a criterion bench per optimized subsystem in crates/scriptbots-core/benches/world_bench.rs (index rebuild, sharing stage) so CI can flag regressions; for lever 3 add a storage test proving a mid-batch statement failure still rolls back the whole transaction (the savepoint skip must not weaken atomicity).

title: Workspace dependency resolution is BROKEN: ft-api/frankentorch checkout is corrupt in the shared cargo-home
description:
SYMPTOM: cargo cannot RESOLVE the workspace. Not build — resolve. Every cargo command in
the repo now fails before compiling anything:

  error: failed to get `ft-api` as a dependency of package `scriptbots-brain-ml v0.1.0`
  Caused by: failed to load source for dependency `ft-api`
  Caused by: unable to update https://github.com/Dicklesworthstone/frankentorch?rev=e4c6bdd5ec629ae70b40da9314da345ade012ca7
  Caused by: could not open '/Volumes/USBNVME16TB/temp_agent_space/cargo-home/git/checkouts/
    frankentorch-e23a3b2338306521/e4c6bdd/artifacts/perf/frankentorch-5oqum/
    pass10_current_head_eigvalsh_components_remote.log' for writing:
    No such file or directory; class=Os (2)

WHO IT AFFECTS: everyone. This is not feature-gated away. `ft-api` is a dependency of
scriptbots-brain-ml, and cargo must fetch a dependency's SOURCE to read its manifest even
when the feature that uses it is off — so resolution fails for the whole workspace
regardless of which crate or feature you are building.

CAUSE (best reading): someone added an ft-api / frankentorch dependency to
crates/scriptbots-brain-ml, and the git checkout of that repo inside the SHARED cargo-home
(/Volumes/USBNVME16TB/temp_agent_space/cargo-home) is corrupt or incomplete — cargo is
trying to write a file into an artifacts/perf/ directory that does not exist in the
checkout. Note the file it wants is a PERF LOG committed into the dependency repo, which is
an odd thing for a library checkout to need to write.

I did NOT touch it. Repairing this means deleting/refetching a checkout inside a cargo-home
that three other agents are actively building against, and AGENTS.md Rule 1 forbids deleting
files without explicit written permission. This needs whoever added the dependency, or a
human.

LIKELY FIXES (for whoever owns the frankentorch integration):
  - Re-fetch the checkout (remove the corrupt frankentorch-e23a3b2338306521 checkout dir and
    let cargo re-clone), or
  - pin ft-api to a rev whose tree does not carry the artifacts/perf/ payload, or
  - vendor it, or drop the dependency if the `ml`/`tch` path is not yet real (see
    bd-2z0.3.7: the ML brain today is `ml.placeholder`, a no-op).

CONTEXT: this is the THIRD independent thing blocking builds in this checkout right now.
See bd-2tse (RCH refuses to offload this path; local fallback cannot link — no mold, linux
target on a mac) and the disk: the Data volume is 100% full (413Gi used, ~200Mi free), so
native fallback builds die on ENOSPC. Until at least one of these is cleared, NOTHING in this
repository can be compiled or tested.
close_reason: RESOLVED (not by me — verified fixed). 'cargo metadata --format-version 1' now resolves the full workspace cleanly, and cargo check/test both build again. Someone re-fetched or repaired the corrupt frankentorch/ft-api checkout in the shared cargo-home. Closing rather than leaving a stale P0 on everyone's frontier. NOTE for whoever owns the frankentorch integration: the failure mode is worth remembering — a corrupt git checkout of a path dependency breaks cargo RESOLUTION for the entire workspace regardless of feature flags (cargo must fetch a dependency's source to read its manifest, even when the feature that uses it is off), so it is not contained to the ml lane. Also note the disk is now healthy again: 102Gi free, was 100% full.
